   217	/-- **One-measurement Naimark lemma** (Lemma 5.2).
   218	
   219	For any submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, there exists a projective
   220	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` such that for every
   221	operator `ρ` on `Op d` and outcome `a`:
   222	`τ(ρ · M_a) = τ'(ρ_lifted · P̂_a)`
   223	where `ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)` and `P̂_a` is the
   224	dilated projector.
   225	
   226	**Proof sketch**: Let `V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a|ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   227	This is an isometry (by the submeasurement property `∑ M_a ≤ I`).
   228	Define `P̂_a = V†(I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|)V`. Then `P̂_a` is an orthogonal projection
   229	(since `|a⟩⟨a|` is), and the compression identity
   230	`(I⊗⟨⊥|) P̂_a (I⊗|⊥⟩) = √M_a · √M_a = M_a` gives the result.
   231	
   232	The proof uses `CFC.sqrt` for PSD operators together with lemmas such as
   233	`CFC.sqrt_mul_sqrt_self`. -/
   234	theorem oneMeasNaimark {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   235	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   236	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d) :
   237	    OneMeasNaimarkLemma α d M := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let auxProj : Option α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   240	    fun oa => Matrix.single oa oa 1
   241	  /-
   242	  The prescribed Naimark isometry column:
   243	    `V (|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩)
   244	      = ∑_a √(M_a)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I - ∑_a M_a)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`,
   245	  encoded by `oneMeasNaimarkColumn M`.  Concretely, this matrix is
   246	  supported only on the input `none = ⊥` slice.
   247	  -/
   248	  let V : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) := oneMeasNaimarkColumn M
   249	  /-
   250	  Extend the isometry column `V` to a unitary `U` on the whole enlarged space.
   251	  The dilated projectors are then `U† (I ⊗ |oa⟩⟨oa|) U`.
   252	  -/
   253	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
   254	    partialIsometry_to_unitary
   255	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn M) (oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d))
   256	      oneMeasNaimarkInputProj_isProj
   257	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn_mul_inputProj M)
   258	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn_isometry M)
   259	  let Umat : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) := U
   260	  refine ⟨{
   261	    source := M
   262	    liftedEffect := fun oa =>
   263	      Umatᴴ * Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa) * Umat
   264	    lifted_isProj := ?_
   265	    lifted_sum_le_one := ?_
   266	    expectation_preservation := ?_
   267	  }, rfl⟩
   268	  · intro oa
   269	    /-
   270	    `U† (I ⊗ |oa⟩⟨oa|) U` is a projection because `I ⊗ |oa⟩⟨oa|` is, and
   271	    conjugation by a unitary preserves Hermitian idempotents.
   272	    -/
   273	    let P : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) :=
   274	      Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa)
   275	    have hPproj : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj P := by
   276	      exact isProj_kronecker
   277	        ((IsStarProjection.one _))
   278	        (optionBasisProj_isProj oa)
   279	    simpa [Umat, P] using isProj_unitary_conj U hPproj
   280	  · /-
   281	    Since the auxiliary rank-one projectors sum to the identity on `Option α`,
   282	    the lifted family is actually a complete projective measurement, hence in
   283	    particular a submeasurement.
   284	    -/
   285	    have hauxDecomp : ∑ oa : Option α, auxProj oa = auxProj none + ∑ a : α, auxProj (some a) := by
   286	      exact Fintype.sum_option (f := auxProj)
   287	    have hsplit :
   288	        ∑ oa : Option α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa) =
   289	          Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj none) +
   290	            ∑ a : α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj (some a)) := by
   291	      exact Fintype.sum_option
   292	          (f := fun oa : Option α =>
   293	            Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa))
   294	    have hsumSome :
   295	        ∑ a : α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj (some a)) =
   296	          Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (∑ a : α, auxProj (some a)) := by
   297	      ext x y
   298	      rcases x with ⟨i, oi⟩
   299	      rcases y with ⟨j, oj⟩
   300	      by_cases hij : i = j
   301	      · subst hij
   302	        rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
   303	        simp [Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.sum_apply]
   304	      · rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
   305	        simp [Matrix.kronecker, hij]
   306	    have hauxSplit : auxProj none + ∑ a : α, auxProj (some a) = 1 := by
   307	      rw [← hauxDecomp, optionBasisProj_sum_eq_one]
   308	    have hbase :
   309	        ∑ oa : Option α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa) = 1 := by
   310	      calc
   311	        ∑ oa : Option α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa)
   312	            = Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj none) +
   313	                ∑ a : α, Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj (some a)) := by
   314	                  exact hsplit
   315	        _ = Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)
   316	              (auxProj none + ∑ a : α, auxProj (some a)) := by
   317	                rw [hsumSome]
   318	                simpa using
   319	                  (Matrix.kronecker_add
   320	                    (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)
   321	                    (auxProj none)
   322	                    (∑ a : α, auxProj (some a))).symm
   323	        _ = Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)
   324	              (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) := by
   325	              rw [hauxSplit]
   326	        _ = (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α)) := by
   327	              exact Matrix.one_kronecker_one
   328	    exact le_of_eq <| unitary_conj_sum_eq_one U _ hbase
   329	  · intro ρ a
   330	    /-
   331	    **Compression/trace identity** (core of Lemma 5.2).
   332	
   333	    From `hU : U * P_⊥ = V`, the `⊥`-column of `U` equals the Naimark column `V`.
   334	    The trace identity `τ(ρ M_a) = τ'(ρ_lifted · P̂_a)` follows from:
   335	    1. `(ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)` restricts the trace to the `⊥`-slice of the auxiliary
   336	    2. On this slice, `U†(I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|)U` acts as `√M_a * √M_a = M_a`
   337	       (by the column identity from `hU` and `CFC.sqrt_mul_sqrt_self`)
   338	    3. The `|Option α|` scaling cancels with the enlarged-space normalization
   339	
   340	    The detailed calculation is entry-level:
   341	      `Tr((ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|) · U†Q_aU)`

   183	/-- The auxiliary pure-state projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` on `Option α`, where `⊥ = none`.
   184	This is the initial state of the auxiliary register before the Naimark
   185	isometry is applied. -/
   186	def naimarkAuxProjector (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   187	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   188	  Matrix.single none none 1
   189	
   190	/-- The lifted density matrix for one-measurement Naimark dilation:
   191	`ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)`.
   192	The scaling by `|Option α|` ensures the normalized trace is preserved:
   193	`τ'(ρ_lifted) = τ(ρ)`, where `τ'` is the normalized trace on the enlarged space. -/
   194	noncomputable def oneMeasLiftedDensity {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   195	    (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   196	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) :
   197	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) :=
   198	  (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) • Matrix.kronecker ρ (naimarkAuxProjector α)

   200	/-- One-measurement Naimark dilation data at the matrix level.
   201	
   202	Given a submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, this witnesses the existence
   203	of a projective submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` that
   204	preserves all expectation values. This is Lemma 5.2 of the paper.
   205	
   206	The construction: let `V : H → H ⊗ ℂ^{|α|+1}` be the isometry
   207	`V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a |ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   208	Then `P̂_a = V† (I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|) V` is a projection, and
   209	`⟨ψ|M_a|ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ⊗⊥|P̂_a|ψ⊗⊥⟩`. -/
   210	structure OneMeasNaimarkData (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   211	    (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
   212	  /-- The source submeasurement being dilated. -/
   213	  source : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d
   214	  /-- The dilated projective effects on `d × Option α`.
   215	  For outcome `some a`, this is the Naimark projector `P̂_a`.
   216	  For outcome `none`, this is the projector for the "missing mass". -/
   217	  liftedEffect : Option α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α)
   218	  /-- Each lifted effect is a genuine orthogonal projection. Positivity follows
   219	  from `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/
   220	  lifted_isProj : ∀ a, MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj (liftedEffect a)
   221	  /-- The lifted projections sum to at most identity (which together with
   222	  `lifted_isProj` implies mutual orthogonality). -/
   223	  lifted_sum_le_one : ∑ a, liftedEffect a ≤ 1
   224	  /-- **Expectation preservation**: for any operator `ρ` on `Op d`,
   225	  the expectation of outcome `a` under the original submeasurement equals
   226	  the expectation under the dilated projective submeasurement with the
   227	  Naimark-lifted state. The identity is linear, so it holds for all operators,
   228	  not just density matrices. This is the core content of the dilation. -/
   229	  expectation_preservation : ∀ (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (a : α),
   230	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * source.effect a) =
   231	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   232	        (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ * liftedEffect (some a))
   233	
   234	/-- Positivity of a lifted Naimark effect, derived from its projectivity.
   235	
   236	Lean-only consequence of the one-measurement Naimark data: the paper records
   237	the lifted effects as projections, and positivity is supplied here by the
   238	Mathlib star-projection order theorem through `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/
   239	theorem OneMeasNaimarkData.lifted_pos {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   240	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   241	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (a : Option α) :
   242	    0 ≤ data.liftedEffect a :=
   243	  (data.lifted_isProj a).nonneg

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)

   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

   512	\subsection{The Magic Square game}
   513	\label{sec:ms}
   514	
   515	We recall the \emph{Magic Square game} of Mermin and
   516	Peres~\cite{mermin1990simple,peres1990incompatible,aravind2002simple}.
   517	The Magic Square game is a simple self-test for EPR pairs (it tests for two of
   518	them). In addition, it allows one to test that a pair of observables
   519	\emph{anticommutes}.
   520	Here we use it as a building block to construct the quantum low-degree test. 
   521	
   522	There are several formulations of the Magic Square game; here we present it as a
   523	\emph{binary constraint satisfaction} game~\cite{cleve2014characterization}.
   524	In this formulation of the game (denoted by $\game_\MS$) there are $6$ linear
   525	equations defined over $9$ variables that take values in $\F_2$.
   526	The variables correspond to the cells of a $3 \times 3$ grid, as depicted in
   527	Figure~\ref{fig:ms}.
   528	Five of the equations correspond to the constraint that the sum of the variables
   529	in each row and the first two columns must be equal to $0$, and the last
   530	equation requires that the sum of the variables in the last column must be equal
   531	to $1$.
   532

   534		\begin{center}

   539				\hline 
   540				$x_4$ & $x_5$ & $x_6$ \\	
   541				\hline

   550	The question set $\type^\ms$ of the Magic Square game is the following:
   551	\begin{equation*}
   552	  \begin{split}
   553	    \type^\msc & = \{ \Constraint_i : i = 1, 2, \ldots, 6\}\;,\\
   554	    \type^\msv & = \{ \Variable_j : j = 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}\;,\\
   555	    \type^\ms & = \type^\msc \cup \type^\msv\;.
   556	  \end{split}
   557	\end{equation*}
   558	The questions $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ correspond to the three row
   559	constraints, the questions $\Constraint_4$, $\Constraint_5$ correspond to the first
   560	two column constraints, and question $\Constraint_6$ corresponds to the third
   561	column constraint.
   562	
   563	In the Magic Square game, the verifier first samples a constraint $\Constraint_i
   564	\in \type^\msc$ uniformly at random, and then samples $\Variable_j$, one of the
   565	three variables in the row or column corresponding to $\Constraint_i$, uniformly
   566	at random.
   567	One player is randomly assigned to be the $\Constraint$ player, and the other is
   568	assigned to be the $\Variable$ player.
   569	The $\Constraint$ player is sent the question $\Constraint_i$ and is expected to
   570	respond with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$,
   571	where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables corresponding to
   572	$\Constraint_i$.
   573	The $\Variable$ player is given question $\Variable_j$ and is expected to
   574	respond with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$.
   575	The players win if the $\Constraint$ player's answers satisfy the equation
   576	associated with $\Constraint_i$, and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   577	More precisely, the verifier samples an edge of the type graph (see Section~\ref{sec:types}) $G^\ms$
   578	in Fig.~\ref{fig:type-graph-ms}, sends one endpoint to a random player, and the
   579	other endpoint to the other player.

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}
   653	
   654	We will need the following theorem,
   655	which shows that any pair of anticommuting observables 
   656	can be used to form a value-$1$ strategy for the Magic Square game.
   657	
   658	\begin{theorem}
   659	  \label{thm:ms-from-ac}
   660	  Let $A = \{A_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ and $B = \{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ be two-outcome

    32	In this section, we will survey two tools for doing so.
    33	The first of these is the textbook Naimark dilation theorem.
    34	In our setting, it states the following.
    35	
    36	\begin{theorem}[Naimark dilation]\label{thm:naimark}
    37	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    38	Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}}$
    39	and $B=\{B^y_b\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    40	Then there exists
    41	\begin{enumerate}
    42	\item Hilbert spaces $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$ and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    43	\item a state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    44	\item and two measurements  $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}^x_a\}$ and $\widehat{B}=\{\widehat{B}^y_b\}$
    45	acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    46	and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    47	respectively,
    48	\end{enumerate}
    49	such that the following is true.
    50	If we write $\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}$,
    51	then for all $x,y, a, b$,
    52	 \begin{equation*}
    53	 \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}
    54	 = \bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat{A}^x_a \ot \widehat{B}^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}.
    55	 \end{equation*}
    56	 In addition, $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$ is a \emph{product state},
    57	 meaning that we can write it as
    58	 \begin{equation*}
    59	 \ket{\mathsf{aux}}= \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}},
    60	 \end{equation*}
    61	for $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    62	and $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$.
    63	\end{theorem}
    64	The second of these is the ``orthogonalization lemma" from~\cite{KV11}.
    65	In the setting of symmetric strategies, it states the following.
    66	
    67	\begin{theorem}[Orthogonalization lemma]\label{thm:orthonormalization}
    68	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state,
    69	and let $A = \{A_a\}$ be a sub-measurement with strong self-consistency
    70	\begin{equation*}
    71	\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_a \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\zeta.
    72	\end{equation*}
    73	Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $P = \{P_a\}$ such that
    74	\begin{equation*}
    75	A_a \otimes I \approx_{100 \zeta^{1/4}} P_a \otimes I.
    76	\end{equation*}
    77	\end{theorem}
    78	
    79	These two results serve largely the same purpose,
    80	and for our applications it will typically suffice to use either one.
    81	That said, there are tradeoffs when choosing to use one or the other.
    82	Naimark dilation is convenient because it can be applied to any family of sub-measurements
    83	and it preserves measurement outcome probabilities exactly.
    84	On the other hand, it requires swapping out the state $\ket{\psi}$ and measurements~$A$ and~$B$
    85	for $\ket{\widehat{\psi}}$ and $\widehat{A}$ and $\widehat{B}$, respectively,
    86	which can be notationally cumbersome.
    87	Most works opt to skip adding the hats,
    88	and instead say something to the effect of ``using Naimark, we can assume that~$A$ and~$B$ are projective."
    89	However, there is subtlety in doing so,
    90	which is that Naimark dilation does not necessarily preserve ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements;
    91	in other words, $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$
    92	does not necessarily imply $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$.
    93	(As an example, \Cref{ex:easy-but-long} below
    94	provides a case in which $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{0} I \ot B^x_a$,
    95	but $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$ only holds for $\delta \geq 1$.)
    96	This can lead to trouble if the same notation is used for~$A, B$ and $\widehat{A}, \widehat{B}$,
    97	as ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements derived before applying Naimark might not necessarily hold after applying Naimark.
    98	(That said, as pointed out at the end of Section~$4.4$ of~\cite{NW19},
    99	``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements are often derived as a consequence of ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements.
   100	And as Naimark preserves ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements,
   101	one could use them to simply rederive any ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements post-Naimark.)
   102	
   103	The downsides of using the orthogonalization lemma
   104	are that it can only be applied to measurements which are strongly self-consistent
   105	and it introduces additional error.
   106	As we will see below, its proof is significantly more complicated than Naimark dilation.
   107	On the plus side, it has none of the notational baggage that Naimark brings,
   108	and so it is more concrete to use.
   109	In addition, it can lead to stronger results,
   110	as it does not require introducing an auxiliary state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$.
   111	
   112	In this work, we will opt to use the orthogonalization lemma rather than Naimark dilation.
   113	However, we will include proofs of both for completeness.
   114	We will prove \Cref{thm:naimark} in \Cref{sec:naimark}
   115	and then \Cref{thm:orthonormalization} in \Cref{sec:orthogonalization}.

   119	To prove \Cref{thm:naimark}, we will first need the following lemma.
   120	
   121	\begin{lemma}
   122	  \label{lem:naimark-helper}
   123	  Let $A = \{A_{a}\}$ be a sub-measurement with $k$ distinct outcomes $a \in \calA$, and let $\ket{\mathsf{aux}} \in \C^{k+1}$ be any state. Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}_{a}\}$ such that
   124	  for each outcome~$a$,
   125	  \[ (I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot \widehat{A}_{a} \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) =
   126	    A_{a}. \]
   127	\end{lemma}
   128	\begin{proof}
   129	We will consider an orthonormal basis for $\C^{k+1}$
   130	consisting of a vector $\ket{a}$ for each $a \in \calA$ and the vector $\ket{\bot}$.
   131	Let~$U$ be any unitary such that for each vector $\ket{\psi} \in \C^d$,
   132	\begin{align*}
   133	U \cdot (\ket{\psi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   134	&= \sum_{a \in \calA} ((A_{a})^{1/2} \ket{\psi}) \ot \ket{a} + ((1 - A)^{1/2}\ket{\psi}) \ot \ket{\bot}\\
   135	&= \Big(\sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}\Big)
   136			\cdot \ket{\psi}.
   137	\end{align*}
   138	This implies that
   139	\begin{equation*}
   140	U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   141	= \sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}.
   142	\end{equation*}
   143	Hence, for any $a \in \calA$,
   144	\begin{equation*}
   145	(I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   146	= (I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot \Big(\sum_{a \in \calA} (A_{a})^{1/2} \ot \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot}\Big)
   147	= (A_a)^{1/2}.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	  Then the desired projective sub-measurement is
   150	  \[ \widehat{A}_a = U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U. \]
   151	  This is because
   152	\begin{align*}
   153	 (I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot \widehat{A}_{a} \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   154	&=(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot (U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U) \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\
   155	&=(I \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \ot \ket{a}) \cdot (I\ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\
   156	&= (A_a)^{1/2} \cdot (A_a)^{1/2} = A_a.
   157	\end{align*}
   158	This completes the proof.
   159	\end{proof}
   160	
   161	Now we prove \Cref{thm:naimark}.
   162	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:naimark}]
   163	For each $x$, let $k$ be the number of outcomes in $A^x$,
   164	and let $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}}$ be a state of dimensionality $k+1$.
   165	Let $\widetilde{A}^x$ be the sub-measurement guaranteed by \Cref{lem:naimark-helper}.
   166	Define $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},x}}$ and $\widetilde{B}^x$ similarly.
   167	We define
   168	\begin{equation*}
   169	\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \ot \big(\ot_{x} \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}}\big)
   170						\ot \big(\ot_{x} \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},x}}\big)
   171	\end{equation*}
   172	and
   173	\begin{align*}
   174	\widehat{A}^x_a
   175	&= \widetilde{A}^x_a \ot \big(\ot_{z \neq x} I_{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},z}}\big)\\
   176	\widehat{B}^y_b
   177	&= \widetilde{B}^y_b \ot \big(\ot_{z\neq y} I_{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},z}}\big).
   178	\end{align*}
   179	Then for all $x,y,z,b$,
   180	\begin{align*}
   181	\bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat{A}^x_a \ot \widehat{B}^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}
   182	& = \bra{\psi} \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}} \ot \bra{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},y}}
   183		\cdot \widetilde{A}^x_a \ot \widetilde{B}^y_b \cdot \ket{\psi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A},x}} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B},y}}\\
   184	&= 	\bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}.
   185	\end{align*}
   186	This completes the proof.
   187	\end{proof}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:292:The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

If $\gamma = 1$, let the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ and $\mathsf{Variable}$ measurements be those produced by Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac} from the anticommuting consistent pair $(A, B)$, acting on the auxiliary $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$ factor, and let the $\mathsf{Pair}$ measurements be trivial. The strategy is symmetric and projective by construction; every measurement is either a post-processed Pauli basis measurement, a measurement supplied by Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, or (in the $\gamma = 0$ case) a product of two commuting consistent measurements, so the strategy is consistent, and commutativity along every edge of $G^{\mathrm{pauli}}$ is checked case by case --- for instance, $(\mathsf{Point},X)$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ commute because both are $X$-basis measurements. /-!
# Transfer of rigidity bounds along the projective dilation

The self-testing argument behind `thm:ms-rigidity` is carried out for the
projective dilation `msDilatedStrategy S` of an arbitrary Magic Square strategy
`S`.  Its conclusions are state-dependent bounds for the *dilated* projectors,
conjugated by local isometries `φ_A`, `φ_B` out of the enlarged local spaces.
The witness for the original strategy is obtained by composing these isometries
with the ground embeddings, and the operators appearing in its bounds are the
conjugates of the *original* effects, that is, of the compressions `Π P Π` of
the dilated projectors `P` to the ground slice (`Π` the ground projection).

Naimark dilation preserves Born probabilities but not state-dependent `≈_δ`
estimates in general (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`,
blueprint `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`), so `Π P Π` and `P` need not act
alike on the dilated state.  Their difference on the dilated state `ψ'` is the
*leakage* `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of `P` out of the ground slice, and the point of this
file is that in the Magic Square game this leakage is controlled by the
cell-consistency defect of the value-to-parity layer: the dilated effect
`P ⊗ 1` almost agrees with the partner effect `1 ⊗ Q` on the other side, and
`(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.  Combined with the closeness of
`(φ_A ⊗ φ_B) ψ'` to the ideal state and the fact that all operators involved
are contractions, this pulls every bound of `thm:ms-rigidity` back from the
dilated strategy to the original one with explicit constants.

## Main statements

* `ms_effect_transfer_A`, `ms_effect_transfer_B`: the bit-measurement distances
  of the original strategy are bounded by three times those of the dilated
  strategy plus `216 ε + 24 η²`, where `η` bounds the state closeness.
* `ms_anticommutator_transfer_A`, `ms_anticommutator_transfer_B`: the
  anticommutator defects transfer with the bound `3 · (dilated) + 15552 ε +
  48 η²`.
* `ms_state_transfer`: the state closeness is unchanged.

## References

`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
-/

/-! ## Cell consistency of the postprocessed effects -/

/-- The Born overlap of Alice's totalized variable bit with Bob's totalized
constraint bit, summed over the bit, is the complement of the reverse
cell-mismatch mass. -/
theorem sum_stateQForm_reverse_eq (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    ∑ b : ZMod 2, stateQForm S.ψ (heteroKron
        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)
        (((S.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)).effect b)) =
      1 - reverseCellMismatchMass S i k := by
  classical
  have hterm : ∀ b : ZMod 2, stateQForm S.ψ (heteroKron
        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)
        (((S.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)).effect b)) =
      ∑ a : msGame.AnswerA, ∑ c : msGame.AnswerB,
        if msBitOrZero a = b then
          (if constraintBitOrZero k c = b then
            outcomeWeight S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) (.constraint i) a c else 0)
        else 0 := by
    intro b
    rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
      heteroKron_finset_sum_left, stateQForm_finset_sum, Finset.sum_filter]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    split_ifs
    · rw [heteroKron_finset_sum_right, stateQForm_finset_sum, Finset.sum_filter]
      rfl
    · simp

/-- The norm of a difference acting on a state is symmetric. -/
theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_comm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M N : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) v‖ = ‖applyOperatorToState (N - M) v‖ := by
  rw [applyOperatorToState_sub_op, applyOperatorToState_sub_op, norm_sub_rev]

/-- Alice's dilated observable of a totalized bit, typed on the enlarged local
space.  Formalization-only abbreviation. -/
abbrev dilatedObsAf (S : Strategy msGame) (x : MsType) (f : MsAnswer → ZMod 2) :
    Op (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) :=
  obsOf (((msDilatedStrategy S).A x).postprocess f)

/-- The inflation of Bob's original observable is the ground compression of
his dilated observable. -/
theorem naimarkInflation_obs_B (S : Strategy msGame) (y : MsType) :
    naimarkInflation (α := MsAnswer) (obsOf ((S.B y).postprocess msBitOrZero)) =
      groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * dilatedObsB S y msBitOrZero *
        groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer := by
  change naimarkInflation (α := MsAnswer) (((S.B y).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect 0 -
    ((S.B y).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect 1) =
    groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
      (dilatedEffectB S y msBitOrZero 0 - dilatedEffectB S y msBitOrZero 1) *
      groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer
  rw [naimarkInflation_sub, naimarkInflation_postprocess_B, naimarkInflation_postprocess_B,
    Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul]

/-- Alice's dilated totalized observables are contractions. -/
theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedObsAf (S : Strategy msGame) (x : MsType)
    (f : MsAnswer → ZMod 2) :
    (dilatedObsAf S x f)ᴴ * dilatedObsAf S x f ≤ 1 :=
  conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_obsOf _

/-- The leakage of Bob's dilated observable out of the ground slice is bounded
by the two forward intertwining defects of its effects. -/
theorem norm_leak_obs_le_B (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) *
        dilatedObsB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero))
        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ≤
      ‖applyOperatorToState
        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 0) 1 -
          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0))
        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ +
      ‖applyOperatorToState
        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 1) 1 -
          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1))
        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ := by
  change ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) *
    (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0 -
      dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1)))
    (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ≤ _
  rw [Matrix.mul_sub, heteroKron_sub_right, applyOperatorToState_sub_op]
  refine le_trans (norm_sub_le _ _) (add_le_add ?_ ?_)
  · exact norm_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _
  · exact norm_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _

This stable public facade re-exports the elementary symmetry facts, the

retaining the imported rigidity theorem and its supporting definitions.

## References

The source statement is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:228-250`, from
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.

open scoped BigOperators Matrix

noncomputable section

/-- The ideal two-qubit projector for one Magic Square output bit. The other
qubit is marginalized by summing the two-qubit Pauli basis projectors. -/
noncomputable def idealMagicBitProj (W : PauliKind) (b : ZMod 2) :
    Op (Fin 2 → ZMod 2) :=
  ∑ e : Fin 2 → ZMod 2, if e 0 = b then pauliProj W e else 0

/-- The ideal state in `thm:ms-rigidity`: two EPR pairs followed by the
auxiliary bipartite state, in local-player register order. -/
noncomputable def idealMsState {ιA'' ιB'' : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA''] [DecidableEq ιA''] [Fintype ιB''] [DecidableEq ιB'']
    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')) :
    EuclideanSpace ℂ
      (((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'') × ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')) :=
  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState (Fin 2 → ZMod 2)) aux)

/-- The isometries and auxiliary unit state in the conclusion of
`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
structure MsRigidityWitness (S : Strategy msGame) where
  ιA'' : Type
  ιB'' : Type
  [ιA''Fintype : Fintype ιA'']
  [ιB''Fintype : Fintype ιB'']
  [ιA''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA'']
  [ιB''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB'']
  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'')
  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')
  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')
  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1

attribute [instance] MsRigidityWitness.ιA''Fintype
  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''Fintype MsRigidityWitness.ιA''DecidableEq
  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''DecidableEq

/-- Alice's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
    (fun _ b => heteroKron
      (conjIsometry w.φA
        (((S.A (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)) 1)
    (fun _ b => heteroKron
      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιA'')) 1)
    (idealMsState w.aux)

/-- Bob's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
      (conjIsometry w.φB
        (((S.B (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)))
    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιB'')))
    (idealMsState w.aux)

/-- Alice's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
  let X := heteroKron
    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
  let Z := heteroKron
    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)

/-- Bob's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
  let X := heteroKron 1
    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
  let Z := heteroKron 1
    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)

/-- `thm:ms-rigidity`, imported from Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:228-250`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.

The paper states the Euclidean estimate at scale `sqrt ε` at lines 624--626
and explains the norm conversion and local basis change at lines 650--652. One
universal constant applies to every strategy and nonnegative error parameter. -/
theorem exists_ms_rigidity :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
      ∀ S : Strategy msGame, 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
        ∃ w : MsRigidityWitness S,
          ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealMsState w.aux‖ ≤
              C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
          msOperatorDistanceA S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
          msOperatorDistanceA S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
          msOperatorDistanceB S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
          msOperatorDistanceB S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
          msAnticommutatorDistanceA S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
          msAnticommutatorDistanceB S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
  sorry

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.NaimarkFull
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.MagicSquareTheorems.Rigidity.Relations
+
+/-!
+# A simultaneous projective dilation of a Magic Square strategy
+
+The rigidity argument for the Magic Square game is stated for an arbitrary
+tensor-product strategy, whose measurements are positive operator valued
+measures.  The self-testing argument, however, manipulates projections.  This
+file removes that discrepancy by dilating an arbitrary strategy to a projective
+one without changing any observable quantity.
+
+Each local Hilbert space `ℂ^ι` is enlarged by one auxiliary register whose
+basis is indexed by `Option MsAnswer`, and the original space is identified with
+the *ground slice* `ℂ^ι ⊗ |⊥⟩`.  The one-measurement Naimark lemma of the low
+individual degree development supplies, for every question separately, a family
+of projections on the enlarged space whose compression to the ground slice
+returns the original effects; the ancilla is the same for all questions, so the
+identification of `ℂ^ι` with the ground slice is a single isometry serving every
+question at once.  Folding the deficiency `1 - ∑_a P_a` into one distinguished
+answer turns the dilated family into a complete projective measurement without
+disturbing the compression, because the original effects already sum to the
+identity.
+
+Since the dilated state is the image of the original state under the two ground
+embeddings, every Born probability, and hence the game value and all the
+rejection, malformed-answer, cell-consistency and parity masses of the
+value-to-parity layer, is unchanged.  Conversely, the local isometries produced
+by a rigidity argument applied to the dilated strategy compose with the ground
+embeddings to give local isometries of the original strategy, and the
+state-dependent norms occurring in the conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` transfer
+along that composition.
+
+## References
+
+The rigidity statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
+proved in Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.  The dilation reuses the
+one-measurement Naimark lemma of
+`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`, formalized as
+`MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.oneMeasNaimark`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+open MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Orthogonality inside a subnormalized family of projections -/
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
+(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  If an orthogonal projection `P` and a
+positive semidefinite operator `Q` satisfy `P + Q ≤ 1`, then `P` annihilates
+`Q`.  Indeed `Tr(P Q)` is nonnegative because both operators are positive
+semidefinite, while `0 ≤ Tr(P (1 - P - Q)) = -Tr(P Q)` because `1 - P - Q` is
+positive semidefinite and `P` is idempotent; so the pairing vanishes and the
+product of two positive semidefinite operators with vanishing trace pairing is
+zero. -/
+theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    {P Q : Op d} (hP : IsProj P) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hPQ : P + Q ≤ 1) :
+    P * Q = 0 := by
+  have hrest : (0 : Op d) ≤ 1 - (P + Q) := sub_nonneg.mpr hPQ
+  have hexpand : P * (1 - (P + Q)) = -(P * Q) := by
+    have hPP : P * P = P := hP.isIdempotentElem
+    rw [Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_add, hPP, Matrix.mul_one]
+    abel
+  have hle : Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) ≤ 0 := by
+    have h := trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hrest
+    rw [hexpand] at h
+    simpa using h
+  have hge : 0 ≤ Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) :=
+    trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hQ
+  exact mul_eq_zero_of_nonneg_of_trace_mul_eq_zero hP.nonneg hQ (le_antisymm hle hge)
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
+(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  A finite family of orthogonal
+projections whose sum is at most the identity is mutually orthogonal: for two
+distinct indices the two projections already sum to at most the identity, so the
+previous lemma applies. -/
+theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
+    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
+    P a * P b = 0 := by
+  refine mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one (hP a) (hP b).nonneg ?_
+  refine le_trans ?_ hsum
+  have hpair : ∑ c ∈ ({a, b} : Finset α), P c = P a + P b := by
+    rw [Finset.sum_pair hab]
+  rw [← hpair]
+  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
+    (fun c _ _ => (hP c).nonneg)
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
+(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  The sum of a mutually orthogonal
+family of projections is again an orthogonal projection; mutual orthogonality is
+supplied by the hypothesis that the sum is at most the identity. -/
+theorem isProj_sum_of_isProj_of_sum_le_one {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
+    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) :
+    IsProj (∑ a, P a) := by
+  constructor
+  · show (∑ a, P a) * (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a
+    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+    rw [Matrix.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single a]
+    · exact (hP a).isIdempotentElem
+    · exact fun b _ hba => mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family hP hsum (Ne.symm hba)
+    · intro ha
+      exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha
+  · show star (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a

   274	  unfold opFamilyDistSq avgOver
   275	  simp [uniformDistribution, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight]

   279	/-- The matrix of an isometry is a matrix isometry. -/
   280	theorem isometryMatrix_conjTranspose_mul {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   281	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   282	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') :
   283	    (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ * isometryMatrix φ = 1 := by
   284	  apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   285	  have hM : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) = φ.toLinearMap :=
   286	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply φ.toLinearMap
   287	  calc
   288	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin ((isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ * isometryMatrix φ) =
   289	        (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ)).adjoint.comp
   290	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ)) :=
   291	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self _
   292	    _ = φ.toLinearMap.adjoint.comp φ.toLinearMap := by rw [hM]
   293	    _ = 1 := φ.adjoint_comp_self'
   294	    _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) := by
   295	      rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_one]
   296	      rfl
   297	
   298	/-- The range projection `V Vᴴ` of a matrix isometry is at most the identity. -/
   299	theorem isometryMatrix_mul_conjTranspose_le_one {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   300	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   301	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') :
   302	    isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ ≤ 1 := by
   303	  have hproj : IsProj (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) := by
   304	    constructor
   305	    · change (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) *
   306	        (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) = isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ
   307	      rw [Matrix.mul_assoc, ← Matrix.mul_assoc (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ,
   308	        isometryMatrix_conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   309	    · change star (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) =
   310	        isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ
   311	      simp [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
   312	  exact sub_nonneg.mp hproj.one_sub.nonneg

   314	/-- Conjugation by an isometry preserves contractions. -/
   315	theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   316	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   317	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') {A : Op ι} (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) :
   318	    (conjIsometry φ A)ᴴ * conjIsometry φ A ≤ 1 := by
   319	  rw [conjIsometry_eq]
   320	  have h1 : (isometryMatrix φ * A * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ)ᴴ *
   321	      (isometryMatrix φ * A * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) =
   322	      isometryMatrix φ * (Aᴴ * A) * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := by
   323	    simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_conjTranspose,
   324	      Matrix.mul_assoc]
   325	    rw [← Matrix.mul_assoc (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ (isometryMatrix φ),
   326	      isometryMatrix_conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   327	  rw [h1]
   328	  calc isometryMatrix φ * (Aᴴ * A) * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ ≤
   329	        isometryMatrix φ * (1 : Op ι) * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := by
   330	        rw [Matrix.le_iff]
   331	        have h := (Matrix.le_iff.mp hA).mul_mul_conjTranspose_same (isometryMatrix φ)
   332	        convert h using 1
   333	        simp [Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul]
   334	    _ = isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := by rw [Matrix.mul_one]
   335	    _ ≤ 1 := isometryMatrix_mul_conjTranspose_le_one φ

   343	  rw [← Matrix.mul_assoc (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ (isometryMatrix φ),

   349	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (A B : Op ι) :

   353	/-- The two-sided isometry image of a state is the action of the Kronecker

   355	theorem isometryTensor_eq_toEuclideanLin {ιA ιB κA κB : Type}

   393	/-- A left-placed conjugated operator acts on the transported state as the

   395	theorem applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_conjIsometry {ιA ιB κA κB : Type}

   408	  rw [conjIsometry_eq, ← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, ← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul,

   431	/-! ## The ground projection -/
   432	
   433	/-- The orthogonal projection of an enlarged local space onto its ground slice,
   434	namely the inflation of the identity.  Formalization-only support for the
   435	transfer step of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   436	def groundProjection (ι α : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   437	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] : Op (ι × Option α) :=
   438	  naimarkInflation (α := α) (1 : Op ι)
   439	
   440	/-- Inflation is multiplicative. -/
   441	theorem naimarkInflation_mul {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   442	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M N : Op ι) :
   443	    naimarkInflation (α := α) M * naimarkInflation (α := α) N =
   444	      naimarkInflation (α := α) (M * N) := by
   445	  ext p q
   446	  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, naimarkInflation_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type,
   447	    Fintype.sum_option]
   448	  by_cases hp : p.2 = none <;> by_cases hq : q.2 = none <;> simp [hp, hq]
   449	
   450	/-- Inflation commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
   451	theorem naimarkInflation_conjTranspose {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   452	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) :
   453	    (naimarkInflation (α := α) M)ᴴ = naimarkInflation (α := α) Mᴴ := by
   454	  ext p q
   455	  simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, naimarkInflation_apply]
   456	  by_cases hp : p.2 = none <;> by_cases hq : q.2 = none <;> simp [hp, hq]
   457	
   458	/-- The ground projection is an orthogonal projection. -/
   459	theorem isProj_groundProjection (ι α : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   460	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] : IsProj (groundProjection ι α) := by
   461	  constructor
   462	  · change groundProjection ι α * groundProjection ι α = groundProjection ι α
   463	    rw [groundProjection, naimarkInflation_mul, Matrix.mul_one]
   464	  · change star (groundProjection ι α) = groundProjection ι α
   465	    rw [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, groundProjection, naimarkInflation_conjTranspose,
   466	      Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   467	
   468	/-- Inflating the compression of an operator to the ground slice is compressing
   469	it by the ground projection. -/
   470	theorem naimarkInflation_naimarkCompression {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   471	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (P : Op (ι × Option α)) :
   472	    naimarkInflation (α := α) (naimarkCompression (α := α) P) =
   473	      groundProjection ι α * P * groundProjection ι α := by
   474	  ext p q
   475	  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, naimarkInflation_apply, naimarkCompression_apply,
   476	    groundProjection, Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.sum_option, Matrix.one_apply]
   477	  by_cases hp : p.2 = none <;> by_cases hq : q.2 = none <;> simp [hp, hq]
   478	
   479	/-- Compression to the ground slice commutes with finite sums. -/
   480	theorem naimarkCompression_finset_sum {ι α β : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   481	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (s : Finset β) (M : β → Op (ι × Option α)) :
   482	    naimarkCompression (α := α) (∑ b ∈ s, M b) =
   483	      ∑ b ∈ s, naimarkCompression (α := α) (M b) := by
   484	  ext i j
   485	  simp [Matrix.sum_apply]

   487	/-- The dilated state lies in the ground slice on Alice's side. -/
   488	theorem applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_groundProjection (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   489	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   490	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   491	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) 1) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   492	      naimarkDilatedState α ψ := by
   493	  have hfull : applyOperatorToState
   494	      (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) (groundProjection ιB α))
   495	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) = naimarkDilatedState α ψ := by
   496	    rw [groundProjection, groundProjection, applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_naimarkInflation,
   497	      heteroKron_one_one, applyOperatorToState_one]
   498	  conv_lhs => rw [← hfull]
   499	  rw [← applyOperatorToState_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   500	    (isProj_groundProjection ιA α).isIdempotentElem.eq, Matrix.one_mul]
   501	  exact hfull

   503	/-- The dilated state lies in the ground slice on Bob's side. -/
   504	theorem applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_groundProjection (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   505	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   506	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   507	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α)) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   508	      naimarkDilatedState α ψ := by
   509	  have hfull : applyOperatorToState
   510	      (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) (groundProjection ιB α))
   511	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) = naimarkDilatedState α ψ := by
   512	    rw [groundProjection, groundProjection, applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_naimarkInflation,
   513	      heteroKron_one_one, applyOperatorToState_one]
   514	  conv_lhs => rw [← hfull]
   515	  rw [← applyOperatorToState_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   516	    (isProj_groundProjection ιB α).isIdempotentElem.eq, Matrix.one_mul]
   517	  exact hfull

   519	/-- The complement of the ground slice annihilates the dilated state on Alice's
   520	side. -/
   521	theorem applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_one_sub_groundProjection (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   522	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   523	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   524	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 - groundProjection ιA α) 1)
   525	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) = 0 := by
   526	  have h : heteroKron (1 - groundProjection ιA α) (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) =
   527	      1 - heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) 1 := by
   528	    rw [heteroKron_sub_left, heteroKron_one_one]
   529	  have hsub : applyOperatorToState (1 - heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) 1)
   530	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   531	      applyOperatorToState 1 (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) -
   532	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) 1)
   533	          (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by
   534	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   535	  rw [h, hsub, applyOperatorToState_one, applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_groundProjection,
   536	    sub_self]

   538	/-- The complement of the ground slice annihilates the dilated state on Bob's
   539	side. -/
   540	theorem applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   541	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   542	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   543	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (1 - groundProjection ιB α))
   544	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) = 0 := by
   545	  have h : heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α)) (1 - groundProjection ιB α) =
   546	      1 - heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α) := by
   547	    rw [heteroKron_sub_right, heteroKron_one_one]
   548	  have hsub : applyOperatorToState (1 - heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α))
   549	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   550	      applyOperatorToState 1 (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) -
   551	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α))
   552	          (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by
   553	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   554	  rw [h, hsub, applyOperatorToState_one, applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_groundProjection,
   555	    sub_self]

   557	/-! ## Leakage out of the ground slice is bounded by the intertwining defect -/
   558	
   559	/-- The leakage of a left-placed operator `P` out of the ground slice on the
   560	dilated state is at most the intertwining defect of `P ⊗ 1` against any
   561	right-placed operator `1 ⊗ Q`, because `(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.
   562	This is the estimate replacing the `≈_δ` preservation that Naimark dilation
   563	lacks (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`). -/
   564	theorem norm_leftTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   565	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   566	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
   567	    (P : Op (ιA × Option α)) (Q : Op (ιB × Option α)) :
   568	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * P) 1)
   569	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   570	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q)
   571	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   572	  set ψ' := naimarkDilatedState α ψ
   573	  set L : Op ((ιA × Option α) × (ιB × Option α)) :=
   574	    heteroKron (1 - groundProjection ιA α) 1
   575	  have hL0 : applyOperatorToState L ψ' = 0 :=
   576	    applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_one_sub_groundProjection α ψ
   577	  have hLcontr : Lᴴ * L ≤ 1 :=
   578	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor
   579	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection ιA α).one_sub)
   580	  have hsplit : heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * P)
   581	      (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) = L * heteroKron P 1 := by
   582	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   583	  have hcomm : L * heteroKron 1 Q = heteroKron 1 Q * L := by
   584	    rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul,
   585	      Matrix.mul_one]
   586	  have key : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * P) 1) ψ' =
   587	      applyOperatorToState L
   588	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q) ψ') := by
   589	    rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   590	    have hdec : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1) ψ' =
   591	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' +
   592	          applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' := by
   593	      simp [applyOperatorToState]
   594	    rw [hdec, applyOperatorToState_add, ← applyOperatorToState_mul L (heteroKron 1 Q), hcomm,
   595	      applyOperatorToState_mul, hL0, applyOperatorToState_zero, add_zero]
   596	  rw [key]
   597	  exact norm_applyOperatorToState_le hLcontr _
   598	
   599	/-- The leakage of a right-placed operator `Q` out of the ground slice on the
   600	dilated state is at most its intertwining defect against any left-placed
   601	operator. -/
   602	theorem norm_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   603	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   604	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
   605	    (P : Op (ιA × Option α)) (Q : Op (ιB × Option α)) :
   606	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * Q))
   607	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   608	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q)
   609	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   610	  set ψ' := naimarkDilatedState α ψ
   611	  set L : Op ((ιA × Option α) × (ιB × Option α)) :=
   612	    heteroKron 1 (1 - groundProjection ιB α)
   613	  have hL0 : applyOperatorToState L ψ' = 0 :=
   614	    applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection α ψ
   615	  have hLcontr : Lᴴ * L ≤ 1 :=
   616	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_rightTensor
   617	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection ιB α).one_sub)
   618	  have hsplit : heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α))
   619	      ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * Q) = L * heteroKron 1 Q := by
   620	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   621	  have hcomm : L * heteroKron P 1 = heteroKron P 1 * L := by
   622	    rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul,
   623	      Matrix.mul_one]
   624	  have key : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * Q)) ψ' =
   625	      applyOperatorToState L
   626	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ') := by
   627	    rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   628	    have hdec : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' =
   629	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ' +
   630	          applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1) ψ' := by
   631	      simp [applyOperatorToState]
   632	    rw [hdec, applyOperatorToState_add, ← applyOperatorToState_mul L (heteroKron P 1), hcomm,
   633	      applyOperatorToState_mul, hL0, applyOperatorToState_zero, add_zero]
   634	  have hneg : -applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' =
   635	      applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ' := by
   636	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   637	  rw [key]
   638	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState L
   639	          (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ')‖ ≤
   640	        ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ'‖ :=
   641	        norm_applyOperatorToState_le hLcontr _
   642	    _ = ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q) ψ'‖ := by
   643	        rw [← hneg, norm_neg]

   269	theorem applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_sub_compression (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   270	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   271	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (P : Op (ιA × Option α)) :
   272	    applyOperatorToState

   276	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by
   277	  have hsplit : P - groundProjection ιA α * P * groundProjection ιA α =
   278	      (1 - groundProjection ιA α) * P +
   279	        (groundProjection ιA α * P) * (1 - groundProjection ιA α) := by
   280	    noncomm_ring
   281	  rw [hsplit, heteroKron_add_left, applyOperatorToState_add_op]
   282	  have hzero : applyOperatorToState
   283	      (heteroKron ((groundProjection ιA α * P) * (1 - groundProjection ιA α)) 1)

   286	        (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) =
   287	        heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α * P) 1 * heteroKron (1 - groundProjection ιA α) 1 by
   288	      rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.mul_one]]

   321	/-- Per-outcome transfer estimate on Alice's side.  For any target operator `T`,
   322	the distance of the conjugated original effect from `T` on the target state
   323	`ξ` is at most the distance of the conjugated dilated effect from `T`, plus the
   324	intertwining defect of the dilated effect against Bob's partner effect `Q` on
   325	the dilated state, plus twice the distance from `ξ` to the transported dilated
   326	state.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   327	theorem norm_effect_transfer_term_le_A {κA κB : Type} [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA]
   328	    [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB] (S : Strategy msGame)
   329	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   330	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιB × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   331	    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB)) (T : Op (κA × κB)) (x y : MsType)
   332	    (f g : MsAnswer → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2) :
   333	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (conjIsometry (φA.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιA MsAnswer))
   334	        (((S.A x).postprocess f).effect b)) 1 - T) ξ‖ ≤
   335	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 - T) ξ‖ +
   336	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   337	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S x f b) 1 - heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S y g b))
   338	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ +
   339	      2 * ‖isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) - ξ‖ := by
   340	  rw [conjIsometry_comp_naimarkEmbedding, naimarkInflation_postprocess_A]
   341	  have hP := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedEffectA S x f b
   342	  have hG : (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)ᴴ * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer ≤ 1 :=
   343	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)
   344	  have hAd : (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) (1 : Op κB))ᴴ *
   345	      heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 ≤ 1 :=
   346	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry φA hP)
   347	  have hAo : (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer *
   348	      dilatedEffectA S x f b * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) (1 : Op κB))ᴴ *
   349	      heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer *
   350	        dilatedEffectA S x f b * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) 1 ≤ 1 :=
   351	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry φA
   352	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hG hP) hG))
   353	  set Ao : Op (κA × κB) := heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer *
   354	    dilatedEffectA S x f b * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) 1 with hAo_def
   355	  set Ad : Op (κA × κB) := heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 with hAd_def
   356	  set ψ'' := isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) with hψ''
   357	  have h1 : applyOperatorToState (Ao - T) ξ =
   358	      applyOperatorToState (Ad - T) ξ - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ := by
   359	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   360	  have h2 : applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ =
   361	      applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ψ'' - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) (ψ'' - ξ) := by
   362	    rw [applyOperatorToState_sub, sub_sub_cancel]
   363	  have h3 : ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ψ''‖ ≤
   364	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   365	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S x f b) 1 - heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S y g b))
   366	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ := by
   367	    have hdiff : Ad - Ao = heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b -
   368	        groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer * dilatedEffectA S x f b *
   369	          groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) 1 := by
   370	      rw [hAd_def, hAo_def, conjIsometry_sub, heteroKron_sub_left]
   371	    rw [hdiff, hψ'', applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_conjIsometry, norm_isometryTensor,
   372	      applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_sub_compression]
   373	    exact norm_leftTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _
   374	  have h4 : ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) (ψ'' - ξ)‖ ≤ 2 * ‖ψ'' - ξ‖ :=
   375	    norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_le hAd hAo _
   376	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (Ao - T) ξ‖ =
   377	        ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - T) ξ - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ‖ := by rw [h1]
   378	    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - T) ξ‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ‖ :=
   379	        norm_sub_le _ _
   380	    _ ≤ _ := by

   383	          (applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) (ψ'' - ξ)), h3, h4]

   422	  have h3 : ‖applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) ψ''‖ ≤
   423	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   424	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S x f b) 1 - heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S y g b))
   425	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ := by
   426	    have hdiff : Bd - Bo = heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedEffectB S y g b -
   427	        groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * dilatedEffectB S y g b *
   428	          groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) := by

   432	    exact norm_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _
   433	  have h4 : ‖applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) (ψ'' - ξ)‖ ≤ 2 * ‖ψ'' - ξ‖ :=
   434	    norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_le hBd hBo _

    56	constraint bit, summed over the bit, is the complement of the reverse

    65	        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)
    66	        (((S.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)).effect b)) =
    67	      ∑ a : msGame.AnswerA, ∑ c : msGame.AnswerB,
    68	        if msBitOrZero a = b then

   162	  rw [point_defect_eq] at h1

   179	      2 * (1 ^ 2 - (1 - reverseCellMismatchMass S i k)) := h1

     3	/-!
     4	# Transfer of rigidity bounds along the projective dilation
     5	
     6	The self-testing argument behind `thm:ms-rigidity` is carried out for the
     7	projective dilation `msDilatedStrategy S` of an arbitrary Magic Square strategy
     8	`S`.  Its conclusions are state-dependent bounds for the *dilated* projectors,
     9	conjugated by local isometries `φ_A`, `φ_B` out of the enlarged local spaces.
    10	The witness for the original strategy is obtained by composing these isometries
    11	with the ground embeddings, and the operators appearing in its bounds are the
    12	conjugates of the *original* effects, that is, of the compressions `Π P Π` of
    13	the dilated projectors `P` to the ground slice (`Π` the ground projection).
    14	
    15	Naimark dilation preserves Born probabilities but not state-dependent `≈_δ`
    16	estimates in general (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`,
    17	blueprint `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`), so `Π P Π` and `P` need not act
    18	alike on the dilated state.  Their difference on the dilated state `ψ'` is the
    19	*leakage* `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of `P` out of the ground slice, and the point of this
    20	file is that in the Magic Square game this leakage is controlled by the
    21	cell-consistency defect of the value-to-parity layer: the dilated effect
    22	`P ⊗ 1` almost agrees with the partner effect `1 ⊗ Q` on the other side, and
    23	`(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.  Combined with the closeness of
    24	`(φ_A ⊗ φ_B) ψ'` to the ideal state and the fact that all operators involved
    25	are contractions, this pulls every bound of `thm:ms-rigidity` back from the
    26	dilated strategy to the original one with explicit constants.
    27	
    28	## Main statements
    29	
    30	* `ms_effect_transfer_A`, `ms_effect_transfer_B`: the bit-measurement distances
    31	  of the original strategy are bounded by three times those of the dilated
    32	  strategy plus `216 ε + 24 η²`, where `η` bounds the state closeness.
    33	* `ms_anticommutator_transfer_A`, `ms_anticommutator_transfer_B`: the
    34	  anticommutator defects transfer with the bound `3 · (dilated) + 15552 ε +
    35	  48 η²`.
    36	* `ms_state_transfer`: the state closeness is unchanged.
