   619	/-! ## Composition of the dilation with later local isometries -/
   620	
   621	/-- The matrix of a linear isometry of Euclidean spaces in the computational
   622	bases.  Formalization-only support for `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   623	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   624	noncomputable def isometryMatrix {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   625	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   626	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') : Matrix ι' ι ℂ :=
   627	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
   628	
   629	/-- Conjugation by an isometry is conjugation by its matrix. -/
   630	theorem conjIsometry_eq {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   631	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   632	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (M : Op ι) :
   633	    conjIsometry φ M = isometryMatrix φ * M * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := rfl
   634	
   635	/-- The matrix of an isometry acts on vectors as the isometry does. -/
   636	theorem isometryMatrix_mulVec {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   637	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   638	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   639	    isometryMatrix φ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x = WithLp.ofLp (φ x) := by
   640	  have h : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) = φ.toLinearMap :=
   641	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply φ.toLinearMap
   642	  have h' : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) x = φ x := by rw [h]; rfl
   643	  simpa using congrArg WithLp.ofLp h'
   644	
   645	/-- The columns of the matrix of an isometry are the images of the basis
   646	vectors. -/
   647	theorem isometryMatrix_apply {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   648	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   649	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (k : ι') (i : ι) :
   650	    isometryMatrix φ k i =
   651	      φ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1)) k := by
   652	  have h := congrFun (isometryMatrix_mulVec φ
   653	    ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) k
   654	  rw [← h]
   655	  simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.equiv, eq_comm]
   656	
   657	/-- The matrix of a composite isometry is the product of the two matrices. -/
   658	theorem isometryMatrix_comp {ι κ ν : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   659	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ν] [DecidableEq ν]
   660	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ν)
   661	    (E : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
   662	    isometryMatrix (φ.comp E) = isometryMatrix φ * isometryMatrix E := by
   663	  ext k i
   664	  have h := congrFun (isometryMatrix_mulVec φ
   665	    (E ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1)))) k
   666	  rw [isometryMatrix_apply, Matrix.mul_apply]
   667	  simp only [isometryMatrix_apply E]
   668	  simpa [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct] using h.symm
   669	
   670	/-- Conjugating by a composite isometry is conjugating twice.  This is how the
   671	ground embeddings of the dilation combine with the local isometries produced by
   672	the self-testing argument of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   673	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   674	theorem conjIsometry_comp {ι κ ν : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   675	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ν] [DecidableEq ν]
   676	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ν)
   677	    (E : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) (M : Op ι) :
   678	    conjIsometry (φ.comp E) M = conjIsometry φ (conjIsometry E M) := by
   679	  rw [conjIsometry_eq, conjIsometry_eq, conjIsometry_eq, isometryMatrix_comp]
   680	  simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.mul_assoc]

   682	/-- The two-sided isometry image of a bipartite state, written through the
   683	Kronecker product of the two isometry matrices. -/
   684	theorem isometryTensor_apply_eq {ιA ιB κA κB : Type}
   685	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   686	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
   687	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   688	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   689	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (p : κA × κB) :
   690	    isometryTensor φA φB ψ p =
   691	      ∑ q : ιA × ιB,
   692	        Matrix.kronecker (isometryMatrix φA) (isometryMatrix φB) p q * ψ q := by
   693	  simp [isometryTensor, Matrix.kronecker, Fintype.sum_prod_type, isometryMatrix_apply,
   694	    EuclideanSpace.equiv, mul_assoc]
   695	
   696	/-- Applying two local isometries after two others is the same as applying their
   697	composites.  Together with `conjIsometry_comp` this is the composition rule used
   698	to turn a rigidity witness for the dilated strategy into one for the original
   699	strategy. -/
   700	theorem isometryTensor_comp {ιA ιB κA κB νA νB : Type}
   701	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   702	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
   703	    [Fintype νA] [DecidableEq νA] [Fintype νB] [DecidableEq νB]
   704	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ κA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ νA)
   705	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ κB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ νB)
   706	    (EA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   707	    (EB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   708	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   709	    isometryTensor (φA.comp EA) (φB.comp EB) ψ =
   710	      isometryTensor φA φB (isometryTensor EA EB ψ) := by
   711	  ext p
   712	  rw [isometryTensor_apply_eq, isometryTensor_apply_eq]
   713	  simp only [isometryTensor_apply_eq, isometryMatrix_comp, Finset.mul_sum]
   714	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   715	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => ?_
   716	  have hk : (isometryMatrix φA * isometryMatrix EA).kronecker
   717	        (isometryMatrix φB * isometryMatrix EB) =
   718	      (isometryMatrix φA).kronecker (isometryMatrix φB) *
   719	        (isometryMatrix EA).kronecker (isometryMatrix EB) :=
   720	    Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul _ _ _ _
   721	  rw [hk, Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.sum_mul]
   722	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => by ring

   724	/-- The ground embeddings of the dilation composed with two later local
   725	isometries carry the original state exactly as those isometries carry the
   726	dilated state. -/
   727	theorem isometryTensor_comp_naimarkEmbedding (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   728	    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   729	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
   730	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × Option α) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   731	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB × Option α) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   732	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :

   739	/-- Conjugating an operator by the ground embedding inflates it: the result acts
   740	as the original operator on the ground slice and annihilates the orthogonal
   741	complement. -/
   742	theorem conjIsometry_naimarkEmbedding {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

   745	  ext p q

   749	  by_cases hp : p.2 = none
   750	  · by_cases hq : q.2 = none <;> simp [hp, hq, eq_comm]
   751	  · simp [hp]

   761	      conjIsometry φ (naimarkInflation (α := α) M) := by
   762	  rw [conjIsometry_comp, conjIsometry_naimarkEmbedding]

   809	    · simp [hoa, hob, heteroKron, applyOperatorToState, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct,

   837	theorem opFamilyDistSq_naimarkInflation (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   838	    {X γ ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype γ] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   839	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   840	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → γ → Op ιA) (P : X → γ → Op ιB)
   841	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :

   845	        (fun x c => heteroKron (naimarkInflation (α := α) (N x c))
   846	          (naimarkInflation (α := α) (P x c)))

   848	      opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x c => heteroKron (M x c) (P x c))
   849	        (fun x c => heteroKron (N x c) (P x c)) ψ := by
   850	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
   851	  congr 1
   852	  funext x
   853	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => ?_

   857	    intro ρA ρB _ _ _ _ X Y Z

   859	    simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, sub_mul]

   862	    ext p q
   863	    by_cases h : p.2 = none ∧ q.2 = none <;> simp [h]

   175	/-! ### One-measurement Naimark dilation (Lemma 5.2)
   176	
   177	The one-measurement Naimark dilation is the building block for the full
   178	theorem. Given a submeasurement `M` on space `d`, it produces a projective
   179	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α`, where `Option α`
   180	models the auxiliary register with one extra dimension `none = ⊥` for the
   181	missing mass `I − ∑ M_a`. -/
   182	
   183	/-- The auxiliary pure-state projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` on `Option α`, where `⊥ = none`.
   184	This is the initial state of the auxiliary register before the Naimark
   185	isometry is applied. -/
   186	def naimarkAuxProjector (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   187	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   188	  Matrix.single none none 1
   189	
   190	/-- The lifted density matrix for one-measurement Naimark dilation:
   191	`ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)`.
   192	The scaling by `|Option α|` ensures the normalized trace is preserved:
   193	`τ'(ρ_lifted) = τ(ρ)`, where `τ'` is the normalized trace on the enlarged space. -/
   194	noncomputable def oneMeasLiftedDensity {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   195	    (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   196	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) :
   197	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) :=
   198	  (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) • Matrix.kronecker ρ (naimarkAuxProjector α)
   199	
   200	/-- One-measurement Naimark dilation data at the matrix level.
   201	
   202	Given a submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, this witnesses the existence
   203	of a projective submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` that
   204	preserves all expectation values. This is Lemma 5.2 of the paper.
   205	
   206	The construction: let `V : H → H ⊗ ℂ^{|α|+1}` be the isometry
   207	`V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a |ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   208	Then `P̂_a = V† (I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|) V` is a projection, and
   209	`⟨ψ|M_a|ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ⊗⊥|P̂_a|ψ⊗⊥⟩`. -/
   210	structure OneMeasNaimarkData (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   211	    (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
   212	  /-- The source submeasurement being dilated. -/
   213	  source : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d
   214	  /-- The dilated projective effects on `d × Option α`.
   215	  For outcome `some a`, this is the Naimark projector `P̂_a`.
   216	  For outcome `none`, this is the projector for the "missing mass". -/
   217	  liftedEffect : Option α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α)
   218	  /-- Each lifted effect is a genuine orthogonal projection. Positivity follows
   219	  from `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/
   220	  lifted_isProj : ∀ a, MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj (liftedEffect a)
   221	  /-- The lifted projections sum to at most identity (which together with
   222	  `lifted_isProj` implies mutual orthogonality). -/
   223	  lifted_sum_le_one : ∑ a, liftedEffect a ≤ 1
   224	  /-- **Expectation preservation**: for any operator `ρ` on `Op d`,
   225	  the expectation of outcome `a` under the original submeasurement equals
   226	  the expectation under the dilated projective submeasurement with the
   227	  Naimark-lifted state. The identity is linear, so it holds for all operators,
   228	  not just density matrices. This is the core content of the dilation. -/
   229	  expectation_preservation : ∀ (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (a : α),
   230	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * source.effect a) =
   231	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   232	        (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ * liftedEffect (some a))
   233	
   234	/-- Positivity of a lifted Naimark effect, derived from its projectivity.
   235	
   236	Lean-only consequence of the one-measurement Naimark data: the paper records
   237	the lifted effects as projections, and positivity is supplied here by the
   238	Mathlib star-projection order theorem through `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/

   240	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   241	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (a : Option α) :
   242	    0 ≤ data.liftedEffect a :=
   243	  (data.lifted_isProj a).nonneg

   139	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData Outcome d) (a : Outcome) (i j : d) :

   141	      data.source.effect a i j := by
   142	  classical
   143	  letI : Nonempty d := ⟨i⟩
   144	  have h := data.expectation_preservation (Matrix.single j i (1 : ℂ)) a
   145	  unfold oneMeasLiftedDensity MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace at h
   146	  simp [Matrix.trace, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.kronecker, naimarkAuxProjector,

   148	  have hd : (Fintype.card d : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
   149	    exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero
   150	  have hOutcome : (Fintype.card (Option Outcome) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
   151	    exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero
   152	  field_simp [hd, hOutcome] at h
   153	  have hsum_if_pair_eq :
   154	      ∀ F : d → d → ℂ,

   157	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   158	    · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
   159	      · simp
   160	      · intro y _ hyi
   161	        simp [show i ≠ y by exact fun h => hyi h.symm]
   162	      · intro hi
   163	        simp at hi
   164	    · intro x _ hxj
   165	      simp [show j ≠ x by exact fun h => hxj h.symm]
   166	    · intro hj
   167	      simp at hj
   168	  rw [hsum_if_pair_eq (fun y x => data.source.effect a y x)] at h
   169	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum] at h
   170	  rw [hsum_if_pair_eq (fun y x => data.liftedEffect (some a) (y, none) (x, none))] at h
   171	  have hc : (↑(Fintype.card Outcome) + 1 : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
   172	    positivity
   173	  exact mul_left_cancel₀ hc (by
   174	    calc
   175	      (↑(Fintype.card Outcome) + 1 : ℂ) *
   176	          data.liftedEffect (some a) (i, none) (j, none) =

   191	    [Fintype OutcomeB] [DecidableEq OutcomeB]

   199	        (naimarkProductExtensionState HA HB
   200	          (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeA)
   201	          (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeB)

   203	          (QuantumState.tensor

/-!
# Section 5 — one-measurement Naimark

Unitary-extension machinery and the one-measurement Naimark lemma.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- The Naimark column acts as an isometry on the input subspace: `VP = V`. -/
private lemma oneMeasNaimarkColumn_mul_inputProj
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d) :
    oneMeasNaimarkColumn M * oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d) =
      oneMeasNaimarkColumn M := by
  ext ⟨d₁, oa₁⟩ ⟨d₂, oa₂⟩
  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, oneMeasNaimarkInputProj,
    oneMeasNaimarkAuxTransition]
  cases oa₂ with
  | none =>
    have : ∀ x : d × Option α,
        oneMeasNaimarkColumn M (d₁, oa₁) x *
          Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)
            (Matrix.single (none : Option α) (none : Option α) (1 : ℂ)) x (d₂, none) =
          if x = (d₂, (none : Option α)) then
            oneMeasNaimarkColumn M (d₁, oa₁) (d₂, none)
          else 0 := by
      intro ⟨k₁, k₂⟩
      cases k₂ with
      | none =>
          by_cases h : k₁ = d₂ <;>
            simp [Matrix.kronecker, Prod.ext_iff, h]
      | some a =>
          have hneq : (k₁, some a) ≠ (d₂, (none : Option α)) := by
            intro h
            cases h
          simp [Matrix.kronecker, hneq]
    simp_rw [this]
    rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq' Finset.univ (d₂, (none : Option α)) (fun _ =>
      oneMeasNaimarkColumn M (d₁, oa₁) (d₂, none))]
    simp
  | some a₂ =>
    simp [oneMeasNaimarkColumn, Matrix.kronecker]

-- This is independent of Naimark and could be moved to `LDT/Preliminaries`.
/-- **Partial isometry to unitary extension** (general fact).

If `V†V = P` where `P` is a projection and `V = VP`, then there exists
a unitary `U` on the full space with `UP = V`.

This is a standard result in finite-dimensional linear algebra: V is an
isometry from range(P) to V's range, and in finite dimensions any
isometry between subspaces extends to a unitary.

**Mathlib route**: `LinearIsometry.extend` provides the extension for
linear isometries between inner product spaces. The gap is the
matrix-to-`EuclideanSpace` transport. -/
private lemma partialIsometry_to_unitary
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (V P : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n)
    (hP : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj P)
    (hVP : V * P = V)
    (hVV : Vᴴ * V = P) :
    ∃ U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ,
      (U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) * P = V := by
  classical
  have toEuclideanLin_mul :
      ∀ A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n,
        Matrix.toEuclideanLin (A * B) =
          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).comp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin B) := by
    intro A B
    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same (p := (2 : ENNReal)) A B]
  let Pₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin P
  let Vₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin V
  let S : Submodule ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := LinearMap.range Pₗ
  letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ S := Submodule.innerProductSpace S
  have hP_fix : ∀ x : S, Pₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = x := by
    intro x
    rcases x.2 with ⟨y, hy⟩
    rw [← hy]
    calc
      Pₗ (Pₗ y) = (Pₗ.comp Pₗ) y := rfl
      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (P * P) y := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
      _ = Pₗ y := by rw [hP.isIdempotentElem.eq]
  have hVP_lin : Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Vₗ := by
    calc
      Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (V * P) := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
      _ = Vₗ := by rw [hVP]
  have hgram : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Pₗ := by
    calc
      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Matrix.toEuclideanLin P := by rw [hVV]
      _ = Pₗ := rfl
  let Llin : S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Vₗ.comp S.subtype
  have hLnorm : ∀ x : S, ‖Llin x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
    exact (LinearMap.norm_map_iff_inner_map_map
      (𝕜 := ℂ) (E := S) (E' := EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
      (F := S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n) Llin).2 fun x y => by
      have hy : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = y := by
        calc
          Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) =
              Pₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hgram]
          _ = y := hP_fix y
      calc
        inner ℂ (Llin x) (Llin y) =
            inner ℂ (Vₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) (Vₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := rfl
        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := by
          dsimp [Vₗ]
          rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
          exact (LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (𝕜 := ℂ)
            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V) (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n))).symm
        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hy]
        _ = inner ℂ x y := rfl
  let L : S →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := { toLinearMap := Llin, norm_map' := hLnorm }
  let Ulin : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n :=
    LinearIsometry.extend (𝕜 := ℂ) (V := EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (S := S) L

    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm Ulin.toLinearMap

     4	/-!
     5	# Contractions, isometries and the ground slice of the dilation
     6	
     7	Support for the transfer step of `thm:ms-rigidity` (blueprint
     8	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
     9	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`):
    10	the calculus needed to compare the dilated projective strategy of
    11	`Rigidity/Dilation.lean` with the original strategy on states.
    12	
    13	* Contractions: operators `K` with `Kᴴ K ≤ 1` do not increase norms; effects,
    14	  observables of binary measurements, orthogonal projections, tensor placements,
    15	  products and isometry conjugates are contractions.
    16	* Matrices of isometries: `Vᴴ V = 1`, the two-sided isometry image of a state
    17	  preserves norms, and a conjugated local operator acts on the transported state
    18	  as the original operator acts on the original state.
    19	* The ground projection `Π` of an enlarged local space: an orthogonal projection
    20	  fixing the dilated state, with `Π P Π` the inflation of the compression of `P`.
    21	* Leakage: the part `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of a dilated operator that leaves the ground
    22	  slice is bounded by the intertwining defect of `P ⊗ 1` against any `1 ⊗ Q`,
    23	  because `(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `(1 ⊗ Q) ψ'`.  This is the estimate that
    24	  replaces the `≈_δ`-preservation which Naimark dilation lacks in general
    25	  (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`, blueprint
    26	  `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`).
    27	
    28	## References
    29	
    30	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
    31	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
    32	-/

    45	/-- Applying a product of operators is successive application. -/
    46	theorem applyOperatorToState_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    47	    (M N : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    48	    applyOperatorToState (M * N) v =
    49	      applyOperatorToState M (applyOperatorToState N v) := by
    50	  unfold applyOperatorToState
    51	  simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same]
    52	
    53	/-- The identity acts trivially. -/
    54	theorem applyOperatorToState_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    55	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    56	    applyOperatorToState (1 : Op ι) v = v := by
    57	  simp [applyOperatorToState]
    58	
    59	/-- Operators act additively on states. -/
    60	theorem applyOperatorToState_add {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    61	    (M : Op ι) (u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    62	    applyOperatorToState M (u + v) =
    63	      applyOperatorToState M u + applyOperatorToState M v := by
    64	  simp [applyOperatorToState]
    65	
    66	/-- Operators act additively on differences of states. -/
    67	theorem applyOperatorToState_sub {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    68	    (M : Op ι) (u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    69	    applyOperatorToState M (u - v) =
    70	      applyOperatorToState M u - applyOperatorToState M v := by
    71	  simp [applyOperatorToState]
    72	
    73	/-- The action on states is additive in the operator. -/
    74	theorem applyOperatorToState_add_op {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    75	    (M N : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    76	    applyOperatorToState (M + N) v =
    77	      applyOperatorToState M v + applyOperatorToState N v := by
    78	  simp [applyOperatorToState]
    79	
    80	/-- Operators annihilate the zero state. -/
    81	theorem applyOperatorToState_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Op ι) :
    82	    applyOperatorToState M (0 : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) = 0 := by
    83	  simp [applyOperatorToState]

    85	/-- Applying a product of rectangular matrices is successive application. -/
    86	theorem toEuclideanLin_mul_apply {m n o : Type*} [Fintype n] [Fintype o]
    87	    [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq o]
    88	    (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (B : Matrix n o ℂ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ o) :
    89	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin (A * B) v =
    90	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin A (Matrix.toEuclideanLin B v) := by
    91	  simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same]

    93	/-- The squared norm of `A v` is the quadratic form of `Aᴴ A` at `v`. -/
    94	theorem norm_toEuclideanLin_sq {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    95	    (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) :
    96	    ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v‖ ^ 2 =
    97	      (inner ℂ v (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Aᴴ * A) v)).re := by
    98	  rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ, Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
    99	  change (inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v) (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v)).re =
   100	    (inner ℂ v ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).adjoint (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v))).re
   101	  rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]

   103	/-- A rectangular matrix `A` with `Aᴴ A = 1` preserves norms. -/
   104	theorem norm_toEuclideanLin_of_conjTranspose_mul_eq_one {m n : Type*} [Fintype m]
   105	    [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℂ} (hA : Aᴴ * A = 1)
   106	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) :
   107	    ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin A v‖ = ‖v‖ := by
   108	  have h := norm_toEuclideanLin_sq A v
   109	  have hv : (inner ℂ v v).re = ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
   110	    simpa using inner_self_eq_norm_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) v
   111	  have hone : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) v = v := by
   112	    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin]
   113	  rw [hA, hone, hv] at h
   114	  exact (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).1 h

   116	/-- The squared norm of `K v` is the quadratic form of `Kᴴ K` at `v`. -/
   117	theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (K : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   119	    ‖applyOperatorToState K v‖ ^ 2 =
   120	      (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState (Kᴴ * K) v)).re :=
   121	  norm_toEuclideanLin_sq K v

   123	/-- An operator `K` with `Kᴴ K ≤ 1` does not increase norms. -/
   124	theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   125	    {K : Op ι} (hK : Kᴴ * K ≤ 1) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   126	    ‖applyOperatorToState K v‖ ≤ ‖v‖ := by
   127	  have h := quadratic_form_mono hK v
   128	  have hv : (inner ℂ v v).re = ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
   129	    simpa using inner_self_eq_norm_sq (𝕜 := ℂ) v
   130	  rw [← norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, applyOperatorToState_one, hv] at h
   131	  exact (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).1 h
   132	
   133	/-- The difference of two contractions at most doubles norms. -/
   134	theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   135	    {A B : Op ι} (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) (hB : Bᴴ * B ≤ 1) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   136	    ‖applyOperatorToState (A - B) v‖ ≤ 2 * ‖v‖ := by
   137	  have hsplit : applyOperatorToState (A - B) v =
   138	      applyOperatorToState A v - applyOperatorToState B v := by
   139	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   140	  rw [hsplit]
   141	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState A v - applyOperatorToState B v‖ ≤
   142	        ‖applyOperatorToState A v‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState B v‖ := norm_sub_le _ _
   143	    _ ≤ ‖v‖ + ‖v‖ := add_le_add (norm_applyOperatorToState_le hA v)
   144	        (norm_applyOperatorToState_le hB v)
   145	    _ = 2 * ‖v‖ := by ring

   147	/-- Orthogonal projections are contractions. -/
   148	theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   149	    {P : Op ι} (hP : IsProj P) : Pᴴ * P ≤ 1 := by
   150	  have hstar : Pᴴ = P := by
   151	    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]
   152	    exact hP.isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
   153	  rw [hstar, hP.isIdempotentElem.eq]
   154	  exact sub_nonneg.mp hP.one_sub.nonneg

   156	/-- Products of contractions are contractions. -/
   157	theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   158	    {A B : Op ι} (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) (hB : Bᴴ * B ≤ 1) :
   159	    (A * B)ᴴ * (A * B) ≤ 1 := by
   160	  have h1 : (1 - Aᴴ * A).PosSemidef := Matrix.le_iff.mp hA
   161	  have h2 := h1.conjTranspose_mul_mul_same B
   162	  have h3 : Bᴴ * (1 - Aᴴ * A) * B = Bᴴ * B - (A * B)ᴴ * (A * B) := by
   163	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
   164	    noncomm_ring
   165	  refine le_trans ?_ hB
   166	  rw [Matrix.le_iff, ← h3]
   167	  exact h2

   169	/-- Effects of a measurement are contractions. -/
   170	theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_effect {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
   171	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ι) (a : α) :
   172	    (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ 1 := by
   173	  rw [measurement_effect_hermitian]
   174	  exact le_trans (sq_le_self (M.pos a) (measurement_effect_le_one M a))
   175	    (measurement_effect_le_one M a)

   177	/-- The observable of a binary measurement is a contraction: writing
   178	`E = M_0`, the observable is `2E - 1` and `1 - (2E - 1)² = 4(E - E²) ≥ 0`. -/
   179	theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_obsOf {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   180	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (ZMod 2) ι) :
   181	    (obsOf M)ᴴ * obsOf M ≤ 1 := by
   182	  have hsum : M.effect 0 + M.effect 1 = 1 := by
   183	    have h : ∑ a : Fin 2, M.effect a = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   184	    rwa [Fin.sum_univ_two] at h
   185	  have hobs : obsOf M = M.effect 0 + M.effect 0 - 1 := by

   187	    rw [← hsum]
   188	    abel
   189	  have hH : (M.effect 0)ᴴ = M.effect 0 := measurement_effect_hermitian M 0

   191	    sub_nonneg.mpr (sq_le_self (M.pos 0) (measurement_effect_le_one M 0))
   192	  rw [hobs]
   193	  have hid : (M.effect 0 + M.effect 0 - 1)ᴴ * (M.effect 0 + M.effect 0 - 1) =

   195	    simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_add,
   196	      Matrix.conjTranspose_one, hH]
   197	    noncomm_ring
   198	  rw [hid]
   199	  exact sub_le_self _ (nsmul_nonneg hsq 4)

   279	/-- The matrix of an isometry is a matrix isometry. -/
   280	theorem isometryMatrix_conjTranspose_mul {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   281	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   282	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') :
   283	    (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ * isometryMatrix φ = 1 := by
   284	  apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   285	  have hM : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) = φ.toLinearMap :=
   286	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply φ.toLinearMap
   287	  calc
   288	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin ((isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ * isometryMatrix φ) =
   289	        (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ)).adjoint.comp
   290	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ)) :=
   291	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self _
   292	    _ = φ.toLinearMap.adjoint.comp φ.toLinearMap := by rw [hM]
   293	    _ = 1 := φ.adjoint_comp_self'
   294	    _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) := by
   295	      rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_one]
   296	      rfl

   298	/-- The range projection `V Vᴴ` of a matrix isometry is at most the identity. -/
   299	theorem isometryMatrix_mul_conjTranspose_le_one {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   300	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   301	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') :
   302	    isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ ≤ 1 := by
   303	  have hproj : IsProj (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) := by
   304	    constructor
   305	    · change (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) *
   306	        (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) = isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ
   307	      rw [Matrix.mul_assoc, ← Matrix.mul_assoc (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ,
   308	        isometryMatrix_conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   309	    · change star (isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) =
   310	        isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ
   311	      simp [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
   312	  exact sub_nonneg.mp hproj.one_sub.nonneg

   314	/-- Conjugation by an isometry preserves contractions. -/
   315	theorem conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   316	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   317	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') {A : Op ι} (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) :
   318	    (conjIsometry φ A)ᴴ * conjIsometry φ A ≤ 1 := by
   319	  rw [conjIsometry_eq]
   320	  have h1 : (isometryMatrix φ * A * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ)ᴴ *
   321	      (isometryMatrix φ * A * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ) =
   322	      isometryMatrix φ * (Aᴴ * A) * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := by
   323	    simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.conjTranspose_conjTranspose,
   324	      Matrix.mul_assoc]
   325	    rw [← Matrix.mul_assoc (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ (isometryMatrix φ),
   326	      isometryMatrix_conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   327	  rw [h1]
   328	  calc isometryMatrix φ * (Aᴴ * A) * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ ≤
   329	        isometryMatrix φ * (1 : Op ι) * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := by
   330	        rw [Matrix.le_iff]
   331	        have h := (Matrix.le_iff.mp hA).mul_mul_conjTranspose_same (isometryMatrix φ)
   332	        convert h using 1
   333	        simp [Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul]
   334	    _ = isometryMatrix φ * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := by rw [Matrix.mul_one]
   335	    _ ≤ 1 := isometryMatrix_mul_conjTranspose_le_one φ

   435	transfer step of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/

   443	    naimarkInflation (α := α) M * naimarkInflation (α := α) N =
   444	      naimarkInflation (α := α) (M * N) := by
   445	  ext p q
   446	  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, naimarkInflation_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type,
   447	    Fintype.sum_option]
   448	  by_cases hp : p.2 = none <;> by_cases hq : q.2 = none <;> simp [hp, hq]

   453	    (naimarkInflation (α := α) M)ᴴ = naimarkInflation (α := α) Mᴴ := by

   463	    rw [groundProjection, naimarkInflation_mul, Matrix.mul_one]
   464	  · change star (groundProjection ι α) = groundProjection ι α

   523	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   524	    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (1 - groundProjection ιA α) 1)
   525	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) = 0 := by
   526	  have h : heteroKron (1 - groundProjection ιA α) (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) =
   527	      1 - heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) 1 := by
   528	    rw [heteroKron_sub_left, heteroKron_one_one]
   529	  have hsub : applyOperatorToState (1 - heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) 1)
   530	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   531	      applyOperatorToState 1 (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) -
   532	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α) 1)
   533	          (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by
   534	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   535	  rw [h, hsub, applyOperatorToState_one, applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_groundProjection,
   536	    sub_self]

   539	side. -/
   540	theorem applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   541	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   542	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :

   544	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) = 0 := by

   546	      1 - heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α) := by

   548	  have hsub : applyOperatorToState (1 - heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α))
   549	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =

   552	          (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by

   554	  rw [h, hsub, applyOperatorToState_one, applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_groundProjection,
   555	    sub_self]

   557	/-! ## Leakage out of the ground slice is bounded by the intertwining defect -/
   558	
   559	/-- The leakage of a left-placed operator `P` out of the ground slice on the
   560	dilated state is at most the intertwining defect of `P ⊗ 1` against any
   561	right-placed operator `1 ⊗ Q`, because `(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.
   562	This is the estimate replacing the `≈_δ` preservation that Naimark dilation
   563	lacks (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`). -/
   564	theorem norm_leftTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   565	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   566	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
   567	    (P : Op (ιA × Option α)) (Q : Op (ιB × Option α)) :
   568	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * P) 1)
   569	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   570	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q)
   571	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   572	  set ψ' := naimarkDilatedState α ψ
   573	  set L : Op ((ιA × Option α) × (ιB × Option α)) :=
   574	    heteroKron (1 - groundProjection ιA α) 1
   575	  have hL0 : applyOperatorToState L ψ' = 0 :=
   576	    applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_one_sub_groundProjection α ψ
   577	  have hLcontr : Lᴴ * L ≤ 1 :=
   578	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor
   579	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection ιA α).one_sub)
   580	  have hsplit : heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * P)
   581	      (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) = L * heteroKron P 1 := by
   582	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   583	  have hcomm : L * heteroKron 1 Q = heteroKron 1 Q * L := by
   584	    rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul,
   585	      Matrix.mul_one]
   586	  have key : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * P) 1) ψ' =
   587	      applyOperatorToState L
   588	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q) ψ') := by
   589	    rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   590	    have hdec : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1) ψ' =
   591	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' +
   592	          applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' := by
   593	      simp [applyOperatorToState]
   594	    rw [hdec, applyOperatorToState_add, ← applyOperatorToState_mul L (heteroKron 1 Q), hcomm,
   595	      applyOperatorToState_mul, hL0, applyOperatorToState_zero, add_zero]
   596	  rw [key]
   597	  exact norm_applyOperatorToState_le hLcontr _
   598	
   599	/-- The leakage of a right-placed operator `Q` out of the ground slice on the
   600	dilated state is at most its intertwining defect against any left-placed
   601	operator. -/

   603	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]

   607	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   608	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q)
   609	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by

   611	  set L : Op ((ιA × Option α) × (ιB × Option α)) :=
   612	    heteroKron 1 (1 - groundProjection ιB α)
   613	  have hL0 : applyOperatorToState L ψ' = 0 :=
   614	    applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection α ψ
   615	  have hLcontr : Lᴴ * L ≤ 1 :=
   616	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_rightTensor
   617	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection ιB α).one_sub)
   618	  have hsplit : heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α))
   619	      ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * Q) = L * heteroKron 1 Q := by
   620	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul]
   621	  have hcomm : L * heteroKron P 1 = heteroKron P 1 * L := by
   622	    rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul,
   623	      Matrix.mul_one]
   624	  have key : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * Q)) ψ' =
   625	      applyOperatorToState L
   626	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ') := by
   627	    rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_mul]
   628	    have hdec : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' =
   629	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ' +
   630	          applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1) ψ' := by
   631	      simp [applyOperatorToState]
   632	    rw [hdec, applyOperatorToState_add, ← applyOperatorToState_mul L (heteroKron P 1), hcomm,
   633	      applyOperatorToState_mul, hL0, applyOperatorToState_zero, add_zero]
   634	  have hneg : -applyOperatorToState (heteroKron P 1 - heteroKron 1 Q) ψ' =
   635	      applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 Q - heteroKron P 1) ψ' := by

### Motivation

Discharge the external Magic Square self-testing boundary used by QPBT
soundness. The canonical project statement is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
matched by `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. The cited
external source is Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.

The cited external proof obtains this as a robust linear-constraint-system
self-test using its general solution-group/stability machinery. This repository
has no such general framework. Formalize only the finite-dimensional Magic
Square consequence needed here; do not introduce a project-wide LCS or
approximate-representation mechanism.

### Target

After the Magic Square foundation/split packet #75, prove only the existing
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_rigidity` in
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean`, preserving its complete public
signature verbatim:

- one universal `C : ℝ` with `1 ≤ C`, before `ε` and `S`;
- every `ε ≥ 0` and every `S : Strategy msGame` with `1 - ε ≤ S.value`;
- an `MsRigidityWitness S`;
- the Euclidean state bound;
- Alice and Bob measurement-distance bounds at zero-based variables 0/X and
  4/Z;
- both anticommutator-distance bounds;
- all seven bounds at scale `C * Real.sqrt ε`.

### Dependencies

- Base on merged #75.
- Base on #49 for the clean state-dependent distance/observable conversion and
  triangle API, especially `opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le`,
  `consistencyDefect_postprocess_le`, and `povm_to_obs` where applicable.
- Base on #64 for clean EPR normalization and the Pauli-projector/observable
  expansions used to identify `idealMagicBitProj`.
- Base on #68 for the binary Pauli involution and twisted-commutation laws.
- It is independent of the perfect-strategy packet, #69, the fixed-field-model
  work, and encoding/decoding. Once the split and these three dependencies
  land, rigidity and perfect strategy may run concurrently in disjoint files.

### Proof route

1. Expand the game value over the 36 directed constraint-variable incidences.
   Convert `1 - ε ≤ S.value` into rejection-mass bounds, then into the
   finitely many row/column consistency relations with explicit constants.
   Include bounds for wrong-form answers folded by `msBitOrZero`; they are not
   definitionally absent.
2. Reduce arbitrary finite POVMs to projective measurements without
   strengthening the theorem. Reuse or adapt the proved one-measurement and
   tensor-product Naimark machinery in
   `MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkFull.lean`, but prove the
   pure-vector/intertwining consequences actually needed here: value
   preservation, composition of the input-space embeddings with the eventual
   self-test isometries, and transfer of state-dependent effect bounds back to
   the original strategy.
3. For the dilated projective strategy, turn the six nearly satisfied parity
   constraints and same-cell agreement into approximate reflection relations.
   Isolate a proved, file-local projective Magic Square rigidity lemma;
   projectivity must be discharged by step 2, not exposed in
   `exists_ms_rigidity`.
4. Follow the finite Magic Square operator argument: extract approximate Pauli
   `X` and `Z` pairs for the two logical qubits, construct the local swap
   isometries, and obtain a normalized auxiliary vector. Keep all intermediate
   relation/error lemmas concrete and proved. Do not restate
   Coladangelo--Stark's general theorem as an axiom or assumed proposition.
5. Translate the cited theorem's ideal observables `I⊗Z` and `ZX⊗ZX` through
   the explicit local basis change to the project's `X⊗I` and `Z⊗I`. Use
   #64/#68 to identify the corresponding
   binary effects with `idealMagicBitProj`.
6. Convert the self-test's density/trace estimate to the exact Euclidean vector
   estimate. Account for the square-root loss explicitly; this is not a
   definitional `simpa`.
7. Derive the four `msOperatorDistanceA/B` bounds, then the two
   `msAnticommutatorDistanceA/B` bounds from binary observable expansion,
   multiplication stability, and the squared-distance triangle estimates from
   #49.
8. Track explicit constants throughout and take a finite maximum to obtain the
   single universal `C ≥ 1`. Handle the theorem's unrestricted `ε ≥ 0`: use
   the robust argument in its small-error range and a separately
   proved coarse large-error bound with canonical padded isometries. Do not
   silently assume `ε ≤ 1`.

Private implementation submodules under
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Rigidity/` are allowed when they keep
individual proofs reviewable. They remain owned by this one issue and must
bottom out in Lean/Mathlib and the already proved local APIs.

### Statement integrity

Paper assumptions: an arbitrary finite-dimensional strategy whose Magic Square
success is `1-ε`. Lean uses arbitrary finite local carriers, a unit pure state,
arbitrary POVMs, nonnegative `ε`, and a lower success bound; the
lower-bound form is the faithful monotone version of the source equality.
Paper conclusion: local isometries extracting two EPR pairs and an auxiliary
state, four binary measurement approximations, and Alice/Bob anticommutation,
all with universal `O(sqrt ε)` control. Lean records exactly these
through `MsRigidityWitness`, `idealMsState`, `msOperatorDistanceA/B`, and
`msAnticommutatorDistanceA/B`; indices 0 and 4 are the paper's variables 1 and
5. Verdict: faithful explicit-constant encoding.

The paper explains two translations at lines 650-652: trace norm to Euclidean
distance and a local basis change. Both are proof obligations. No additional
strategy-projectivity assumption, bridge package, residual input, or changed
error exponent is source-faithful.

### Ownership and non-goals

Own `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean` and, if needed, new private
rigidity-only submodules below
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Rigidity/`. Do not touch
`MagicSquare.lean`, `MagicSquareTheorems/Basic.lean`,
`MagicSquareTheorems/PerfectStrategy.lean`, Pauli/distance source files,

import MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.Distribution

/-!
# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value

This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
`Measurement` structure.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/--
A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
-/
structure Game where
  QuestionA : Type
  QuestionB : Type
  AnswerA : Type
  AnswerB : Type
  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool

attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq

/--
The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
  M.postprocess Prod.fst

/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
  M.postprocess Prod.snd

/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)

/--
The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
-/
structure Strategy (G : Game) where
  ιA : Type
  ιB : Type
  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB

attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq

/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
  Matrix.kronecker A B

/-! ### Algebra of the tensor placement

The shared tensor-placement API.  These identities are used both by the perfect
Magic Square strategy (`thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:257-267`) and by the rigidity transfer
step (`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`), so they live
with the definition rather than in either development. -/

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
(blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`): the tensor
placement is multiplicative, `(A ⊗ C) * (B ⊗ D) = (A * B) ⊗ (C * D)`. -/
theorem heteroKron_mul {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [Fintype ιB]
    (A B : Op ιA) (C D : Op ιB) :
    heteroKron A C * heteroKron B D = heteroKron (A * B) (C * D) := by
  unfold heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
  exact (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul A B C D).symm

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
(blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`): the tensor
placement of the two identity operators is the identity operator on the product
space. -/
theorem heteroKron_one_one {ιA ιB : Type*} [DecidableEq ιA] [DecidableEq ιB] :
    heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (1 : Op ιB) = 1 := by
  unfold heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
  exact Matrix.one_kronecker_one

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
(blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`): tensor placement
respects negation in the left factor. -/
theorem heteroKron_neg_left {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (C : Op ιB) :
    heteroKron (-A) C = -heteroKron A C := by
  ext p q
  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker]

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
(blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`): tensor placement
respects negation in the right factor. -/
theorem heteroKron_neg_right {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (C : Op ιB) :
    heteroKron A (-C) = -heteroKron A C := by
  ext p q
  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker]

/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ

/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-48`. -/
noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re

/-- Alice's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
noncomputable def aliceOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (a : G.AnswerA) : ℝ :=
  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1
  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re

/-- Bob's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
noncomputable def bobOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)
  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re

/-- The Born weight of a decidable event on the two answers at fixed questions. -/
noncomputable def outcomeEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] : ℝ :=
  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
    if E a b then outcomeWeight S x y a b else 0

/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Alice's answer. -/
noncomputable def aliceEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, if E a then aliceOutcomeWeight S x a else 0

/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Bob's answer. -/
noncomputable def bobEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (y : G.QuestionB) (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
  ∑ b : G.AnswerB, if E b then bobOutcomeWeight S y b else 0

/-- Every answer-pair Born weight is nonnegative.  This is formalization-only
support for the probability expression in `def:tensor-product-value`. -/
theorem outcomeWeight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) :
    0 ≤ outcomeWeight S x y a b := by
  unfold outcomeWeight applyOperatorToState heteroKron
  exact
    (Matrix.isPositive_toEuclideanLin_iff.mpr
      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
        (kronecker_nonneg ((S.A x).pos a) ((S.B y).pos b)))).re_inner_nonneg_right S.ψ

/-- The squared norm of `M ψ` is the quadratic form of `Mᴴ M`. -/
private theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ ^ 2 =
      (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (Mᴴ * M) ψ)).re := by
  rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
  unfold applyOperatorToState
  rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
  change (inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ) (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ)).re =
    (inner ℂ ψ ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ))).re
  rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Fact 4.20: evaluation in a fixed
vector preserves operator order. -/
theorem quadratic_form_mono {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {S T : Op ι} (hST : S ≤ T) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState S v)).re ≤
      (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState T v)).re := by
  have hpsd : (T - S).PosSemidef := Matrix.le_iff.mp hST
  have hnonneg := hpsd.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg v
  have hdiff : 0 ≤ (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState (T - S) v)).re := by
    simp only [applyOperatorToState, Matrix.toEuclideanLin,
      Matrix.toLpLin_apply, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
    rw [dotProduct_comm]
    exact (Complex.nonneg_iff.mp hnonneg).1
  rw [show T = S + (T - S) by abel]
  simp only [applyOperatorToState, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, inner_add_right,
    Complex.add_re]
  exact le_add_of_nonneg_right hdiff

/-- Applying a product of operators agrees with successive application. -/
private theorem applyOperatorToState_mul {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M N : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    applyOperatorToState (M * N) v =
      applyOperatorToState M (applyOperatorToState N v) := by
  unfold applyOperatorToState
  simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same]

/-- Finite-subset form of contraction by square-summable left multipliers. -/
private theorem finset_sum_norm_mul_apply_le {γ ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (s : Finset γ) (C : γ → Op ι) (D : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
    (hC : ∑ c ∈ s, (C c)ᴴ * C c ≤ 1) :
    ∑ c ∈ s, ‖applyOperatorToState (C c * D) v‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ‖applyOperatorToState D v‖ ^ 2 := by
  calc
    ∑ c ∈ s, ‖applyOperatorToState (C c * D) v‖ ^ 2 =
        ∑ c ∈ s,
          (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState D v)
            (applyOperatorToState ((C c)ᴴ * C c)
              (applyOperatorToState D v))).re := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro c _
          rw [applyOperatorToState_mul]
          exact norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq (C c) _
    _ = (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState D v)
          (applyOperatorToState (∑ c ∈ s, (C c)ᴴ * C c)
            (applyOperatorToState D v))).re := by
          simp [applyOperatorToState]
    _ ≤ (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState D v)
          (applyOperatorToState (1 : Op ι) (applyOperatorToState D v))).re :=
      quadratic_form_mono hC _
    _ = ‖applyOperatorToState D v‖ ^ 2 := by
      simpa [applyOperatorToState] using
        (norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq (1 : Op ι) (applyOperatorToState D v)).symm

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Fact 4.20: a square-summable family
of left multipliers contracts total squared norm. -/
theorem sum_norm_mul_apply_le {γ ι : Type*}
    [Fintype γ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (C : γ → Op ι) (D : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
    (hC : ∑ c : γ, (C c)ᴴ * C c ≤ 1) :
    ∑ c : γ, ‖applyOperatorToState (C c * D) v‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ‖applyOperatorToState D v‖ ^ 2 := by
  simpa using finset_sum_norm_mul_apply_le Finset.univ C D v (by simpa using hC)

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the function-indexed multiplication
estimate at paper lines 347--361: fiber-indexed left multiplication contracts
the associated squared-norm sum. -/
theorem sum_norm_mul_funIndexed_apply_le {α Γ ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype Γ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (eval : Γ → α) (S : Γ → Op ι) (D : α → Op ι)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hS : ∑ g : Γ, (S g)ᴴ * S g ≤ 1) :
    ∑ g : Γ, ‖applyOperatorToState (S g * D (eval g)) v‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (D a) v‖ ^ 2 := by
  classical
  rw [show (∑ g : Γ, ‖applyOperatorToState (S g * D (eval g)) v‖ ^ 2) =
      ∑ a : α, ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g => eval g = a),
        ‖applyOperatorToState (S g * D a) v‖ ^ 2 by
    calc
      _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g => eval g = a),
          ‖applyOperatorToState (S g * D (eval g)) v‖ ^ 2 :=
        (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ eval
          (fun g => ‖applyOperatorToState (S g * D (eval g)) v‖ ^ 2)).symm
      _ = _ := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro a _
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro g hg
        rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp hg).2]]
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro a _
  apply finset_sum_norm_mul_apply_le
  calc
    ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g => eval g = a), (S g)ᴴ * S g ≤
        ∑ g : Γ, (S g)ᴴ * S g := by
      exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
        (Finset.filter_subset _ _)
        (fun g _ _ => star_mul_self_nonneg (S g))
    _ ≤ 1 := hS

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the projective-sum estimate at paper
lines 364--380: distinct effects of a projective measurement are orthogonal. -/
theorem projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero {α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ι)
    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M)
    {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
    M.effect a * M.effect b = 0 := by
  classical
  cases isEmpty_or_nonempty ι with
  | inl hι =>
      letI := hι
      exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
  | inr hι =>
      letI := hι
      let H : FiniteHilbertSpace :=
        { carrier := ι
          instFintype := inferInstance
          instDecidableEq := inferInstance
          instNonempty := inferInstance }
      let P : ProjMeas α ι :=
        { toMeasurement := MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := H) M
          proj := fun a => (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq }
      simpa [P, H] using P.outcome_orthogonal a b hab

/-- Gram expansion for a finite sum with mutually orthogonal left projectors. -/
private theorem gram_finset_sum_projector_mul {α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι]
    (P D : α → Op ι) (hproj : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
    (horth : ∀ {a b}, a ≠ b → P a * P b = 0) (s : Finset α) :
    (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a)ᴴ * (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a) =
      ∑ a ∈ s, (D a)ᴴ * P a * D a := by
  classical
  let T : α → Op ι := fun a => P a * D a
  have hstar (a : α) : (P a)ᴴ = P a := by
    simpa [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose] using (hproj a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
  calc
    _ = (∑ a ∈ s, (T a)ᴴ) * (∑ b ∈ s, T b) := by
      simp only [T, Matrix.conjTranspose_sum]
    _ = ∑ a ∈ s, ∑ b ∈ s, (T a)ᴴ * T b := by
      rw [Matrix.sum_mul]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      rw [Matrix.mul_sum]
    _ = ∑ a ∈ s, (D a)ᴴ * P a * D a := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a ha
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a]
      · simp only [T, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hstar a]
        rw [mul_assoc (D a)ᴴ (P a) (P a * D a),
          ← mul_assoc (P a) (P a) (D a), (hproj a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
        exact (mul_assoc (D a)ᴴ (P a) (D a)).symm
      · intro b _ hba
        calc
          (T a)ᴴ * T b = (D a)ᴴ * (P a * P b) * D b := by
            simp [T, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hstar a, mul_assoc]
          _ = 0 := by rw [horth (Ne.symm hba)]; simp
      · exact fun h => (h ha).elim

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the projective-sum estimate at paper
lines 364--380: an orthogonal projective left sum is bounded by the full input
norm sum. -/
theorem norm_finset_sum_projector_mul_sq_le {α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (P D : α → Op ι) (hproj : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
    (horth : ∀ {a b}, a ≠ b → P a * P b = 0)
    (s : Finset α) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (D a) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
  classical
  have hgram :
      (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a)ᴴ * (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a) ≤
        ∑ a : α, (D a)ᴴ * D a := by
    rw [gram_finset_sum_projector_mul P D hproj horth s]
    calc
      ∑ a ∈ s, (D a)ᴴ * P a * D a ≤
          ∑ a ∈ s, (D a)ᴴ * D a := by
        refine Finset.sum_le_sum ?_
        intro a _
        simpa [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose] using
          (star_left_conjugate_le_conjugate (hproj a).le_one (D a))
      _ ≤ ∑ a : α, (D a)ᴴ * D a :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (by simp)
          (fun a _ _ => (Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (D a)).nonneg)
  rw [norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq]
  calc
    (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState
        ((∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a)ᴴ * (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a)) ψ)).re ≤
        (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (∑ a : α, (D a)ᴴ * D a) ψ)).re :=
      quadratic_form_mono hgram ψ
    _ = ∑ a : α,
          (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState ((D a)ᴴ * D a) ψ)).re := by
      simp [applyOperatorToState]
    _ = ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (D a) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      exact (norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq (D a) ψ).symm

/-- Formalization-only definition for the agreement facts (Facts 4.13 and 4.14):
the real quadratic form of an operator evaluated in a state vector. -/
noncomputable def stateQForm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (M : Op ι) : ℝ :=
  (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState M ψ)).re

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the agreement facts (Facts 4.13 and
4.14): the state quadratic form is additive in its operator. -/
theorem stateQForm_add {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (M N : Op ι) :
    stateQForm ψ (M + N) = stateQForm ψ M + stateQForm ψ N := by
  simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]

/-- The state quadratic form preserves operator subtraction. -/
private theorem stateQForm_sub {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (M N : Op ι) :
    stateQForm ψ (M - N) = stateQForm ψ M - stateQForm ψ N := by
  simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]

/-!
# Quantitative state and operator distances

The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
estimates to later proof stages.

## References

These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/--
Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/
noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2

/--
Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/
noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Distance
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistributionAux
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.State

/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness

The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-237`,
from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-288`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
      if a = b then 0 else
        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ

/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ

/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl

/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
      S.ψ ≤ δ
  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
      S.ψ ≤ δ

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.Support

import MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.Defs

/-!
# Tensor-placement and marginal identities

This module collects tensor-placement, marginal, and finite-fiber identities
used in data processing and the commutator estimate.

## References

- `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:397-461`
- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:381-445`
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
open MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective

/-- Formalization-only definition used in the proof of Fact 4.26: place a
complete measurement on the left tensor factor. -/
noncomputable def leftPlacedMeasurement {α ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (ιA × ιB) :=
  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    (fun a => heteroKron (M.effect a) 1)
    (fun a => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (M.pos a)
      (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg : 0 ≤ (1 : Op ιB)))
    (by
      change ∑ a : α, leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect a) = 1
      rw [leftTensor_finset_sum, M.sum_eq_one, leftTensor_one])

/-- Formalization-only definition used in the proof of Fact 4.26: place a
complete measurement on the right tensor factor. -/
noncomputable def rightPlacedMeasurement {α ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (ιA × ιB) :=
  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    (fun a => heteroKron 1 (M.effect a))
    (fun a => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
      (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg : 0 ≤ (1 : Op ιA)) (M.pos a))
    (by
      change ∑ a : α, rightTensor (ι₁ := ιA) (M.effect a) = 1
      rw [rightTensor_finset_sum, M.sum_eq_one, rightTensor_one])

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Fact 4.26: products of left and right
placements evaluate as a Kronecker product. -/
theorem placed_product_stateQForm_eq {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) :
    stateQForm ψ (heteroKron A 1 * heteroKron 1 B) =
      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron A B) := by
  congr 1
  exact leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor A B

/-- The (possibly unnormalized) rank-one state associated to a Euclidean vector. -/
private noncomputable def vectorQuantumState {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : QuantumState ι where
  density := pureDensity ψ.ofLp
  density_psd := by
    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    exact (Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star ψ.ofLp).smul
      (by positivity : 0 ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℂ))

/-- Evaluation in the rank-one vector state is the corresponding quadratic form. -/
private theorem vectorQuantumState_ev_eq_stateQForm {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (T : Op ι) :
    ev (vectorQuantumState ψ) T = stateQForm ψ T := by
  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 :=
    Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
  change (MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (pureDensity ψ.ofLp * T)).re =
    stateQForm ψ T
  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm]
  unfold pureDensity MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
  rw [Matrix.mul_smul, Matrix.mul_vecMulVec, Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_vecMulVec]
  change (((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
      ((T *ᵥ ψ.ofLp) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.ofLp)) /
      (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)).re = stateQForm ψ T
  rw [mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ hcard]
  unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState
  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
  simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply]

/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Fact 4.26: postprocessing can only
increase diagonal tensor overlap. -/
theorem diagonal_postprocess_stateQForm_ge {α β ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA)
    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιB) (f : α → β) :
    (∑ b : β, stateQForm ψ
        (heteroKron ((A.postprocess f).effect b) ((B.postprocess f).effect b))) ≥
      ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a)) := by
  classical
  cases isEmpty_or_nonempty (ιA × ιB) with
  | inl hι =>
      letI := hι
      have hψ : ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      subst ψ
      simp [stateQForm, applyOperatorToState]
  | inr hι =>
      letI := hι
      letI : Nonempty ιA := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).1⟩
      letI : Nonempty ιB := ⟨(Classical.choice hι).2⟩
      let HA : FiniteHilbertSpace :=
        { carrier := ιA
          instFintype := inferInstance
          instDecidableEq := inferInstance
          instNonempty := inferInstance }
      let HB : FiniteHilbertSpace :=
        { carrier := ιB
          instFintype := inferInstance
          instDecidableEq := inferInstance
          instNonempty := inferInstance }
      let As : SubMeas α ιA :=
        (MatrixMeasurement.toMeasurement (H := HA) A).toSubMeas

This aggregate module provides the QPBT algebraic, game-theoretic, and test
declarations.

## References

Blueprint chapters `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`, `ch12_qpbt_games.tex`, and
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
-/

/-!
# Basic Magic Square symmetry facts

This file proves symmetry of the Magic Square question distribution and
decision predicate, packages the game as a `SymmetricGame`, and defines the
observable associated with a binary measurement.

## References

The game is `def:ms-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, from
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- Symmetry of the Magic Square question distribution from `def:ms-game`;
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`. -/
theorem msQuestionDistribution_symm (x y : MsType) :
    msGame.μ.weight (x, y) = msGame.μ.weight (y, x) := by
  classical
  simp [msGame, graphDistribution, Sym2.eq_swap]

/-- Symmetry of the Magic Square decision predicate from `def:ms-game`;
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`. -/
theorem msWinPredicate_symm (x y : MsType) (a b : MsAnswer) :
    msWinPredicate x y a b = msWinPredicate y x b a := by
  cases x <;> cases y <;> cases a <;> cases b <;>
    simp [msWinPredicate, and_comm, eq_comm]

/-- The symmetric-game presentation of the Magic Square game. -/
noncomputable def msGameSymm : SymmetricGame where
  Question := MsType
  Answer := MsAnswer
  μ := msGame.μ
  μ_prob := msGame.μ_prob
  μ_symm := msQuestionDistribution_symm
  decide := msWinPredicate
  decide_symm := msWinPredicate_symm

/-- The symmetric presentation has the Magic Square game as its
underlying game. -/
theorem msGameSymm_toGame : msGameSymm.toGame = msGame := by
  rfl

/-- The observable associated with a binary measurement; formalization-only notation
used in `thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:257-267`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:658-722`. -/
def obsOf {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement (ZMod 2) ι) : Op ι :=
  M.effect 0 - M.effect 1

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
