   169	
   170	/-- The concrete expectation `τ(ρ X)` on the local matrix layer. -/
   171	noncomputable def matrixExpectation {H : FiniteHilbertSpace}
   172	    (ρ : PositiveMatrixState H) (X : MatrixOperator H) : ℂ :=
   173	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ.matrix * X)
   174	
   175	/-! ### One-measurement Naimark dilation (Lemma 5.2)
   176	
   177	The one-measurement Naimark dilation is the building block for the full
   178	theorem. Given a submeasurement `M` on space `d`, it produces a projective
   179	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α`, where `Option α`
   180	models the auxiliary register with one extra dimension `none = ⊥` for the
   181	missing mass `I − ∑ M_a`. -/
   182	
   183	/-- The auxiliary pure-state projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` on `Option α`, where `⊥ = none`.
   184	This is the initial state of the auxiliary register before the Naimark
   185	isometry is applied. -/
   186	def naimarkAuxProjector (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   187	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   188	  Matrix.single none none 1
   189	
   190	/-- The lifted density matrix for one-measurement Naimark dilation:
   191	`ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)`.
   192	The scaling by `|Option α|` ensures the normalized trace is preserved:
   193	`τ'(ρ_lifted) = τ(ρ)`, where `τ'` is the normalized trace on the enlarged space. -/
   194	noncomputable def oneMeasLiftedDensity {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   195	    (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   196	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) :
   197	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) :=
   198	  (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) • Matrix.kronecker ρ (naimarkAuxProjector α)
   199	
   200	/-- One-measurement Naimark dilation data at the matrix level.
   201	
   202	Given a submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, this witnesses the existence
   203	of a projective submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` that
   204	preserves all expectation values. This is Lemma 5.2 of the paper.
   205	
   206	The construction: let `V : H → H ⊗ ℂ^{|α|+1}` be the isometry
   207	`V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a |ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   208	Then `P̂_a = V† (I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|) V` is a projection, and
   209	`⟨ψ|M_a|ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ⊗⊥|P̂_a|ψ⊗⊥⟩`. -/
   210	structure OneMeasNaimarkData (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   211	    (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
   212	  /-- The source submeasurement being dilated. -/
   213	  source : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d
   214	  /-- The dilated projective effects on `d × Option α`.
   215	  For outcome `some a`, this is the Naimark projector `P̂_a`.
   216	  For outcome `none`, this is the projector for the "missing mass". -/
   217	  liftedEffect : Option α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α)
   218	  /-- Each lifted effect is a genuine orthogonal projection. Positivity follows
   219	  from `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/
   220	  lifted_isProj : ∀ a, MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj (liftedEffect a)
   221	  /-- The lifted projections sum to at most identity (which together with
   222	  `lifted_isProj` implies mutual orthogonality). -/
   223	  lifted_sum_le_one : ∑ a, liftedEffect a ≤ 1
   224	  /-- **Expectation preservation**: for any operator `ρ` on `Op d`,
   225	  the expectation of outcome `a` under the original submeasurement equals
   226	  the expectation under the dilated projective submeasurement with the
   227	  Naimark-lifted state. The identity is linear, so it holds for all operators,
   228	  not just density matrices. This is the core content of the dilation. -/
   229	  expectation_preservation : ∀ (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (a : α),
   230	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * source.effect a) =
   231	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   232	        (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ * liftedEffect (some a))
   233	
   234	/-- Positivity of a lifted Naimark effect, derived from its projectivity.
   235	
   236	Lean-only consequence of the one-measurement Naimark data: the paper records
   237	the lifted effects as projections, and positivity is supplied here by the
   238	Mathlib star-projection order theorem through `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/
   239	theorem OneMeasNaimarkData.lifted_pos {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   240	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   241	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (a : Option α) :
   242	    0 ≤ data.liftedEffect a :=
   243	  (data.lifted_isProj a).nonneg
   244	
   245	/-! ### Questionwise Naimark data
   246	
   247	The current Lean data applies one-measurement Naimark independently to each
   248	question on each side. -/
   249	
   250	/-- Questionwise Naimark data for the prospective full assembly.
   251	
   252	Given submeasurements on space `ι`, this carries the questionwise
   253	one-measurement Naimark dilations used as the local building blocks for the
   254	full tensor-product assembly. -/
   255	structure NaimarkData (QuestionA OutcomeA QuestionB OutcomeB : Type*)
   256	    (ι : Type*)
   257	    [Fintype QuestionA] [DecidableEq QuestionA]
   258	    [Fintype OutcomeA] [DecidableEq OutcomeA]
   259	    [Fintype QuestionB] [DecidableEq QuestionB]
   260	    [Fintype OutcomeB] [DecidableEq OutcomeB]
   261	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
   262	  /-- Alice's questionwise one-measurement Naimark dilations. -/
   263	  left : (x : QuestionA) → OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeA ι
   264	  /-- Bob's questionwise one-measurement Naimark dilations. -/
   265	  right : (y : QuestionB) → OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeB ι
   266	
   267	-- NOTE: no global `Inhabited` instance for `NaimarkData`:
   268	-- constructing defaults for projective measurements is mathematically non-canonical
   269	-- and would require additional assumptions on outcome types.
   270	
   271	/-! ### Error functions for orthonormalization -/
   272	
   273	/-- The explicit error in `thm:orthonormalization`. -/
   274	noncomputable def orthonormalizationError (ζ : Error) : Error :=
   275	  100 * Real.rpow ζ (1 / (4 : Error))
   276	
   277	/-- Error bound of the direct completion-route orthonormalization theorem.
   278	
   279	The paper proves the sharper `orthonormalizationError ζ`.  The direct completion
   280	route first converts the completed measurement's `2ζ` self-consistency estimate
   281	into a `4ζ` source-almost-projective estimate, and therefore uses this weaker
   282	named envelope. -/
   283	noncomputable def orthonormalizationCompletionRouteError (ζ : Error) : Error :=
   284	  120 * Real.rpow ζ (1 / (4 : Error))
   285	
   286	/-- The explicit error in the measurement version of the lemma. -/
   287	noncomputable def orthonormalizationMainLemmaError (ζ : Error) : Error :=
   288	  84 * Real.rpow ζ (1 / (4 : Error))
   289	
   290	/-- The almost-projective error extracted from a consistency hypothesis. -/
   291	def consistencyToAlmostProjectiveError (ζ : Error) : Error :=
   292	  2 * ζ
   293	
   294	/-- The spectral-truncation error when rounding one almost-projective effect to a
   295	    projection via eigenvalue truncation. Dominated by `√ζ`. -/
   296	noncomputable def spectralTruncationError (ζ : Error) : Error :=
   297	  Real.rpow ζ (1 / (2 : Error))
   298	
   299	/-- The rounding error when converting an almost-projective POVM to a projective submeasurement. -/
   300	noncomputable def roundingToProjectiveError (ζ : Error) : Error :=
   301	  12 * Real.rpow ζ (1 / (2 : Error))
   302	
   303	end MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective

     3	/-!
     4	# Section 5 — Naimark tensor-product assembly
     5	
     6	Questionwise one-measurement Naimark data, the two-sided trace identity, and
     7	the source-facing tensor-product Naimark theorem in the projective-submeasurement
     8	form supplied by the paper's helper lemma.
     9	-/
    10	
    11	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    12	
    13	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
    14	
    15	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    16	
    17	universe u
    18	
    19	private theorem idxSubMeas_outcome_sum_le_one
    20	    {Question Outcome ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    22	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) (x : Question) :
    23	    ∑ a, (A x).outcome a ≤ 1 := by
    24	  simpa [(A x).sum_eq_total] using (A x).total_le_one
    25	
    26	/-! ### Questionwise Naimark dilation interface -/
    27	
    28	/-- The one-measurement Naimark dilation attached to a single question.
    29	
    30	Paper origin: this is the questionwise application of
    31	`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`
    32	(`\label{lem:naimark-helper}`) used in the proof of
    33	`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:36-80`
    34	(`\label{thm:naimark}`), specifically the tensor-product assembly at
    35	`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:161-187`. -/
    36	noncomputable def questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData
    37	    {Question Outcome ι : Type*}
    38	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    39	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    40	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) (x : Question) :
    41	    OneMeasNaimarkData Outcome ι :=
    42	  Classical.choose <| oneMeasNaimark ({
    43	    effect := (A x).outcome
    44	    pos := (A x).outcome_pos
    45	    sum_le_one := idxSubMeas_outcome_sum_le_one A x
    46	  } : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement Outcome ι)
    47	
    48	/-- The questionwise Naimark data is attached to the intended source
    49	submeasurement. -/
    50	theorem questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData_source_effect
    51	    {Question Outcome ι : Type*}
    52	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    53	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    54	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) (x : Question) :
    55	    (questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData A x).source.effect = (A x).outcome := by
    56	  simpa [questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData] using
    57	    congrArg MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement.effect <|
    58	      Classical.choose_spec <| oneMeasNaimark ({
    59	        effect := (A x).outcome
    60	        pos := (A x).outcome_pos
    61	        sum_le_one := idxSubMeas_outcome_sum_le_one A x
    62	      } : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement Outcome ι)
    63	
    64	/-- Lean-only questionwise Naimark interface.
    65	
    66	This theorem proves `NaimarkStatement`, the restricted interface consisting of
    67	per-question local dilations and single-outcome marginal preservation.  It is
    68	not the full tensor-product preservation statement of `thm:naimark`. -/
    69	theorem questionwiseNaimark {QuestionA OutcomeA QuestionB OutcomeB : Type*}
    70	    {ι : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype QuestionA] [DecidableEq QuestionA]
    72	    [Fintype OutcomeA] [DecidableEq OutcomeA]
    73	    [Fintype QuestionB] [DecidableEq QuestionB]
    74	    [Fintype OutcomeB] [DecidableEq OutcomeB]
    75	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    76	    (ψ : QuantumState ι)
    77	    (A : IdxSubMeas QuestionA OutcomeA ι)
    78	    (B : IdxSubMeas QuestionB OutcomeB ι) :
    79	    ∃ data : NaimarkData QuestionA OutcomeA QuestionB OutcomeB ι,
    80	      NaimarkStatement ψ A B data := by
    81	  classical
    82	  let leftData : (x : QuestionA) → OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeA ι :=
    83	    questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData A
    84	  let rightData : (y : QuestionB) → OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeB ι :=
    85	    questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData B
    86	  have hleft : ∀ x : QuestionA, (leftData x).source.effect = (A x).outcome := by
    87	    intro x
    88	    simpa [leftData] using questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData_source_effect A x
    89	  have hright : ∀ y : QuestionB, (rightData y).source.effect = (B y).outcome := by
    90	    intro y
    91	    simpa [rightData] using questionwiseOneMeasNaimarkData_source_effect B y
    92	  refine ⟨{ left := leftData, right := rightData }, ?_⟩
    93	  refine ⟨hleft, hright, ?_, ?_⟩
    94	  · intro x ρ a
    95	    simpa [leftData, hleft x] using (leftData x).expectation_preservation ρ a
    96	  · intro y ρ b
    97	    simpa [rightData, hright y] using (rightData y).expectation_preservation ρ b
    98	
    99	/-! ### Full tensor-product Naimark interface -/
   100	
   101	/-- The single auxiliary Hilbert space used by the full Naimark assembly on one side.
   102	
   103	The one-measurement theorem produces projectors on `H × Option Outcome`.  Since
   104	all questions on one side have the same outcome type, the different question
   105	measurements may be represented on the same auxiliary space, with a different
   106	Naimark unitary for each question. -/
   107	def oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace (Outcome : Type u)
   108	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome] :
   109	    FiniteHilbertSpace.{u} where
   110	  carrier := Option Outcome
   111	  instFintype := inferInstance
   112	  instDecidableEq := inferInstance
   113	  instNonempty := ⟨none⟩
   114	
   115	/-- The distinguished auxiliary basis state `|⊥⟩` for the one-register Naimark
   116	assembly. -/
   117	noncomputable def oneNaimarkAuxPureState (Outcome : Type u)
   118	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome] :
   119	    PureState (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace Outcome).carrier :=
   120	  PureState.basis (none : Option Outcome)
   121	
   122	/-- The normalized auxiliary density state `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|`. -/
   123	noncomputable def oneNaimarkAuxState (Outcome : Type u)
   124	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome] :
   125	    QuantumState (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace Outcome).carrier :=
   126	  oneNaimarkAuxPureState Outcome
   127	
   128	/-- The one-register auxiliary state is normalized. -/

   180	/-- The two-sided trace identity for the full tensor-product Naimark assembly.

   188	theorem OneMeasNaimarkData.twoSidedCorrelationPreservation
   189	    {OutcomeA OutcomeB : Type u}
   190	    [Fintype OutcomeA] [DecidableEq OutcomeA]
   191	    [Fintype OutcomeB] [DecidableEq OutcomeB]
   192	    (HA HB : FiniteHilbertSpace.{u})
   193	    (ψ : QuantumState (HA.carrier × HB.carrier))
   194	    (leftData : OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeA HA.carrier)
   195	    (rightData : OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeB HB.carrier)
   196	    (a : OutcomeA) (b : OutcomeB) :
   197	    ev ψ (opTensor (leftData.source.effect a) (rightData.source.effect b)) =
   198	      ev
   199	        (naimarkProductExtensionState HA HB
   200	          (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeA)
   201	          (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeB)
   202	          ψ
   203	          (QuantumState.tensor
   204	            (oneNaimarkAuxState OutcomeA)
   205	            (oneNaimarkAuxState OutcomeB)))
   206	        (opTensor
   207	          ((leftData.toProjSubMeas).outcome a)
   208	          ((rightData.toProjSubMeas).outcome b)) := by
   209	  classical
   210	  have hleft_comp :
   211	      ∀ i j : HA.carrier,
   212	        leftData.liftedEffect (some a) (i, none) (j, none) =
   213	          leftData.source.effect a i j :=
   214	    OneMeasNaimarkData.compression_none_none leftData a
   215	  have hright_comp :
   216	      ∀ i j : HB.carrier,
   217	        rightData.liftedEffect (some b) (i, none) (j, none) =
   218	          rightData.source.effect b i j :=
   219	    OneMeasNaimarkData.compression_none_none rightData b

   221	  congr 1
   222	  unfold MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   223	  simp [naimarkProductExtensionState, naimarkProductExtensionDensity,
   224	    QuantumState.tensor, oneNaimarkAuxState, oneNaimarkAuxPureState,
   225	    PureState.density, pureDensity, PureState.basis, Matrix.mul_apply,
   226	    Matrix.trace, opTensor, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.vecMulVec]
   227	  simp [Fintype.sum_prod_type, OneMeasNaimarkData.toProjSubMeas,
   228	    mul_assoc, mul_left_comm, mul_comm]
   229	  field_simp
   230	  let cA : ℂ := Fintype.card (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeA).carrier
   231	  let cB : ℂ := Fintype.card (oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeB).carrier
   232	  let S : ℂ :=
   233	    ∑ x : HA.carrier,
   234	      ∑ x_1 : HB.carrier,
   235	        ∑ x_2 : HA.carrier,
   236	          ∑ x_3 : HB.carrier,
   237	            ψ.density (x, x_1) (x_2, x_3) *
   238	              leftData.source.effect a x_2 x *
   239	              rightData.source.effect b x_3 x_1

   242	      ∑ x_1 : HB.carrier,
   243	        ∑ x_2 : HA.carrier,
   244	          ∑ x_3 : HB.carrier,

   246	              leftData.liftedEffect (some a) (x_2, none) (x, none) *
   247	              rightData.liftedEffect (some b) (x_3, none) (x_1, none)

   249	      (∑ x : HA.carrier,
   250	        ∑ x_1 : HB.carrier,
   251	          ∑ x_2 : HA.carrier,
   252	            ∑ x_3 : HB.carrier,
   253	              cA * cB * ψ.density (x, x_1) (x_2, x_3) *
   254	                leftData.liftedEffect (some a) (x_2, none) (x, none) *
   255	                rightData.liftedEffect (some b) (x_3, none) (x_1, none)) =
   256	        cA * cB * S by
   257	      calc
   258	        (∑ x : HA.carrier,
   259	          ∑ x_1 : HB.carrier,
   260	            ∑ x_2 : HA.carrier,
   261	              ∑ x_3 : HB.carrier,
   262	                cA * cB * ψ.density (x, x_1) (x_2, x_3) *
   263	                  leftData.liftedEffect (some a) (x_2, none) (x, none) *
   264	                  rightData.liftedEffect (some b) (x_3, none) (x_1, none))
   265	            = ∑ x : HA.carrier,
   266	              ∑ x_1 : HB.carrier,
   267	                ∑ x_2 : HA.carrier,
   268	                  ∑ x_3 : HB.carrier,
   269	                    cA * cB *
   270	                      (ψ.density (x, x_1) (x_2, x_3) *
   271	                        leftData.source.effect a x_2 x *
   272	                        rightData.source.effect b x_3 x_1) := by
   273	              refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   274	              intro x _
   275	              refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   276	              intro x_1 _
   277	              refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   278	              intro x_2 _
   279	              refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   280	              intro x_3 _
   281	              rw [hleft_comp x_2 x, hright_comp x_3 x_1]
   282	              ring
   283	        _ = cA * cB * S := by
   284	              simp [S, mul_assoc, Finset.mul_sum]]
   285	  ring_nf

   287	/-- Full tensor-product Naimark correlation theorem.
   288	
   289	This is the Lean statement corresponding to
   290	`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:36-80`
   291	(`\label{thm:naimark}`).  It is proved from the checked one-measurement
   292	Naimark construction and the two-sided trace identity
   293	`OneMeasNaimarkData.twoSidedCorrelationPreservation`. -/
   294	theorem naimarkTensorProductCorrelation
   295	    {QuestionA OutcomeA QuestionB OutcomeB : Type u}
   296	    [Fintype QuestionA] [DecidableEq QuestionA]
   297	    [Fintype OutcomeA] [DecidableEq OutcomeA]
   298	    [Fintype QuestionB] [DecidableEq QuestionB]
   299	    [Fintype OutcomeB] [DecidableEq OutcomeB]
   300	    (HA HB : FiniteHilbertSpace.{u})
   301	    (ψ : QuantumState (HA.carrier × HB.carrier))
   302	    (A : IdxSubMeas QuestionA OutcomeA HA.carrier)
   303	    (B : IdxSubMeas QuestionB OutcomeB HB.carrier) :
   304	    NaimarkTensorProductCorrelationStatement HA HB ψ A B := by
   305	  classical
   306	  intro hψ
   307	  let HauxA : FiniteHilbertSpace.{u} := oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeA
   308	  let HauxB : FiniteHilbertSpace.{u} := oneNaimarkAuxHilbertSpace OutcomeB
   309	  let auxLeft : QuantumState HauxA.carrier := oneNaimarkAuxState OutcomeA
   310	  let auxRight : QuantumState HauxB.carrier := oneNaimarkAuxState OutcomeB
   311	  let auxState : QuantumState (HauxA.carrier × HauxB.carrier) :=
   312	    QuantumState.tensor auxLeft auxRight
   313	  let leftData : (x : QuestionA) → OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeA HA.carrier :=
   314	    fun x => Classical.choose <| oneMeasNaimark ({
   315	      effect := (A x).outcome
   316	      pos := (A x).outcome_pos
   317	      sum_le_one := idxSubMeas_outcome_sum_le_one A x
   318	    } : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement OutcomeA HA.carrier)
   319	  let rightData : (y : QuestionB) → OneMeasNaimarkData OutcomeB HB.carrier :=
   320	    fun y => Classical.choose <| oneMeasNaimark ({
   321	      effect := (B y).outcome
   322	      pos := (B y).outcome_pos
   323	      sum_le_one := idxSubMeas_outcome_sum_le_one B y
   324	    } : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement OutcomeB HB.carrier)
   325	  have hleft : ∀ x : QuestionA, (leftData x).source.effect = (A x).outcome := by
   326	    intro x
   327	    simpa [leftData] using congrArg MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement.effect <|
   328	      Classical.choose_spec <| oneMeasNaimark ({
   329	        effect := (A x).outcome
   330	        pos := (A x).outcome_pos
   331	        sum_le_one := idxSubMeas_outcome_sum_le_one A x
   332	      } : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement OutcomeA HA.carrier)
   333	  have hright : ∀ y : QuestionB, (rightData y).source.effect = (B y).outcome := by
   334	    intro y
   335	    simpa [rightData] using congrArg MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement.effect <|
   336	      Classical.choose_spec <| oneMeasNaimark ({
   337	        effect := (B y).outcome
   338	        pos := (B y).outcome_pos
   339	        sum_le_one := idxSubMeas_outcome_sum_le_one B y
   340	      } : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement OutcomeB HB.carrier)
   341	  have hauxLeft : auxLeft.IsNormalized := by
   342	    simpa [auxLeft, HauxA] using oneNaimarkAuxState_isNormalized OutcomeA
   343	  have hauxRight : auxRight.IsNormalized := by
   344	    simpa [auxRight, HauxB] using oneNaimarkAuxState_isNormalized OutcomeB
   345	  have hauxState : auxState.IsNormalized := by
   346	    exact QuantumState.tensor_isNormalized hauxLeft hauxRight
   347	  refine ⟨HauxA, HauxB, ⟨?_⟩⟩
   348	  exact {
   349	    auxState := auxState
   350	    auxState_normalized := hauxState
   351	    auxLeft := auxLeft
   352	    auxRight := auxRight
   353	    auxLeft_normalized := hauxLeft
   354	    auxRight_normalized := hauxRight
   355	    auxState_product := rfl
   356	    dilatedState := naimarkProductExtensionState HA HB HauxA HauxB ψ auxState

   358	    dilatedState_normalized :=
   359	      naimarkProductExtensionState_isNormalized HA HB HauxA HauxB hψ hauxState
   360	    left := fun x => (leftData x).toProjSubMeas

1	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

     4	/-!
     5	# A simultaneous projective dilation of a Magic Square strategy
     6	
     7	The rigidity argument for the Magic Square game is stated for an arbitrary
     8	tensor-product strategy, whose measurements are positive operator valued
     9	measures.  The self-testing argument, however, manipulates projections.  This
    10	file removes that discrepancy by dilating an arbitrary strategy to a projective
    11	one without changing any observable quantity.
    12	
    13	Each local Hilbert space `ℂ^ι` is enlarged by one auxiliary register whose
    14	basis is indexed by `Option MsAnswer`, and the original space is identified with
    15	the *ground slice* `ℂ^ι ⊗ |⊥⟩`.  The one-measurement Naimark lemma of the low
    16	individual degree development supplies, for every question separately, a family
    17	of projections on the enlarged space whose compression to the ground slice
    18	returns the original effects; the ancilla is the same for all questions, so the
    19	identification of `ℂ^ι` with the ground slice is a single isometry serving every
    20	question at once.  Folding the deficiency `1 - ∑_a P_a` into one distinguished
    21	answer turns the dilated family into a complete projective measurement without
    22	disturbing the compression, because the original effects already sum to the
    23	identity.
    24	
    25	Since the dilated state is the image of the original state under the two ground
    26	embeddings, every Born probability, and hence the game value and all the
    27	rejection, malformed-answer, cell-consistency and parity masses of the
    28	value-to-parity layer, is unchanged.  Conversely, the local isometries produced
    29	by a rigidity argument applied to the dilated strategy compose with the ground
    30	embeddings to give local isometries of the original strategy, and the
    31	state-dependent norms occurring in the conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` transfer
    32	along that composition.
    33	
    34	## References
    35	
    36	The rigidity statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
    37	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
    39	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.  The dilation reuses the
    40	one-measurement Naimark lemma of
    41	`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`, formalized as
    42	`MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.oneMeasNaimark`.
    43	-/

    54	/-! ## Orthogonality inside a subnormalized family of projections -/
    55	
    56	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
    57	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  If an orthogonal projection `P` and a
    58	positive semidefinite operator `Q` satisfy `P + Q ≤ 1`, then `P` annihilates
    59	`Q`.  Indeed `Tr(P Q)` is nonnegative because both operators are positive
    60	semidefinite, while `0 ≤ Tr(P (1 - P - Q)) = -Tr(P Q)` because `1 - P - Q` is
    61	positive semidefinite and `P` is idempotent; so the pairing vanishes and the
    62	product of two positive semidefinite operators with vanishing trace pairing is
    63	zero. -/
    64	theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    65	    {P Q : Op d} (hP : IsProj P) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hPQ : P + Q ≤ 1) :
    66	    P * Q = 0 := by
    67	  have hrest : (0 : Op d) ≤ 1 - (P + Q) := sub_nonneg.mpr hPQ
    68	  have hexpand : P * (1 - (P + Q)) = -(P * Q) := by
    69	    have hPP : P * P = P := hP.isIdempotentElem
    70	    rw [Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_add, hPP, Matrix.mul_one]
    71	    abel
    72	  have hle : Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) ≤ 0 := by
    73	    have h := trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hrest
    74	    rw [hexpand] at h
    75	    simpa using h
    76	  have hge : 0 ≤ Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) :=
    77	    trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hQ
    78	  exact mul_eq_zero_of_nonneg_of_trace_mul_eq_zero hP.nonneg hQ (le_antisymm hle hge)
    79	
    80	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
    81	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  A finite family of orthogonal
    82	projections whose sum is at most the identity is mutually orthogonal: for two
    83	distinct indices the two projections already sum to at most the identity, so the
    84	previous lemma applies. -/
    85	theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    86	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
    87	    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
    88	    P a * P b = 0 := by
    89	  refine mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one (hP a) (hP b).nonneg ?_
    90	  refine le_trans ?_ hsum
    91	  have hpair : ∑ c ∈ ({a, b} : Finset α), P c = P a + P b := by
    92	    rw [Finset.sum_pair hab]
    93	  rw [← hpair]
    94	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
    95	    (fun c _ _ => (hP c).nonneg)
    96	
    97	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
    98	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  The sum of a mutually orthogonal
    99	family of projections is again an orthogonal projection; mutual orthogonality is
   100	supplied by the hypothesis that the sum is at most the identity. -/

   225	/-! ## The dilated projective measurement -/
   226	
   227	/-- A one-measurement Naimark dilation of a positive operator valued measure,
   228	chosen once and for all.  It provides orthogonal projections on the enlarged
   229	space `ℂ^{d × Option α}` whose ground-slice compressions are the given effects;
   230	see `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`. -/
   231	noncomputable def naimarkData {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   232	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) : OneMeasNaimarkData α d :=
   233	  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
   234	
   235	/-- The chosen dilation dilates the intended measurement. -/
   236	theorem naimarkData_source {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   237	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   238	    (naimarkData M).source = M.toSubmeasurement :=
   239	  Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
   240	
   241	/-- The dilated projections indexed by genuine answers already sum to at most the
   242	identity, since the projection attached to the adjoined point is positive
   243	semidefinite. -/
   244	theorem naimarkData_sum_some_le_one {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   245	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   246	    ∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) ≤ 1 := by
   247	  have hsplit : ∑ oa : Option α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect oa =
   248	      (naimarkData M).liftedEffect none +
   249	        ∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) :=
   250	    Fintype.sum_option (f := fun oa => (naimarkData M).liftedEffect oa)
   251	  have hle := (naimarkData M).lifted_sum_le_one
   252	  rw [hsplit] at hle
   253	  have hnone : (0 : Op (d × Option α)) ≤ (naimarkData M).liftedEffect none :=
   254	    (naimarkData M).lifted_pos none
   255	  exact le_trans (le_add_of_nonneg_left hnone) hle

   257	/-- The sum of the dilated projections indexed by genuine answers is itself an
   258	orthogonal projection. -/
   259	theorem naimarkData_isProj_sum_some {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   260	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   261	    IsProj (∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a)) :=
   262	  isProj_sum_of_isProj_of_sum_le_one
   263	    (fun a => (naimarkData M).lifted_isProj (some a))
   264	    (naimarkData_sum_some_le_one M)
   265	
   266	/-- The effects of the dilated measurement.  The projection attached to the
   267	answer `a` is the Naimark projection of `a`, except that the distinguished answer
   268	`a₀` also absorbs the deficiency `1 - ∑_a P_a`, which makes the family complete.
   269	Formalization-only construction supporting `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   270	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   271	noncomputable def naimarkDilatedEffect {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   272	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (a₀ a : α) :
   273	    Op (d × Option α) :=
   274	  (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) +
   275	    (if a = a₀ then 1 - ∑ b : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some b) else 0)
   276	
   277	/-- The dilated effects are positive semidefinite. -/
   278	theorem naimarkDilatedEffect_pos {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   279	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (a₀ a : α) :
   280	    0 ≤ naimarkDilatedEffect M a₀ a := by
   281	  unfold naimarkDilatedEffect
   282	  refine add_nonneg ((naimarkData M).lifted_pos (some a)) ?_
   283	  by_cases h : a = a₀
   284	  · simpa [h] using sub_nonneg.mpr (naimarkData_sum_some_le_one M)
   285	  · simp [h]

   287	/-- The dilated effects sum to the identity. -/
   288	theorem naimarkDilatedEffect_sum {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   289	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (a₀ : α) :
   290	    ∑ a : α, naimarkDilatedEffect M a₀ a = 1 := by
   291	  unfold naimarkDilatedEffect
   292	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_ite_eq' Finset.univ a₀]
   293	  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, if_pos]
   294	  abel

   305	    · simpa using (naimarkData_isProj_sum_some M).one_sub

   369	/-- The image of a bipartite state under the two ground embeddings.  This is the

   378	/-- The coordinates of the dilated state: the original amplitudes sit on the

   392	    · simp [hob]

    60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game

    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.
    93	
    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   130	\end{proof}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}

   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer. 
   175	
   176	\begin{definition}
   177	  \label{def:spcc}
   178	  We say that a strategy $\strategy$ for a game $\game$ is \emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\game$.
   179	  Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.
   180	\end{definition}

   183	Recall that for a (pure) state $\ket{\psi}\in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$, the \emph{Schmidt rank} of $\ket{\psi}$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that 
   184	\[ \ket{\psi} = \sum_{i=1}^k\, \alpha_i \ket{u_i}\otimes \ket{v_i}\;,\]
   185	for some orthonormal families $\{\ket{u_i}\}\subset \mH_\alice$ and $\{\ket{v_i}\}\subset\mH_\bob$ and $\alpha_i>0$. The coefficients $\alpha_i$ are uniquely defined by $\ket{\psi}$ and called \emph{Schmidt coefficients}. The state $\ket{\psi}$ is called \emph{maximally entangled} if $\alpha_i=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots,k$.

     3	/-!
     4	# Transfer of rigidity bounds along the projective dilation
     5	
     6	The self-testing argument behind `thm:ms-rigidity` is carried out for the
     7	projective dilation `msDilatedStrategy S` of an arbitrary Magic Square strategy
     8	`S`.  Its conclusions are state-dependent bounds for the *dilated* projectors,
     9	conjugated by local isometries `φ_A`, `φ_B` out of the enlarged local spaces.
    10	The witness for the original strategy is obtained by composing these isometries
    11	with the ground embeddings, and the operators appearing in its bounds are the
    12	conjugates of the *original* effects, that is, of the compressions `Π P Π` of
    13	the dilated projectors `P` to the ground slice (`Π` the ground projection).
    14	
    15	Naimark dilation preserves Born probabilities but not state-dependent `≈_δ`
    16	estimates in general (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`,
    17	blueprint `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`), so `Π P Π` and `P` need not act
    18	alike on the dilated state.  Their difference on the dilated state `ψ'` is the
    19	*leakage* `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of `P` out of the ground slice, and the point of this
    20	file is that in the Magic Square game this leakage is controlled by the
    21	cell-consistency defect of the value-to-parity layer: the dilated effect
    22	`P ⊗ 1` almost agrees with the partner effect `1 ⊗ Q` on the other side, and
    23	`(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.  Combined with the closeness of
    24	`(φ_A ⊗ φ_B) ψ'` to the ideal state and the fact that all operators involved
    25	are contractions, this pulls every bound of `thm:ms-rigidity` back from the
    26	dilated strategy to the original one with explicit constants.
    27	
    28	## Main statements
    29	
    30	* `ms_effect_transfer_A`, `ms_effect_transfer_B`: the bit-measurement distances
    31	  of the original strategy are bounded by three times those of the dilated
    32	  strategy plus `216 ε + 24 η²`, where `η` bounds the state closeness.
    33	* `ms_anticommutator_transfer_A`, `ms_anticommutator_transfer_B`: the
    34	  anticommutator defects transfer with the bound `3 · (dilated) + 15552 ε +
    35	  48 η²`.
    36	* `ms_state_transfer`: the state closeness is unchanged.
    37	
    38	## References
    39	
    40	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
    41	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
    42	-/

   692	`Y ψ'`, which commutes past `(1 - Π) A`. -/

   701	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * B) 1)
   702	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   703	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * A) 1)
   704	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   705	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron B 1 - heteroKron 1 Y) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by

   707	    (isProj_groundProjection ιA α).isIdempotentElem.eq

   715	      applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α * B) 1)

   718	        (groundProjection ιA α * B * groundProjection ιA α) =
   719	        groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α * B * groundProjection ιA α := by

   721	      rw [← Matrix.mul_assoc (groundProjection ιA α) (groundProjection ιA α) (B * _), hGG]

    59	/-- The leakage of Bob's dilated observable out of the ground slice is bounded
    60	by the two forward intertwining defects of its effects. -/
    61	theorem norm_leak_obs_le_B (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    62	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) *
    63	        dilatedObsB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero))
    64	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ≤
    65	      ‖applyOperatorToState
    66	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 0) 1 -
    67	          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0))
    68	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ +
    69	      ‖applyOperatorToState
    70	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 1) 1 -
    71	          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1))

    82	/-- The intertwining defect of Alice's dilated constraint observable against
    83	Bob's dilated variable observable is bounded by the two forward defects. -/
    84	theorem norm_intertwine_obs_le_B (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    85	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (dilatedObsAf S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k)) 1 -
    86	        heteroKron 1 (dilatedObsB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero))
    87	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ≤
    88	      ‖applyOperatorToState
    89	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 0) 1 -
    90	          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0))
    91	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ +
    92	      ‖applyOperatorToState
    93	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 1) 1 -
    94	          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1))
    95	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ := by
    96	  have hsplit : heteroKron (dilatedObsAf S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k)) (1 : Op _) -
    97	      heteroKron 1 (dilatedObsB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero) =
    98	      (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 0) 1 -
    99	        heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0)) -
   100	      (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 1) 1 -
   101	        heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1)) := by
   102	    change heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 0 -
   103	      dilatedEffectA S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) 1) (1 : Op _) -
   104	      heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 0 -
   105	        dilatedEffectB S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero 1) = _
   106	    rw [heteroKron_sub_left, heteroKron_sub_right]
   107	    abel
   108	  rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_sub_op]
   109	  exact norm_sub_le _ _

   111	/-- Right-placed counterpart of `norm_leftTensor_compressed_product_sub_le`. -/
   112	theorem norm_rightTensor_compressed_product_sub_le (α : Type) [Fintype α]
   113	    [DecidableEq α] {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   114	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
   115	    (A B : Op (ιB × Option α)) (Y : Op (ιA × Option α))
   116	    (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) (hY : Yᴴ * Y ≤ 1) :
   117	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α *
   118	        (groundProjection ιB α * B * groundProjection ιB α) - A * B))
   119	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   120	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B))
   121	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   122	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A))
   123	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   124	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron Y 1 - heteroKron 1 B) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   125	  have hGG : groundProjection ιB α * groundProjection ιB α = groundProjection ιB α :=
   126	    (isProj_groundProjection ιB α).isIdempotentElem.eq
   127	  have hGc : (groundProjection ιB α)ᴴ * groundProjection ιB α ≤ 1 :=
   128	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection ιB α)
   129	  have h1Gc : (1 - groundProjection ιB α)ᴴ * (1 - groundProjection ιB α) ≤ 1 :=
   130	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection ιB α).one_sub
   131	  have hstep1 : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A *
   132	      groundProjection ιB α * (groundProjection ιB α * B * groundProjection ιB α)))
   133	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   134	      applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α * B))
   135	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by
   136	    have hassoc : groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α *
   137	        (groundProjection ιB α * B * groundProjection ιB α) =
   138	        groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α * B * groundProjection ιB α := by
   139	      simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   140	      rw [← Matrix.mul_assoc (groundProjection ιB α) (groundProjection ιB α) (B * _), hGG]
   141	    rw [hassoc, show heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α)) (groundProjection ιB α * A *
   142	        groundProjection ιB α * B * groundProjection ιB α) =
   143	        heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α * B) *
   144	          heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α) by rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.mul_one],
   145	      applyOperatorToState_mul, applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_groundProjection]
   146	  have hdec : groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α * B - A * B =
   147	      -(groundProjection ιB α * A * ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B)) -
   148	        ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) * B := by
   149	    noncomm_ring
   150	  have hfirst : ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A *
   151	      ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B))) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   152	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B))
   153	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   154	    rw [show heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α)) (groundProjection ιB α * A *
   155	        ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B)) =
   156	        heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A) * heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B)
   157	        by rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.mul_one], applyOperatorToState_mul]
   158	    exact norm_applyOperatorToState_le
   159	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_rightTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hGc hA)) _
   160	  have hsecond : ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) * B))
   161	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   162	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron Y 1 - heteroKron 1 B) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   163	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A))
   164	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   165	    have hL : (heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α)) ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A))ᴴ *
   166	        heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) ≤ 1 :=
   167	      conjTranspose_mul_le_one_rightTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul h1Gc hA)
   168	    have hYc : (heteroKron Y (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)))ᴴ * heteroKron Y 1 ≤ 1 :=
   169	      conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor hY
   170	    have hcomm : heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α)) ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) *
   171	        heteroKron Y 1 = heteroKron Y 1 * heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) := by
   172	      rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul,
   173	        Matrix.mul_one]
   174	    rw [show heteroKron (1 : Op (ιA × Option α)) (((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) * B) =
   175	        heteroKron 1 ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) * heteroKron 1 B
   176	        by rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.mul_one], applyOperatorToState_mul]
   177	    have hdecB : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 B) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   178	        applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 B - heteroKron Y 1) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) +
   179	          applyOperatorToState (heteroKron Y 1) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by
   180	      rw [applyOperatorToState_sub_op, sub_add_cancel]
   181	    rw [hdecB, applyOperatorToState_add, ← applyOperatorToState_mul _ (heteroKron Y 1), hcomm,
   182	      applyOperatorToState_mul, norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_comm (heteroKron Y 1)]
   183	    refine le_trans (norm_add_le _ _) (add_le_add ?_ ?_)
   184	    · exact norm_applyOperatorToState_le hL _
   185	    · exact norm_applyOperatorToState_le hYc _
   186	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α *
   187	          (groundProjection ιB α * B * groundProjection ιB α) - A * B))
   188	          (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ =
   189	        ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A * groundProjection ιB α *
   190	          B - A * B)) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   191	        rw [heteroKron_sub_right, heteroKron_sub_right, applyOperatorToState_sub_op,
   192	          applyOperatorToState_sub_op, hstep1]
   193	    _ = ‖-applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A *
   194	          ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B))) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) -
   195	          applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) * B))
   196	            (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   197	        rw [hdec, heteroKron_sub_right, heteroKron_neg_right, applyOperatorToState_sub_op,
   198	          applyOperatorToState_neg_op]
   199	    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection ιB α * A *
   200	          ((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * B))) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   201	          ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (((1 - groundProjection ιB α) * A) * B))
   202	            (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   203	        refine le_trans (norm_sub_le _ _) ?_
   204	        rw [norm_neg]
   205	    _ ≤ _ := by linarith [hfirst, hsecond]

   207	/-- Right-placed counterpart of `norm_product_transfer_le_A`. -/
   208	theorem norm_product_transfer_le_B {κA κB : Type} [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA]
   209	    [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB] (S : Strategy msGame)
   210	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   211	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιB × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   212	    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB)) (A B : Op (S.ιB × Option MsAnswer))
   213	    (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) (hB : Bᴴ * B ≤ 1) :
   214	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   215	        (heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A *
   216	            groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) *
   217	          heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B *
   218	            groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) -
   219	          heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB A) * heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB B)) ξ‖ ≤
   220	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A *
   221	          groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B *
   222	            groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) - A * B)) (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ +
   223	      2 * ‖isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) - ξ‖ := by
   224	  have hGc : (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)ᴴ * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer ≤ 1 :=
   225	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)
   226	  have hGA := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hGc hA) hGc
   227	  have hGB := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hGc hB) hGc
   228	  have hprod : heteroKron (1 : Op κA) (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A *
   229	      groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) *
   230	      heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B *
   231	        groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) -
   232	      heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB A) * heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB B) =
   233	      heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A *
   234	        groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B *
   235	          groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) - A * B)) := by
   236	    rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, Matrix.mul_one, conjIsometry_mul, conjIsometry_mul,
   237	      conjIsometry_sub, heteroKron_sub_right]
   238	  rw [hprod]
   239	  have hT : (heteroKron (1 : Op κA) (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A *
   240	      groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B *

   243	        groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B *
   244	          groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer))) - heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (A * B)) := by
   245	    rw [conjIsometry_sub, heteroKron_sub_right]
   246	  have h1 : (heteroKron (1 : Op κA) (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A *
   247	      groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B *

   252	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_rightTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry φB
   253	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hGA hGB))

   256	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_rightTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry φB
   257	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hA hB))
   258	  have hswap : applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB
   259	      (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
   260	        (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) - A * B))) ξ =

   262	        (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
   263	          (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * B * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer) - A * B)))
   264	        (isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)) -

   266	        (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * A * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *

   268	        (isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) - ξ) := by
   269	    rw [applyOperatorToState_sub, sub_sub_cancel]

   271	  refine le_trans (norm_sub_le _ _) (add_le_add ?_ ?_)
   272	  · rw [applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_conjIsometry, norm_isometryTensor]

   276	/-- Transfer of Bob's anticommutator estimate of `thm:ms-rigidity` from the
   277	dilated strategy to the original one; see `ms_anticommutator_transfer_A`.
   278	The left-hand side is `msAnticommutatorDistanceB S w` for the witness whose
   279	isometry is the composite of the dilation embedding and `φ_B`. -/
   280	theorem ms_anticommutator_transfer_B {κA κB : Type} [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA]
   281	    [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB] (S : Strategy msGame)
   282	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   283	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιB × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   284	    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB)) (ε η : ℝ)
   285	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   286	    (hξ : ‖isometryTensor φA φB (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ - ξ‖ ≤ η) :
   287	    opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   288	        (fun _ => heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry (φB.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιB MsAnswer))
   289	            (obsOf ((S.B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) *
   290	          heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry (φB.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιB MsAnswer))
   291	            (obsOf ((S.B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))))
   292	        (fun _ => -(heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry (φB.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιB MsAnswer))
   293	            (obsOf ((S.B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) *
   294	          heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry (φB.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιB MsAnswer))
   295	            (obsOf ((S.B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))))) ξ ≤
   296	      3 * opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   297	        (fun _ => heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB
   298	            (obsOf (((msDilatedStrategy S).B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) *
   299	          heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB
   300	            (obsOf (((msDilatedStrategy S).B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))))
   301	        (fun _ => -(heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB
   302	            (obsOf (((msDilatedStrategy S).B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) *
   303	          heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB
   304	            (obsOf (((msDilatedStrategy S).B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))))) ξ +
   305	      15552 * ε + 48 * η ^ 2 := by
   306	  obtain ⟨i0, k0, h0⟩ := every_variable_is_incident 0
   307	  obtain ⟨i4, k4, h4⟩ := every_variable_is_incident 4
   308	  have hξ' : ‖isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) - ξ‖ ≤ η := hξ
   309	  rw [opDistSq_uniform_unit, opDistSq_uniform_unit, conjIsometry_comp_naimarkEmbedding,
   310	    conjIsometry_comp_naimarkEmbedding, naimarkInflation_obs_B, naimarkInflation_obs_B]
   311	  change ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
   312	      dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) *
   313	      heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
   314	        dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) -
   315	      -(heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
   316	        dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) *
   317	      heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
   318	        dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)))) ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   319	    3 * ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero)) *
   320	      heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero)) -
   321	      -(heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero)) *
   322	      heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero)))) ξ‖ ^ 2 +
   323	    15552 * ε + 48 * η ^ 2
   324	  have hXc := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero
   325	  have hZc := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero
   326	  have hYXc := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedObsAf S (.constraint i0) (constraintBitOrZero k0)
   327	  have hYZc := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedObsAf S (.constraint i4) (constraintBitOrZero k4)
   328	  have hleakX := norm_leak_obs_le_B S i0 k0
   329	  have hintX := norm_intertwine_obs_le_B S i0 k0
   330	  have hleakZ := norm_leak_obs_le_B S i4 k4
   331	  have hintZ := norm_intertwine_obs_le_B S i4 k4
   332	  have hsqX := sq_add_le_of_sum_sq_le _ _ ε (sum_norm_sq_intertwining_le_forward S i0 k0)
   333	    (forward_cell_mismatch_mass_le S ε hwin i0 k0)
   334	  have hsqZ := sq_add_le_of_sum_sq_le _ _ ε (sum_norm_sq_intertwining_le_forward S i4 k4)
   335	    (forward_cell_mismatch_mass_le S ε hwin i4 k4)
   336	  rw [h0] at hleakX hintX hsqX
   337	  rw [h4] at hleakZ hintZ hsqZ
   338	  have hXZ := norm_product_transfer_le_B S φA φB ξ (dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero)
   339	    (dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero) hXc hZc
   340	  have hZX := norm_product_transfer_le_B S φA φB ξ (dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero)
   341	    (dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero) hZc hXc
   342	  have hdXZ := norm_rightTensor_compressed_product_sub_le MsAnswer S.ψ
   343	    (dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero) (dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero)
   344	    (dilatedObsAf S (.constraint i4) (constraintBitOrZero k4)) hXc hYZc
   345	  have hdZX := norm_rightTensor_compressed_product_sub_le MsAnswer S.ψ
   346	    (dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero) (dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero)
   347	    (dilatedObsAf S (.constraint i0) (constraintBitOrZero k0)) hZc hYXc
   348	  have hsplit : ∀ (Xo Zo Xd Zd : Op (κA × κB)),
   349	      applyOperatorToState (Xo * Zo - -(Zo * Xo)) ξ =
   350	        applyOperatorToState (Xd * Zd - -(Zd * Xd)) ξ +
   351	          applyOperatorToState (Xo * Zo - Xd * Zd) ξ +
   352	          applyOperatorToState (Zo * Xo - Zd * Xd) ξ := by
   353	    intro Xo Zo Xd Zd
   354	    rw [← applyOperatorToState_add_op, ← applyOperatorToState_add_op]
   355	    congr 1
   356	    abel
   357	  rw [hsplit _ _ (heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedObsB S (.var 0) msBitOrZero)))
   358	    (heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedObsB S (.var 4) msBitOrZero)))]
   359	  refine anticommutator_arith (norm_nonneg _) ?_ hsqX hsqZ
   360	  refine le_trans (norm_add_le _ _) (le_trans (add_le_add_left (norm_add_le _ _) _) ?_)

     4	/-!
     5	# Magic Square value-to-parity relations
     6	
     7	This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
     8	the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
     9	total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
    10	supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
    11	incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
    12	of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
    13	six row or column constraints.
    14	
    15	The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
    16	answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
    17	`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The Magic Square game is defined in
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`
    23	and `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:201-222`.  These relations are the
    24	probabilistic input to the rigidity result cited at paper lines 612-652 from
    25	Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    29	
    30	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

    36	/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/
    37	
    38	/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
    39	def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → MsType × MsType
    40	  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k))
    41	  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)
    42	
    43	/-- Every question pair in the Magic Square distribution is a directed incidence. -/
    44	theorem ms_support_subset_directed_incidences :
    45	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support ⊆
    46	      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image directedIncidence := by
    47	  intro xy hxy
    48	  have hedge : Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges :=
    49	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
    50	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨ik, _hik, heq⟩
    51	  have heq' :
    52	      ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) = xy ∨
    53	        ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) =
    54	          xy.swap :=
    55	    (Sym2.mk_eq_mk_iff (α := MsType)).mp heq
    56	  rcases heq' with heq' | heq'
    57	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, false), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    58	    simpa [directedIncidence] using heq'
    59	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, true), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    60	    simpa [directedIncidence] using congrArg Prod.swap heq'
    61	
    62	/-- The Magic Square question distribution has at most 36 support points. -/
    63	theorem ms_support_card_le :
    64	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤ 36 := by
    65	  calc
    66	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤
    67	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image
    68	          directedIncidence).card :=
    69	      Finset.card_le_card ms_support_subset_directed_incidences
    70	    _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).card :=
    71	      Finset.card_image_le
    72	    _ = 36 := by norm_num
    73	
    74	/-- A constraint-to-variable incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    75	theorem ms_forward_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    76	    (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∈
    77	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    78	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    79	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    80	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    81	
    82	/-- A variable-to-constraint incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    83	theorem ms_reverse_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    84	    (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i) ∈
    85	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    86	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    87	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    88	  rw [Sym2.eq_swap]
    89	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    90	
    91	/-- Every supported question pair has probability at least `1 / 36`. -/
    92	theorem ms_question_weight_ge {xy : MsType × MsType}
    93	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
    94	    (1 : ℝ) / 36 ≤ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy := by
    95	  have hmemFilter :
    96	      xy ∈ ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
    97	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges) := hxy
    98	  rw [show (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy =
    99	      1 / ((graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card : ℝ) by
   100	    change (Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   101	        ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   102	          Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges)).weight xy =
   103	      1 / (((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   104	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges).card : ℝ)
   105	    rw [Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight, if_pos hmemFilter]]
   106	  apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le
   107	  · exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨xy, hxy⟩
   108	  · exact_mod_cast ms_support_card_le
