     4	/-!
     5	# Magic Square value-to-parity relations
     6	
     7	This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
     8	the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
     9	total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
    10	supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
    11	incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
    12	of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
    13	six row or column constraints.
    14	
    15	The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
    16	answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
    17	`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The Magic Square game is defined in
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`
    23	and `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:201-222`.  These relations are the
    24	probabilistic input to the rigidity result cited at paper lines 612-652 from
    25	Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    29	
    30	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    33	
    34	noncomputable section
    35	
    36	/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/
    37	
    38	/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
    39	def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → MsType × MsType
    40	  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k))
    41	  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)
    42	
    43	/-- Every question pair in the Magic Square distribution is a directed incidence. -/
    44	theorem ms_support_subset_directed_incidences :
    45	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support ⊆
    46	      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image directedIncidence := by
    47	  intro xy hxy
    48	  have hedge : Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges :=
    49	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
    50	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨ik, _hik, heq⟩
    51	  have heq' :
    52	      ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) = xy ∨
    53	        ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) =
    54	          xy.swap :=
    55	    (Sym2.mk_eq_mk_iff (α := MsType)).mp heq
    56	  rcases heq' with heq' | heq'
    57	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, false), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    58	    simpa [directedIncidence] using heq'
    59	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, true), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    60	    simpa [directedIncidence] using congrArg Prod.swap heq'
    61	
    62	/-- The Magic Square question distribution has at most 36 support points. -/
    63	theorem ms_support_card_le :
    64	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤ 36 := by
    65	  calc
    66	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤
    67	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image
    68	          directedIncidence).card :=
    69	      Finset.card_le_card ms_support_subset_directed_incidences
    70	    _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).card :=
    71	      Finset.card_image_le
    72	    _ = 36 := by norm_num
    73	
    74	/-- A constraint-to-variable incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    75	theorem ms_forward_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    76	    (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∈
    77	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    78	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    79	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    80	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    81	
    82	/-- A variable-to-constraint incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    83	theorem ms_reverse_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    84	    (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i) ∈
    85	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    86	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    87	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    88	  rw [Sym2.eq_swap]
    89	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    90	
    91	/-- Every supported question pair has probability at least `1 / 36`. -/
    92	theorem ms_question_weight_ge {xy : MsType × MsType}
    93	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
    94	    (1 : ℝ) / 36 ≤ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy := by

   112	/-- The rejection mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   113	noncomputable def rejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   114	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false
   115	
   116	/-- The acceptance mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   117	noncomputable def acceptanceMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   118	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = true
   119	
   120	/-- The rejection mass averaged over the Magic Square question distribution. -/
   121	noncomputable def totalRejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) : ℝ :=
   122	  avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   123	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2
   124	
   125	/-- Acceptance and rejection partition the conditioned answer mass. -/
   126	theorem acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
   127	    acceptanceMass S x y + rejectionMass S x y = 1 := by
   128	  rw [← show (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = 1 by
   129	    exact outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one S x y]
   130	  unfold acceptanceMass rejectionMass outcomeEventWeight
   131	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   132	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   133	  intro a _
   134	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   135	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   136	  intro b _
   137	  cases h : msWinPredicate x y a b <;> simp [h]

   139	/-- The strategy value is the average conditioned acceptance mass. -/

   141	    S.value = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   142	      acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2 := by
   143	  rfl

   188	/-- A supported conditioned rejection mass is at most 36 times total rejection. -/
   189	theorem rejection_mass_le_thirty_six_mul_total (S : Strategy msGame)

   192	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤ 36 * totalRejectionMass S := by
   193	  have hrejection : 0 ≤ rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 :=

   195	  have hweight := ms_question_weight_ge hxy
   196	  have hterm :

   201	      (fun z _ => mul_nonneg

   207	    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hweight hrejection

   211	theorem rejection_mass_le (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)

   213	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :

   216	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤ 36 * totalRejectionMass S :=
   217	      rejection_mass_le_thirty_six_mul_total S hxy

    79	These two results serve largely the same purpose,
    80	and for our applications it will typically suffice to use either one.
    81	That said, there are tradeoffs when choosing to use one or the other.
    82	Naimark dilation is convenient because it can be applied to any family of sub-measurements
    83	and it preserves measurement outcome probabilities exactly.
    84	On the other hand, it requires swapping out the state $\ket{\psi}$ and measurements~$A$ and~$B$
    85	for $\ket{\widehat{\psi}}$ and $\widehat{A}$ and $\widehat{B}$, respectively,
    86	which can be notationally cumbersome.
    87	Most works opt to skip adding the hats,
    88	and instead say something to the effect of ``using Naimark, we can assume that~$A$ and~$B$ are projective."
    89	However, there is subtlety in doing so,
    90	which is that Naimark dilation does not necessarily preserve ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements;
    91	in other words, $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$
    92	does not necessarily imply $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$.
    93	(As an example, \Cref{ex:easy-but-long} below
    94	provides a case in which $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{0} I \ot B^x_a$,
    95	but $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$ only holds for $\delta \geq 1$.)
    96	This can lead to trouble if the same notation is used for~$A, B$ and $\widehat{A}, \widehat{B}$,
    97	as ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements derived before applying Naimark might not necessarily hold after applying Naimark.
    98	(That said, as pointed out at the end of Section~$4.4$ of~\cite{NW19},
    99	``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements are often derived as a consequence of ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements.
   100	And as Naimark preserves ``$\simeq_{\delta}$" statements,
   101	one could use them to simply rederive any ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements post-Naimark.)
   102	
   103	The downsides of using the orthogonalization lemma
   104	are that it can only be applied to measurements which are strongly self-consistent

   106	As we will see below, its proof is significantly more complicated than Naimark dilation.
   107	On the plus side, it has none of the notational baggage that Naimark brings,
   108	and so it is more concrete to use.
   109	In addition, it can lead to stronger results,
   110	as it does not require introducing an auxiliary state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$.

   112	In this work, we will opt to use the orthogonalization lemma rather than Naimark dilation.
   113	However, we will include proofs of both for completeness.

   140	U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})

   142	\end{equation*}

   157	\end{align*}

   167	private theorem gram_finset_sum_projector_mul {α ι : Type*}
   168	    [Fintype ι]
   169	    (P D : α → Op ι) (hproj : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
   170	    (horth : ∀ {a b}, a ≠ b → P a * P b = 0) (s : Finset α) :
   171	    (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a)ᴴ * (∑ a ∈ s, P a * D a) =
   172	      ∑ a ∈ s, (D a)ᴴ * P a * D a := by
   173	  classical
   174	  let T : α → Op ι := fun a => P a * D a
   175	  have hstar (a : α) : (P a)ᴴ = P a := by
   176	    simpa [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose] using (hproj a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
   177	  calc
   178	    _ = (∑ a ∈ s, (T a)ᴴ) * (∑ b ∈ s, T b) := by
   179	      simp only [T, Matrix.conjTranspose_sum]
   180	    _ = ∑ a ∈ s, ∑ b ∈ s, (T a)ᴴ * T b := by
   181	      rw [Matrix.sum_mul]
   182	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   183	      intro a _
   184	      rw [Matrix.mul_sum]
   185	    _ = ∑ a ∈ s, (D a)ᴴ * P a * D a := by
   186	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   187	      intro a ha
   188	      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a]
   189	      · simp only [T, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hstar a]
   190	        rw [mul_assoc (D a)ᴴ (P a) (P a * D a),
   191	          ← mul_assoc (P a) (P a) (D a), (hproj a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   192	        exact (mul_assoc (D a)ᴴ (P a) (D a)).symm
   193	      · intro b _ hba
   194	        calc
   195	          (T a)ᴴ * T b = (D a)ᴴ * (P a * P b) * D b := by
   196	            simp [T, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hstar a, mul_assoc]
   197	          _ = 0 := by rw [horth (Ne.symm hba)]; simp
   198	      · exact fun h => (h ha).elim

   406	        stateQForm ψ (A.effect a) + stateQForm ψ (B.effect a) -
   407	          2 * stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a) := by
   408	    rw [norm_effect_sub_effect_sq_expand A B ψ a]
   409	    have hA := quadratic_form_mono
   410	      (MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (A.pos a) (measurement_effect_le_one A a)) ψ
   411	    have hB := quadratic_form_mono
   412	      (MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (B.pos a) (measurement_effect_le_one B a)) ψ
   413	    exact sub_le_sub_right (add_le_add hA hB) _
   414	  calc
   415	    _ ≤ ∑ a : α, (stateQForm ψ (A.effect a) + stateQForm ψ (B.effect a) -
   416	          2 * stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a)) :=
   417	      Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => hterm a
   418	    _ = (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a)) +
   419	          (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (B.effect a)) -
   420	          2 * (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a)) := by
   421	      rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
   422	    _ = 2 * (‖ψ‖ ^ 2 -
   423	          ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a)) := by
   424	      rw [stateQForm_effect_sum A ψ, stateQForm_effect_sum B ψ]
   425	      ring
   426	    _ = _ := by rw [point_defect_eq A B ψ]
   427	
   428	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the agreement facts (Facts 4.13 and
   429	4.14), item 2: projective measurements make distance exactly twice the
   430	pointwise defect. -/
   431	theorem point_distance_eq_two_defect_of_projective {α ι : Type*}
   432	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   433	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ι)
   434	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
   435	    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
   436	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
   437	    (∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (A.effect a - B.effect a) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
   438	      2 * (∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
   439	        if a = b then 0 else stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect b)) := by
   440	  calc
   441	    _ = ∑ a : α, (stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * A.effect a) +
   442	          stateQForm ψ (B.effect a * B.effect a) -
   443	          2 * stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a)) := by
   444	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   445	      intro a _
   446	      exact norm_effect_sub_effect_sq_expand A B ψ a
   447	    _ = ∑ a : α, (stateQForm ψ (A.effect a) + stateQForm ψ (B.effect a) -
   448	          2 * stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a)) := by
   449	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   450	      intro a _
   451	      rw [(hA a).isIdempotentElem.eq, (hB a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   452	    _ = (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a)) +
   453	          (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (B.effect a)) -
   454	          2 * (∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a)) := by
   455	      rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
   456	    _ = 2 * (‖ψ‖ ^ 2 -
   457	          ∑ a : α, stateQForm ψ (A.effect a * B.effect a)) := by
   458	      rw [stateQForm_effect_sum A ψ, stateQForm_effect_sum B ψ]
   459	      ring
   460	    _ = _ := by rw [point_defect_eq A B ψ]

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs

     3	/-!
     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    23	
    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    38	-/
    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45	
    46	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   321	/-- Per-outcome transfer estimate on Alice's side.  For any target operator `T`,
   322	the distance of the conjugated original effect from `T` on the target state
   323	`ξ` is at most the distance of the conjugated dilated effect from `T`, plus the
   324	intertwining defect of the dilated effect against Bob's partner effect `Q` on
   325	the dilated state, plus twice the distance from `ξ` to the transported dilated
   326	state.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   327	theorem norm_effect_transfer_term_le_A {κA κB : Type} [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA]
   328	    [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB] (S : Strategy msGame)
   329	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   330	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιB × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   331	    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB)) (T : Op (κA × κB)) (x y : MsType)
   332	    (f g : MsAnswer → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2) :
   333	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (conjIsometry (φA.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιA MsAnswer))
   334	        (((S.A x).postprocess f).effect b)) 1 - T) ξ‖ ≤
   335	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 - T) ξ‖ +
   336	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   337	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S x f b) 1 - heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S y g b))
   338	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ +
   339	      2 * ‖isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) - ξ‖ := by
   340	  rw [conjIsometry_comp_naimarkEmbedding, naimarkInflation_postprocess_A]
   341	  have hP := conjTranspose_mul_le_one_dilatedEffectA S x f b
   342	  have hG : (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)ᴴ * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer ≤ 1 :=
   343	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)
   344	  have hAd : (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) (1 : Op κB))ᴴ *
   345	      heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 ≤ 1 :=
   346	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry φA hP)
   347	  have hAo : (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer *
   348	      dilatedEffectA S x f b * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) (1 : Op κB))ᴴ *
   349	      heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer *
   350	        dilatedEffectA S x f b * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) 1 ≤ 1 :=
   351	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry φA
   352	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hG hP) hG))
   353	  set Ao : Op (κA × κB) := heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer *
   354	    dilatedEffectA S x f b * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) 1 with hAo_def
   355	  set Ad : Op (κA × κB) := heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 with hAd_def
   356	  set ψ'' := isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) with hψ''
   357	  have h1 : applyOperatorToState (Ao - T) ξ =
   358	      applyOperatorToState (Ad - T) ξ - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ := by
   359	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   360	  have h2 : applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ =
   361	      applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ψ'' - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) (ψ'' - ξ) := by
   362	    rw [applyOperatorToState_sub, sub_sub_cancel]
   363	  have h3 : ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ψ''‖ ≤
   364	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   365	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S x f b) 1 - heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S y g b))
   366	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ := by
   367	    have hdiff : Ad - Ao = heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b -
   368	        groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer * dilatedEffectA S x f b *
   369	          groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)) 1 := by
   370	      rw [hAd_def, hAo_def, conjIsometry_sub, heteroKron_sub_left]
   371	    rw [hdiff, hψ'', applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_conjIsometry, norm_isometryTensor,
   372	      applyOperatorToState_leftTensor_sub_compression]
   373	    exact norm_leftTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _
   374	  have h4 : ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) (ψ'' - ξ)‖ ≤ 2 * ‖ψ'' - ξ‖ :=
   375	    norm_applyOperatorToState_sub_le hAd hAo _
   376	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (Ao - T) ξ‖ =
   377	        ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - T) ξ - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ‖ := by rw [h1]
   378	    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - T) ξ‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ‖ :=
   379	        norm_sub_le _ _
   380	    _ ≤ _ := by
   381	        rw [h2]
   382	        linarith [norm_sub_le (applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ψ'')
   383	          (applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) (ψ'' - ξ)), h3, h4]

   411	      (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_mul hG hQ) hG))
   412	  set Bo : Op (κA × κB) := heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer *
   413	    dilatedEffectB S y g b * groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) with hBo_def
   414	  set Bd : Op (κA × κB) := heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedEffectB S y g b)) with hBd_def
   415	  set ψ'' := isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) with hψ''
   416	  have h1 : applyOperatorToState (Bo - T) ξ =
   417	      applyOperatorToState (Bd - T) ξ - applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) ξ := by
   418	    simp [applyOperatorToState]

   420	      applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) ψ'' - applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) (ψ'' - ξ) := by
   421	    rw [applyOperatorToState_sub, sub_sub_cancel]
   422	  have h3 : ‖applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) ψ''‖ ≤
   423	      ‖applyOperatorToState
   424	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S x f b) 1 - heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S y g b))
   425	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ := by
   426	    have hdiff : Bd - Bo = heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB (dilatedEffectB S y g b -
   427	        groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer * dilatedEffectB S y g b *
   428	          groundProjection S.ιB MsAnswer)) := by
   429	      rw [hBd_def, hBo_def, conjIsometry_sub, heteroKron_sub_right]
   430	    rw [hdiff, hψ'', applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_conjIsometry, norm_isometryTensor,
   431	      applyOperatorToState_rightTensor_sub_compression]
   432	    exact norm_rightTensor_one_sub_groundProjection_mul_le MsAnswer S.ψ _ _

   436	        ‖applyOperatorToState (Bd - T) ξ - applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) ξ‖ := by rw [h1]
   437	    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (Bd - T) ξ‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState (Bd - Bo) ξ‖ :=
   438	        norm_sub_le _ _

   444	/-- Squaring a three-term estimate. -/
   445	theorem sq_le_three_mul_of_le {w x y z : ℝ} (hw : 0 ≤ w) (h : w ≤ x + y + z) :
   446	    w ^ 2 ≤ 3 * x ^ 2 + 3 * y ^ 2 + 3 * z ^ 2 := by
   447	  have h1 : w ^ 2 ≤ (x + y + z) ^ 2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ hw h 2
   448	  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x - y), sq_nonneg (y - z), sq_nonneg (x - z)]
   449	
   450	/-- Summing the per-outcome estimates over the two outcomes. -/
   451	theorem sum_sq_le_of_le (d ℓ o : ZMod 2 → ℝ) (η ε m : ℝ)
   452	    (ho : ∀ b, 0 ≤ o b) (h : ∀ b, o b ≤ d b + ℓ b + 2 * η)
   453	    (hL : ∑ b, ℓ b ^ 2 ≤ 2 * m) (hm : m ≤ 36 * ε) :
   454	    ∑ b, o b ^ 2 ≤ 3 * ∑ b, d b ^ 2 + 216 * ε + 24 * η ^ 2 := by
   455	  have hterm : ∀ b, o b ^ 2 ≤ 3 * d b ^ 2 + 3 * ℓ b ^ 2 + 3 * (2 * η) ^ 2 :=
   456	    fun b => sq_le_three_mul_of_le (ho b) (h b)
   457	  calc ∑ b, o b ^ 2 ≤ ∑ b, (3 * d b ^ 2 + 3 * ℓ b ^ 2 + 3 * (2 * η) ^ 2) :=
   458	        Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => hterm b
   459	    _ = 3 * ∑ b, d b ^ 2 + 3 * ∑ b, ℓ b ^ 2 + 24 * η ^ 2 := by
   460	        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum,
   461	          ← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card, nsmul_eq_mul]
   462	        push_cast
   463	        ring
   464	    _ ≤ 3 * ∑ b, d b ^ 2 + 216 * ε + 24 * η ^ 2 := by nlinarith [hL, hm]

   466	/-- Transfer of Alice's bit-measurement estimate of `thm:ms-rigidity` from the
   467	dilated strategy to the original one.  For every target family `I` and target
   468	state `ξ`, the distance of Alice's conjugated original variable bits from `I`
   469	is at most three times the distance of the conjugated dilated bits, plus
   470	`216 ε` from the cell-consistency masses of a strategy of value `1 - ε`, plus
   471	`24 η²` where `η` bounds the distance of the transported dilated state from
   472	`ξ`.  The isometry of the original strategy is the composite of the dilation
   473	embedding and `φ_A`, exactly as in the witness of `exists_ms_rigidity`; the
   474	left-hand side is `msOperatorDistanceA S w j W` for that witness, and the
   475	distance on the right is `msOperatorDistanceA (msDilatedStrategy S) w' j W`.
   476	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
   477	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
   478	theorem ms_effect_transfer_A {κA κB : Type} [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA]
   479	    [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB] (S : Strategy msGame)
   480	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   481	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιB × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   482	    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB)) (I : ZMod 2 → Op (κA × κB)) (ε η : ℝ)
   483	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (j : Fin 9)
   484	    (hξ : ‖isometryTensor φA φB (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ - ξ‖ ≤ η) :
   485	    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   486	        (fun _ b => heteroKron (conjIsometry (φA.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιA MsAnswer))
   487	          (((S.A (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)) 1)
   488	        (fun _ b => I b) ξ ≤
   489	      3 * opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   490	        (fun _ b => heteroKron (conjIsometry φA
   491	          ((((msDilatedStrategy S).A (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)) 1)
   492	        (fun _ b => I b) ξ + 216 * ε + 24 * η ^ 2 := by
   493	  obtain ⟨i, k, rfl⟩ := every_variable_is_incident j
   494	  rw [opFamilyDistSq_uniform_unit, opFamilyDistSq_uniform_unit]
   495	  have hL := sum_norm_sq_intertwining_le_reverse S i k
   496	  have hmis := reverse_cell_mismatch_mass_le S ε hwin i k
   497	  have hξ' : ‖isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ) - ξ‖ ≤ η := hξ
   498	  have h := sum_sq_le_of_le
   499	    (fun b => ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA
   500	      (dilatedEffectA S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero b)) 1 - I b) ξ‖)
   501	    (fun b => ‖applyOperatorToState
   502	      (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero b) 1 -
   503	        heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) b))
   504	      (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖)
   505	    (fun b => ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron
   506	      (conjIsometry (φA.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιA MsAnswer))
   507	        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)) 1 - I b) ξ‖)
   508	    η ε (reverseCellMismatchMass S i k) (fun b => norm_nonneg _)
   509	    (fun b => by
   510	      have hb := norm_effect_transfer_term_le_A S φA φB ξ (I b) (.var (msConstraintVars i k))
   511	        (.constraint i) msBitOrZero (constraintBitOrZero k) b
   512	      linarith [hb, hξ'])
   513	    hL hmis
   514	  linarith [h]

   516	/-- Transfer of Bob's bit-measurement estimate of `thm:ms-rigidity` from the
   517	dilated strategy to the original one; see `ms_effect_transfer_A`. -/
   518	theorem ms_effect_transfer_B {κA κB : Type} [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA]
   519	    [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB] (S : Strategy msGame)
   520	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   521	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιB × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   522	    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB)) (I : ZMod 2 → Op (κA × κB)) (ε η : ℝ)
   523	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (j : Fin 9)
   524	    (hξ : ‖isometryTensor φA φB (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ - ξ‖ ≤ η) :
   525	    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   526	        (fun _ b => heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry (φB.comp (naimarkEmbedding S.ιB MsAnswer))

This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
`Measurement` structure.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.

pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.

structure Game where
  QuestionA : Type
  QuestionB : Type

  AnswerB : Type
  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]

  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]

  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq

/--
The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
  M.postprocess Prod.fst

/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.

    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=

/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)

  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)

  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB

attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq

/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
-/
def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
  Matrix.kronecker A B

/-! ### Algebra of the tensor placement

The shared tensor-placement API.  These identities are used both by the perfect
Magic Square strategy (`thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint

  unfold heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
  exact (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul A B C D).symm

    32	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ := by
    33	  let L : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ :=
    34	    { toFun := fun ψ => (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).symm fun j =>
    35	        if (e j).2 = 0 then (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e j).1 else 0
    36	      map_add' := by
    37	        intro ψ φ
    38	        apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).injective
    39	        change (fun j => if (e j).2 = 0 then
    40	          (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ (ψ + φ)) (e j).1 else 0) = _
    41	        ext j
    42	        simp only [map_add, Pi.add_apply]
    43	        split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]
    44	      map_smul' := by
    45	        intro c ψ
    46	        apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ).injective
    47	        change (fun j => if (e j).2 = 0 then
    48	          (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ (c • ψ)) (e j).1 else 0) = _
    49	        ext j
    50	        simp only [map_smul, Pi.smul_apply]
    51	        split_ifs with h <;> simp [h] }

    53	  apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp
    54	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
    55	  change (∑ j : κ, ‖if (e j).2 = 0 then ψ (e j).1 else 0‖ ^ 2) = _
    56	  change (∑ j : κ, (fun p : ι × (Fin n → Bool) =>
    57	    ‖if p.2 = 0 then ψ p.1 else 0‖ ^ 2) (e j)) = _

   622	bases.  Formalization-only support for `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   623	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   624	noncomputable def isometryMatrix {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   625	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   626	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') : Matrix ι' ι ℂ :=
   627	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap

   629	/-- Conjugation by an isometry is conjugation by its matrix. -/
   630	theorem conjIsometry_eq {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   631	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   632	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (M : Op ι) :
   633	    conjIsometry φ M = isometryMatrix φ * M * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := rfl

   635	/-- The matrix of an isometry acts on vectors as the isometry does. -/
   636	theorem isometryMatrix_mulVec {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   637	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   638	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   639	    isometryMatrix φ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x = WithLp.ofLp (φ x) := by
   640	  have h : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) = φ.toLinearMap :=
   641	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply φ.toLinearMap
   642	  have h' : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) x = φ x := by rw [h]; rfl
   643	  simpa using congrArg WithLp.ofLp h'

   645	/-- The columns of the matrix of an isometry are the images of the basis
   646	vectors. -/
   647	theorem isometryMatrix_apply {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   648	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
   649	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (k : ι') (i : ι) :
   650	    isometryMatrix φ k i =
   651	      φ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1)) k := by
   652	  have h := congrFun (isometryMatrix_mulVec φ
   653	    ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) k
   654	  rw [← h]
   655	  simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.equiv, eq_comm]

   657	/-- The matrix of a composite isometry is the product of the two matrices. -/
   658	theorem isometryMatrix_comp {ι κ ν : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   659	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ν] [DecidableEq ν]
   660	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ν)
   661	    (E : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
   662	    isometryMatrix (φ.comp E) = isometryMatrix φ * isometryMatrix E := by
   663	  ext k i
   664	  have h := congrFun (isometryMatrix_mulVec φ
   665	    (E ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1)))) k
   666	  rw [isometryMatrix_apply, Matrix.mul_apply]
   667	  simp only [isometryMatrix_apply E]
   668	  simpa [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct] using h.symm

   684	theorem isometryTensor_apply_eq {ιA ιB κA κB : Type}
   685	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   686	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]

   689	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (p : κA × κB) :
   690	    isometryTensor φA φB ψ p =

   692	        Matrix.kronecker (isometryMatrix φA) (isometryMatrix φB) p q * ψ q := by

   696	/-- Applying two local isometries after two others is the same as applying their
   697	composites.  Together with `conjIsometry_comp` this is the composition rule used
   698	to turn a rigidity witness for the dilated strategy into one for the original
   699	strategy. -/
   700	theorem isometryTensor_comp {ιA ιB κA κB νA νB : Type}
   701	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   702	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
   703	    [Fintype νA] [DecidableEq νA] [Fintype νB] [DecidableEq νB]
   704	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ κA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ νA)
   705	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ κB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ νB)
   706	    (EA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
   707	    (EB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
   708	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   709	    isometryTensor (φA.comp EA) (φB.comp EB) ψ =
   710	      isometryTensor φA φB (isometryTensor EA EB ψ) := by
   711	  ext p
   712	  rw [isometryTensor_apply_eq, isometryTensor_apply_eq]
   713	  simp only [isometryTensor_apply_eq, isometryMatrix_comp, Finset.mul_sum]
   714	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   715	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => ?_
   716	  have hk : (isometryMatrix φA * isometryMatrix EA).kronecker
   717	        (isometryMatrix φB * isometryMatrix EB) =
   718	      (isometryMatrix φA).kronecker (isometryMatrix φB) *
   719	        (isometryMatrix EA).kronecker (isometryMatrix EB) :=
   720	    Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul _ _ _ _
   721	  rw [hk, Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.sum_mul]
   722	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => by ring

     3	/-!
     4	# Transfer of rigidity bounds along the projective dilation
     5	
     6	The self-testing argument behind `thm:ms-rigidity` is carried out for the
     7	projective dilation `msDilatedStrategy S` of an arbitrary Magic Square strategy
     8	`S`.  Its conclusions are state-dependent bounds for the *dilated* projectors,
     9	conjugated by local isometries `φ_A`, `φ_B` out of the enlarged local spaces.
    10	The witness for the original strategy is obtained by composing these isometries
    11	with the ground embeddings, and the operators appearing in its bounds are the
    12	conjugates of the *original* effects, that is, of the compressions `Π P Π` of
    13	the dilated projectors `P` to the ground slice (`Π` the ground projection).
    14	
    15	Naimark dilation preserves Born probabilities but not state-dependent `≈_δ`
    16	estimates in general (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`,
    17	blueprint `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`), so `Π P Π` and `P` need not act
    18	alike on the dilated state.  Their difference on the dilated state `ψ'` is the
    19	*leakage* `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of `P` out of the ground slice, and the point of this
    20	file is that in the Magic Square game this leakage is controlled by the
    21	cell-consistency defect of the value-to-parity layer: the dilated effect
    22	`P ⊗ 1` almost agrees with the partner effect `1 ⊗ Q` on the other side, and
    23	`(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `1 ⊗ Q ψ'`.  Combined with the closeness of
    24	`(φ_A ⊗ φ_B) ψ'` to the ideal state and the fact that all operators involved
    25	are contractions, this pulls every bound of `thm:ms-rigidity` back from the
    26	dilated strategy to the original one with explicit constants.
    27	
    28	## Main statements
    29	
    30	* `ms_effect_transfer_A`, `ms_effect_transfer_B`: the bit-measurement distances
    31	  of the original strategy are bounded by three times those of the dilated
    32	  strategy plus `216 ε + 24 η²`, where `η` bounds the state closeness.
    33	* `ms_anticommutator_transfer_A`, `ms_anticommutator_transfer_B`: the
    34	  anticommutator defects transfer with the bound `3 · (dilated) + 15552 ε +
    35	  48 η²`.
    36	* `ms_state_transfer`: the state closeness is unchanged.
    37	
    38	## References
    39	
    40	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
    41	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
    42	-/

    55	/-- The Born overlap of Alice's totalized variable bit with Bob's totalized
    56	constraint bit, summed over the bit, is the complement of the reverse
    57	cell-mismatch mass. -/
    58	theorem sum_stateQForm_reverse_eq (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    59	    ∑ b : ZMod 2, stateQForm S.ψ (heteroKron
    60	        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)
    61	        (((S.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)).effect b)) =
    62	      1 - reverseCellMismatchMass S i k := by
    63	  classical
    64	  have hterm : ∀ b : ZMod 2, stateQForm S.ψ (heteroKron
    65	        (((S.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)
    66	        (((S.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)).effect b)) =
    67	      ∑ a : msGame.AnswerA, ∑ c : msGame.AnswerB,
    68	        if msBitOrZero a = b then
    69	          (if constraintBitOrZero k c = b then
    70	            outcomeWeight S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) (.constraint i) a c else 0)
    71	        else 0 := by
    72	    intro b
    73	    rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
    74	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
    75	      heteroKron_finset_sum_left, stateQForm_finset_sum, Finset.sum_filter]
    76	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    77	    split_ifs
    78	    · rw [heteroKron_finset_sum_right, stateQForm_finset_sum, Finset.sum_filter]
    79	      rfl
    80	    · simp
    81	  have htotal := outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) (.constraint i)
    82	  unfold reverseCellMismatchMass outcomeEventWeight
    83	  simp_rw [hterm]
    84	  rw [Finset.sum_comm, eq_sub_iff_add_eq, ← htotal, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    85	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    86	  rw [Finset.sum_comm, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    87	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => ?_
    88	  rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq]
    89	  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    90	  by_cases h : msBitOrZero a = constraintBitOrZero k c
    91	  · simp [h]
    92	  · simp [h, Ne.symm h]

   135	/-- Alice's dilated postprocessed effect, typed on the enlarged local space

   137	abbrev dilatedEffectA (S : Strategy msGame) (x : MsType) (f : MsAnswer → ZMod 2)

   147	/-- Alice's dilated variable bit approximately intertwines with Bob's dilated

   150	`fact:agreement` (blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:245-254`) applied to the
   151	dilated strategy, whose Born masses are those of the original one. -/
   152	theorem sum_norm_sq_intertwining_le_reverse (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
   153	    ∑ b : ZMod 2, ‖applyOperatorToState
   154	        (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero b) 1 -
   155	          heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) b))
   156	        (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * reverseCellMismatchMass S i k := by

   158	  set PA := (S'.A (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).postprocess msBitOrZero
   159	  set QB := (S'.B (.constraint i)).postprocess (constraintBitOrZero k)
   160	  have h1 := point_distance_le_two_defect (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := S'.ιB) PA)
   161	    (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := S'.ιA) QB) S'.ψ
   162	  rw [point_defect_eq] at h1
   163	  have hnorm : ‖S'.ψ‖ = 1 := S'.ψ_norm
   164	  have hover : ∑ a : ZMod 2, stateQForm S'.ψ
   165	      ((leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := S'.ιB) PA).effect a *

   173	    rw [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul]

   176	      (heteroKron (dilatedEffectA S (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) msBitOrZero b) 1 -
   177	        heteroKron 1 (dilatedEffectB S (.constraint i) (constraintBitOrZero k) b))
   178	      (naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ)‖ ^ 2 ≤
   179	      2 * (1 ^ 2 - (1 - reverseCellMismatchMass S i k)) := h1
   180	  linarith

   335	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 - T) ξ‖ +
   336	      ‖applyOperatorToState

   342	  have hG : (groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)ᴴ * groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer ≤ 1 :=
   343	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection S.ιA MsAnswer)
   344	  have hAd : (heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) (1 : Op κB))ᴴ *
   345	      heteroKron (conjIsometry φA (dilatedEffectA S x f b)) 1 ≤ 1 :=
   346	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_leftTensor (conjTranspose_mul_le_one_conjIsometry φA hP)

   357	  have h1 : applyOperatorToState (Ao - T) ξ =
   358	      applyOperatorToState (Ad - T) ξ - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ := by
   359	    simp [applyOperatorToState]
   360	  have h2 : applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ξ =
   361	      applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) ψ'' - applyOperatorToState (Ad - Ao) (ψ'' - ξ) := by

   470	`216 ε` from the cell-consistency masses of a strategy of value `1 - ε`, plus

   477	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/

   480	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ιA × Option MsAnswer) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)

   687	/-- The defect of the compressed product `Π A Π · Π B Π` against `A B` on the
   688	dilated state is controlled by the leakage of `A` and `B` and the intertwining
   689	defect of `B` against any right-placed contraction `Y`.  Since `Π ψ' = ψ'`,

   691	term is bounded by the leakage of `B`, and in the second `B ψ'` is replaced by
   692	`Y ψ'`, which commutes past `(1 - Π) A`. -/

   695	    [DecidableEq ιB] (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
   696	    (A B : Op (ιA × Option α)) (Y : Op (ιB × Option α))
   697	    (hA : Aᴴ * A ≤ 1) (hY : Yᴴ * Y ≤ 1) :
   698	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α *
   699	        (groundProjection ιA α * B * groundProjection ιA α) - A * B) 1)
   700	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ ≤
   701	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * B) 1)
   702	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   703	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * A) 1)
   704	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ +
   705	      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron B 1 - heteroKron 1 Y) (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ := by
   706	  have hGG : groundProjection ιA α * groundProjection ιA α = groundProjection ιA α :=
   707	    (isProj_groundProjection ιA α).isIdempotentElem.eq
   708	  have hGc : (groundProjection ιA α)ᴴ * groundProjection ιA α ≤ 1 :=
   709	    conjTranspose_mul_le_one_of_isProj (isProj_groundProjection ιA α)
   710	  have h1Gc : (1 - groundProjection ιA α)ᴴ * (1 - groundProjection ιA α) ≤ 1 :=

   713	      groundProjection ιA α * (groundProjection ιA α * B * groundProjection ιA α)) 1)
   714	      (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
   715	      applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α * B) 1)
   716	        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) := by
   717	    have hassoc : groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α *
   718	        (groundProjection ιA α * B * groundProjection ιA α) =
   719	        groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α * B * groundProjection ιA α := by
   720	      simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   721	      rw [← Matrix.mul_assoc (groundProjection ιA α) (groundProjection ιA α) (B * _), hGG]
   722	    rw [hassoc, show heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α * B *
   723	        groundProjection ιA α) (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) =

   727	  have hdec : groundProjection ιA α * A * groundProjection ιA α * B - A * B =

   735	    rw [show heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α * A * ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * B))

   737	        heteroKron (groundProjection ιA α * A) 1 * heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * B) 1

   751	    have hcomm : heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * A) (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) *
   752	        heteroKron 1 Y = heteroKron 1 Y * heteroKron ((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * A) 1 := by

   755	    rw [show heteroKron (((1 - groundProjection ιA α) * A) * B) (1 : Op (ιB × Option α)) =

   762	    rw [hdecB, applyOperatorToState_add, ← applyOperatorToState_mul _ (heteroKron 1 Y), hcomm,

   766	    · exact norm_applyOperatorToState_le hYc _

     4	/-!
     5	# A simultaneous projective dilation of a Magic Square strategy
     6	
     7	The rigidity argument for the Magic Square game is stated for an arbitrary
     8	tensor-product strategy, whose measurements are positive operator valued
     9	measures.  The self-testing argument, however, manipulates projections.  This
    10	file removes that discrepancy by dilating an arbitrary strategy to a projective
    11	one without changing any observable quantity.
    12	
    13	Each local Hilbert space `ℂ^ι` is enlarged by one auxiliary register whose
    14	basis is indexed by `Option MsAnswer`, and the original space is identified with
    15	the *ground slice* `ℂ^ι ⊗ |⊥⟩`.  The one-measurement Naimark lemma of the low
    16	individual degree development supplies, for every question separately, a family
    17	of projections on the enlarged space whose compression to the ground slice
    18	returns the original effects; the ancilla is the same for all questions, so the
    19	identification of `ℂ^ι` with the ground slice is a single isometry serving every
    20	question at once.  Folding the deficiency `1 - ∑_a P_a` into one distinguished
    21	answer turns the dilated family into a complete projective measurement without
    22	disturbing the compression, because the original effects already sum to the
    23	identity.
    24	
    25	Since the dilated state is the image of the original state under the two ground
    26	embeddings, every Born probability, and hence the game value and all the
    27	rejection, malformed-answer, cell-consistency and parity masses of the
    28	value-to-parity layer, is unchanged.  Conversely, the local isometries produced
    29	by a rigidity argument applied to the dilated strategy compose with the ground
    30	embeddings to give local isometries of the original strategy, and the
    31	state-dependent norms occurring in the conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` transfer
    32	along that composition.
    33	
    34	## References
    35	
    36	The rigidity statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
    37	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
    39	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.  The dilation reuses the
    40	one-measurement Naimark lemma of
    41	`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`, formalized as
    42	`MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.oneMeasNaimark`.
    43	-/
    44

    55	
    56	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
    57	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  If an orthogonal projection `P` and a
    58	positive semidefinite operator `Q` satisfy `P + Q ≤ 1`, then `P` annihilates
    59	`Q`.  Indeed `Tr(P Q)` is nonnegative because both operators are positive
    60	semidefinite, while `0 ≤ Tr(P (1 - P - Q)) = -Tr(P Q)` because `1 - P - Q` is
    61	positive semidefinite and `P` is idempotent; so the pairing vanishes and the
    62	product of two positive semidefinite operators with vanishing trace pairing is
    63	zero. -/
    64	theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    65	    {P Q : Op d} (hP : IsProj P) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hPQ : P + Q ≤ 1) :
    66	    P * Q = 0 := by
    67	  have hrest : (0 : Op d) ≤ 1 - (P + Q) := sub_nonneg.mpr hPQ
    68	  have hexpand : P * (1 - (P + Q)) = -(P * Q) := by
    69	    have hPP : P * P = P := hP.isIdempotentElem
    70	    rw [Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_add, hPP, Matrix.mul_one]
    71	    abel
    72	  have hle : Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) ≤ 0 := by
    73	    have h := trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hrest
    74	    rw [hexpand] at h
    75	    simpa using h
    76	  have hge : 0 ≤ Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) :=
    77	    trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hQ
    78	  exact mul_eq_zero_of_nonneg_of_trace_mul_eq_zero hP.nonneg hQ (le_antisymm hle hge)

    81	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  A finite family of orthogonal
    82	projections whose sum is at most the identity is mutually orthogonal: for two
    83	distinct indices the two projections already sum to at most the identity, so the
    84	previous lemma applies. -/
    85	theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    86	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
    87	    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
    88	    P a * P b = 0 := by
    89	  refine mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one (hP a) (hP b).nonneg ?_
    90	  refine le_trans ?_ hsum
    91	  have hpair : ∑ c ∈ ({a, b} : Finset α), P c = P a + P b := by
    92	    rw [Finset.sum_pair hab]
    93	  rw [← hpair]
    94	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
    95	    (fun c _ _ => (hP c).nonneg)

    98	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  The sum of a mutually orthogonal
    99	family of projections is again an orthogonal projection; mutual orthogonality is
   100	supplied by the hypothesis that the sum is at most the identity. -/
   101	theorem isProj_sum_of_isProj_of_sum_le_one {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   102	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))

   105	  constructor
   106	  · show (∑ a, P a) * (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a
   107	    rw [Finset.sum_mul]

   114	  · show star (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a
   115	    rw [star_sum]
   116	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (hP a).isSelfAdjoint

   120	/-- The linear map sending a vector `x` of `ℂ^ι` to `x ⊗ |⊥⟩`, where `|⊥⟩` is the

+import MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.NaimarkFull
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.MagicSquareTheorems.Rigidity.Relations
+
+/-!
+# A simultaneous projective dilation of a Magic Square strategy
+
+The rigidity argument for the Magic Square game is stated for an arbitrary
+tensor-product strategy, whose measurements are positive operator valued
+measures.  The self-testing argument, however, manipulates projections.  This
+file removes that discrepancy by dilating an arbitrary strategy to a projective
+one without changing any observable quantity.
+
+Each local Hilbert space `ℂ^ι` is enlarged by one auxiliary register whose
+basis is indexed by `Option MsAnswer`, and the original space is identified with
+the *ground slice* `ℂ^ι ⊗ |⊥⟩`.  The one-measurement Naimark lemma of the low
+individual degree development supplies, for every question separately, a family
+of projections on the enlarged space whose compression to the ground slice
+returns the original effects; the ancilla is the same for all questions, so the
+identification of `ℂ^ι` with the ground slice is a single isometry serving every
+question at once.  Folding the deficiency `1 - ∑_a P_a` into one distinguished
+answer turns the dilated family into a complete projective measurement without
+disturbing the compression, because the original effects already sum to the
+identity.
+
+Since the dilated state is the image of the original state under the two ground
+embeddings, every Born probability, and hence the game value and all the
+rejection, malformed-answer, cell-consistency and parity masses of the
+value-to-parity layer, is unchanged.  Conversely, the local isometries produced
+by a rigidity argument applied to the dilated strategy compose with the ground
+embeddings to give local isometries of the original strategy, and the
+state-dependent norms occurring in the conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` transfer
+along that composition.
+
+## References
+
+The rigidity statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
+proved in Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.  The dilation reuses the
+one-measurement Naimark lemma of
+`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`, formalized as
+`MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.oneMeasNaimark`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+open MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Orthogonality inside a subnormalized family of projections -/
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
+(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  If an orthogonal projection `P` and a
+positive semidefinite operator `Q` satisfy `P + Q ≤ 1`, then `P` annihilates
+`Q`.  Indeed `Tr(P Q)` is nonnegative because both operators are positive
+semidefinite, while `0 ≤ Tr(P (1 - P - Q)) = -Tr(P Q)` because `1 - P - Q` is
+positive semidefinite and `P` is idempotent; so the pairing vanishes and the
+product of two positive semidefinite operators with vanishing trace pairing is
+zero. -/
+theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    {P Q : Op d} (hP : IsProj P) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hPQ : P + Q ≤ 1) :
+    P * Q = 0 := by
+  have hrest : (0 : Op d) ≤ 1 - (P + Q) := sub_nonneg.mpr hPQ
+  have hexpand : P * (1 - (P + Q)) = -(P * Q) := by
+    have hPP : P * P = P := hP.isIdempotentElem
+    rw [Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_add, hPP, Matrix.mul_one]
+    abel
+  have hle : Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) ≤ 0 := by
+    have h := trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hrest
+    rw [hexpand] at h
+    simpa using h
+  have hge : 0 ≤ Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) :=
+    trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hQ
+  exact mul_eq_zero_of_nonneg_of_trace_mul_eq_zero hP.nonneg hQ (le_antisymm hle hge)
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
+(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  A finite family of orthogonal
+projections whose sum is at most the identity is mutually orthogonal: for two
+distinct indices the two projections already sum to at most the identity, so the
+previous lemma applies. -/
+theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
+    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
+    P a * P b = 0 := by
+  refine mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one (hP a) (hP b).nonneg ?_
+  refine le_trans ?_ hsum
+  have hpair : ∑ c ∈ ({a, b} : Finset α), P c = P a + P b := by
+    rw [Finset.sum_pair hab]
+  rw [← hpair]
+  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
+    (fun c _ _ => (hP c).nonneg)
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
+(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  The sum of a mutually orthogonal
+family of projections is again an orthogonal projection; mutual orthogonality is
+supplied by the hypothesis that the sum is at most the identity. -/
+theorem isProj_sum_of_isProj_of_sum_le_one {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
+    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) :
+    IsProj (∑ a, P a) := by
+  constructor
+  · show (∑ a, P a) * (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a
+    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+    rw [Matrix.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single a]
+    · exact (hP a).isIdempotentElem
+    · exact fun b _ hba => mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family hP hsum (Ne.symm hba)
+    · intro ha
+      exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha
+  · show star (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a
+    rw [star_sum]
+    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (hP a).isSelfAdjoint
+
+/-! ## The ground slice of an enlarged local space -/
+
+/-- The linear map sending a vector `x` of `ℂ^ι` to `x ⊗ |⊥⟩`, where `|⊥⟩` is the
+basis vector of the auxiliary register `ℂ^{Option α}` indexed by the adjoined
+point.  Formalization-only support for the dilation used by `thm:ms-rigidity`,
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
+def naimarkEmbeddingMap (ι α : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × Option α) where
+  toFun x := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ι × Option α) ℂ).symm
+    (fun p => if p.2 = none then x p.1 else 0)
+  map_add' x y := by
+    ext p
+    by_cases h : p.2 = none <;> simp [h]
+  map_smul' c x := by
+    ext p
+    by_cases h : p.2 = none <;> simp [h]
+
+/-- The isometric identification of a local Hilbert space `ℂ^ι` with the *ground
+slice* `ℂ^ι ⊗ |⊥⟩` of the enlarged space `ℂ^{ι × Option α}`.  This single
+embedding serves every question of the dilation supporting `thm:ms-rigidity`,
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
+noncomputable def naimarkEmbedding (ι α : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × Option α) :=
+  LinearMap.isometryOfInner (naimarkEmbeddingMap ι α) <| by
+    intro x y
+    simp [PiLp.inner_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type, naimarkEmbeddingMap]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem naimarkEmbedding_apply {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (p : ι × Option α) :
+    naimarkEmbedding ι α x p = if p.2 = none then x p.1 else 0 := rfl
+
+/-- The compression of an operator on the enlarged space to the ground slice.
+Formalization-only support for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
+def naimarkCompression {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op (ι × Option α)) : Op ι :=
+  M.submatrix (fun i => (i, none)) (fun j => (j, none))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem naimarkCompression_apply {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op (ι × Option α)) (i j : ι) :
+    naimarkCompression (α := α) M i j = M (i, none) (j, none) := rfl
+
+/-- The compression of the zero operator to the ground slice vanishes. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem naimarkCompression_zero {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
+    naimarkCompression (α := α) (0 : Op (ι × Option α)) = 0 := by
+  ext i j; simp
+
+/-- The compression to the ground slice is additive. -/
+theorem naimarkCompression_add {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M N : Op (ι × Option α)) :
+    naimarkCompression (α := α) (M + N) =
+      naimarkCompression (α := α) M + naimarkCompression (α := α) N := by
+  ext i j; simp
+
+/-- The compression to the ground slice commutes with finite sums. -/
+theorem naimarkCompression_sum {ι α β : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] (M : β → Op (ι × Option α)) :
+    naimarkCompression (α := α) (∑ b, M b) = ∑ b, naimarkCompression (α := α) (M b) := by
+  ext i j; simp [Matrix.sum_apply]
+
+/-- The compression of the identity to the ground slice is the identity. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem naimarkCompression_one {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
+    naimarkCompression (α := α) (1 : Op (ι × Option α)) = 1 := by
+  ext i j
+  by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [Matrix.one_apply, h]
+
+/-- The operator on the enlarged space that acts as `M` on the ground slice and
+annihilates its orthogonal complement.  Formalization-only support for the
+dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
+def naimarkInflation {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) : Op (ι × Option α) :=
+  Matrix.of fun p q => if p.2 = none ∧ q.2 = none then M p.1 q.1 else 0
+
+@[simp]
+theorem naimarkInflation_apply {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) (p q : ι × Option α) :
+    naimarkInflation (α := α) M p q =
+      if p.2 = none ∧ q.2 = none then M p.1 q.1 else 0 := rfl
+
+/-- Inflating an operator to the enlarged space and compressing it back returns
+the original operator. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem naimarkCompression_naimarkInflation {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) :
+    naimarkCompression (α := α) (naimarkInflation (α := α) M) = M := by
+  ext i j; simp
+
+/-- The compression to the ground slice respects differences. -/
+theorem naimarkCompression_sub {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M N : Op (ι × Option α)) :
+    naimarkCompression (α := α) (M - N) =
+      naimarkCompression (α := α) M - naimarkCompression (α := α) N := by
+  ext i j; simp
+
+/-! ## The dilated projective measurement -/
+
+/-- A one-measurement Naimark dilation of a positive operator valued measure,
+chosen once and for all.  It provides orthogonal projections on the enlarged
+space `ℂ^{d × Option α}` whose ground-slice compressions are the given effects;
+see `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`. -/
+noncomputable def naimarkData {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) : OneMeasNaimarkData α d :=
+  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
+
+/-- The chosen dilation dilates the intended measurement. -/
+theorem naimarkData_source {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
+    (naimarkData M).source = M.toSubmeasurement :=
+  Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
+
+/-- The dilated projections indexed by genuine answers already sum to at most the
+identity, since the projection attached to the adjoined point is positive
+semidefinite. -/
+theorem naimarkData_sum_some_le_one {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
+    ∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) ≤ 1 := by
+  have hsplit : ∑ oa : Option α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect oa =
+      (naimarkData M).liftedEffect none +
+        ∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) :=
+    Fintype.sum_option (f := fun oa => (naimarkData M).liftedEffect oa)

+/-! ## Composition of the dilation with later local isometries -/
+
+/-- The matrix of a linear isometry of Euclidean spaces in the computational
+bases.  Formalization-only support for `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
+noncomputable def isometryMatrix {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
+    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') : Matrix ι' ι ℂ :=
+  Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
+
+/-- Conjugation by an isometry is conjugation by its matrix. -/
+theorem conjIsometry_eq {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
+    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (M : Op ι) :
+    conjIsometry φ M = isometryMatrix φ * M * (isometryMatrix φ)ᴴ := rfl
+
+/-- The matrix of an isometry acts on vectors as the isometry does. -/
+theorem isometryMatrix_mulVec {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
+    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
+    isometryMatrix φ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x = WithLp.ofLp (φ x) := by
+  have h : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) = φ.toLinearMap :=
+    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply φ.toLinearMap
+  have h' : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (isometryMatrix φ) x = φ x := by rw [h]; rfl
+  simpa using congrArg WithLp.ofLp h'
+
+/-- The columns of the matrix of an isometry are the images of the basis
+vectors. -/
+theorem isometryMatrix_apply {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
+    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι') (k : ι') (i : ι) :
+    isometryMatrix φ k i =
+      φ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1)) k := by
+  have h := congrFun (isometryMatrix_mulVec φ
+    ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) k
+  rw [← h]
+  simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.equiv, eq_comm]
+
+/-- The matrix of a composite isometry is the product of the two matrices. -/
+theorem isometryMatrix_comp {ι κ ν : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ν] [DecidableEq ν]
+    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ν)
+    (E : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
+    isometryMatrix (φ.comp E) = isometryMatrix φ * isometryMatrix E := by
+  ext k i
+  have h := congrFun (isometryMatrix_mulVec φ
+    (E ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1)))) k
+  rw [isometryMatrix_apply, Matrix.mul_apply]
+  simp only [isometryMatrix_apply E]
+  simpa [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct] using h.symm
+
+/-- Conjugating by a composite isometry is conjugating twice.  This is how the
+ground embeddings of the dilation combine with the local isometries produced by
+the self-testing argument of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
+theorem conjIsometry_comp {ι κ ν : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ν] [DecidableEq ν]
+    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ν)
+    (E : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) (M : Op ι) :
+    conjIsometry (φ.comp E) M = conjIsometry φ (conjIsometry E M) := by
+  rw [conjIsometry_eq, conjIsometry_eq, conjIsometry_eq, isometryMatrix_comp]
+  simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
+
+/-- The two-sided isometry image of a bipartite state, written through the
+Kronecker product of the two isometry matrices. -/
+theorem isometryTensor_apply_eq {ιA ιB κA κB : Type}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
+    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
+    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (p : κA × κB) :
+    isometryTensor φA φB ψ p =
+      ∑ q : ιA × ιB,
+        Matrix.kronecker (isometryMatrix φA) (isometryMatrix φB) p q * ψ q := by
+  simp [isometryTensor, Matrix.kronecker, Fintype.sum_prod_type, isometryMatrix_apply,
+    EuclideanSpace.equiv, mul_assoc]
+
+/-- Applying two local isometries after two others is the same as applying their
+composites.  Together with `conjIsometry_comp` this is the composition rule used
+to turn a rigidity witness for the dilated strategy into one for the original
+strategy. -/
+theorem isometryTensor_comp {ιA ιB κA κB νA νB : Type}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
+    [Fintype νA] [DecidableEq νA] [Fintype νB] [DecidableEq νB]
+    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ κA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ νA)
+    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ κB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ νB)
+    (EA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
+    (EB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    isometryTensor (φA.comp EA) (φB.comp EB) ψ =
+      isometryTensor φA φB (isometryTensor EA EB ψ) := by
+  ext p
+  rw [isometryTensor_apply_eq, isometryTensor_apply_eq]
+  simp only [isometryTensor_apply_eq, isometryMatrix_comp, Finset.mul_sum]
+  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => ?_
+  have hk : (isometryMatrix φA * isometryMatrix EA).kronecker
+        (isometryMatrix φB * isometryMatrix EB) =
+      (isometryMatrix φA).kronecker (isometryMatrix φB) *
+        (isometryMatrix EA).kronecker (isometryMatrix EB) :=
+    Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul _ _ _ _
+  rw [hk, Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.sum_mul]
+  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => by ring
+
+/-- The ground embeddings of the dilation composed with two later local
+isometries carry the original state exactly as those isometries carry the
+dilated state. -/
+theorem isometryTensor_comp_naimarkEmbedding (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
+    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × Option α) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
+    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB × Option α) →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    isometryTensor (φA.comp (naimarkEmbedding ιA α)) (φB.comp (naimarkEmbedding ιB α)) ψ =
+      isometryTensor φA φB (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) :=
+  isometryTensor_comp φA φB _ _ ψ
+
+/-! ## Transfer of state-dependent bounds -/
+
+/-- Conjugating an operator by the ground embedding inflates it: the result acts
+as the original operator on the ground slice and annihilates the orthogonal
+complement. -/
+theorem conjIsometry_naimarkEmbedding {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) :
+    conjIsometry (naimarkEmbedding ι α) M = naimarkInflation (α := α) M := by
+  ext p q
+  rw [conjIsometry_eq]
+  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, isometryMatrix_apply,
+    naimarkEmbedding_apply, naimarkInflation_apply, EuclideanSpace.equiv]
+  by_cases hp : p.2 = none
+  · by_cases hq : q.2 = none <;> simp [hp, hq, eq_comm]
+  · simp [hp]
+
+/-- The action of an operator on the dilated state only sees its ground-slice
+columns. -/
+theorem applyOperatorToState_naimarkDilatedState (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (K : Op ((ιA × Option α) × (ιB × Option α)))
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (p : (ιA × Option α) × (ιB × Option α)) :
+    applyOperatorToState K (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) p =
+      ∑ k : ιA, ∑ l : ιB, K p ((k, none), (l, none)) * ψ (k, l) := by
+  classical
+  simp [applyOperatorToState, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fintype.sum_prod_type,
+    Fintype.sum_option, naimarkDilatedState_apply_mul]
+
+/-- Inflated operators act on the dilated state exactly as the original
+operators act on the original state.  This is the identity that transfers
+state-dependent effect bounds back to the undilated strategy. -/
+theorem applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_naimarkInflation
+    (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    applyOperatorToState
+        (heteroKron (naimarkInflation (α := α) M) (naimarkInflation (α := α) N))
+        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
+      naimarkDilatedState α (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron M N) ψ) := by
+  classical
+  ext p
+  rw [applyOperatorToState_naimarkDilatedState, naimarkDilatedState_apply]
+  obtain ⟨⟨i, oa⟩, ⟨j, ob⟩⟩ := p
+  by_cases hoa : oa = none
+  · by_cases hob : ob = none
+    · simp [hoa, hob, heteroKron, applyOperatorToState, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct,
+        Fintype.sum_prod_type, mul_assoc]
+    · simp [hob, heteroKron]
+  · simp [hoa, heteroKron]
+
+/-- The state-dependent norm of an inflated operator on the dilated state equals
+the state-dependent norm of the original operator on the original state. -/
+theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_naimarkInflation
+    (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    ‖applyOperatorToState
+        (heteroKron (naimarkInflation (α := α) M) (naimarkInflation (α := α) N))
+        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ)‖ =
+      ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron M N) ψ‖ := by
+  rw [applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_naimarkInflation, naimarkDilatedState_norm]
+
+/-- Transfer of state-dependent effect bounds.  Every average squared distance
+between two families of inflated operators, measured on the dilated state, is
+the corresponding distance between the original families measured on the
+original state; a bound obtained for the dilated strategy is therefore a bound
+for the strategy one started from.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
+paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
+theorem opFamilyDistSq_naimarkInflation (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    {X γ ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype γ] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
+    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → γ → Op ιA) (P : X → γ → Op ιB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    opFamilyDistSq μ
+        (fun x c => heteroKron (naimarkInflation (α := α) (M x c))
+          (naimarkInflation (α := α) (P x c)))
+        (fun x c => heteroKron (naimarkInflation (α := α) (N x c))
+          (naimarkInflation (α := α) (P x c)))
+        (naimarkDilatedState α ψ) =
+      opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x c => heteroKron (M x c) (P x c))
+        (fun x c => heteroKron (N x c) (P x c)) ψ := by
+  unfold opFamilyDistSq
+  congr 1
+  funext x

     4	/-!
     5	# Contractions, isometries and the ground slice of the dilation
     6	
     7	Support for the transfer step of `thm:ms-rigidity` (blueprint
     8	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
     9	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`):
    10	the calculus needed to compare the dilated projective strategy of
    11	`Rigidity/Dilation.lean` with the original strategy on states.
    12	
    13	* Contractions: operators `K` with `Kᴴ K ≤ 1` do not increase norms; effects,
    14	  observables of binary measurements, orthogonal projections, tensor placements,
    15	  products and isometry conjugates are contractions.
    16	* Matrices of isometries: `Vᴴ V = 1`, the two-sided isometry image of a state
    17	  preserves norms, and a conjugated local operator acts on the transported state
    18	  as the original operator acts on the original state.
    19	* The ground projection `Π` of an enlarged local space: an orthogonal projection
    20	  fixing the dilated state, with `Π P Π` the inflation of the compression of `P`.
    21	* Leakage: the part `(1 - Π) P ψ'` of a dilated operator that leaves the ground
    22	  slice is bounded by the intertwining defect of `P ⊗ 1` against any `1 ⊗ Q`,
    23	  because `(1 - Π) ⊗ 1` annihilates `(1 ⊗ Q) ψ'`.  This is the estimate that
    24	  replaces the `≈_δ`-preservation which Naimark dilation lacks in general
    25	  (`references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:82-101`, blueprint
    26	  `ch04_projective.tex:255-270`).
    27	
    28	## References
    29	
    30	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`,
    31	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
    32	-/

    34	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    35	
    36	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
    37	
    38	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    39	open MIPStarRE.Quantum MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus
